# Getting Started

## Getting Started
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/start.html

New here? This section takes you from an empty chat to a published post: connect your channel, connect a sender bot, schedule the first message — then explore the tools that keep a channel running on autopilot. The three setup steps are short guides with pictures of what to tap. After that, the glossary explains any term you meet along the way, and the SetDate topic covers bulk-creating schedules from a file.

## Get Started: What Fast Scheduler Does
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/getting_started.html

Fast Scheduler publishes posts to your Telegram channel at the date and time you choose. You write the post once, tell the bot when it should go out, and it sends it later — even if your phone is off or the app is closed. It is a publishing tool for channel owners, not a chat bot: there is nothing to talk to, only a queue to fill. ## Why people use it • A week of posts in one message. Send date + text pairs separated by a blank line and all of them are scheduled at once — see the example below. This is the feature most owners switch for: it turns a weekend of writing into one send.• Recurring posts are free. One repeating rule — daily, weekly, every Monday at 9:00 — is included on the Free plan, so a channel can run its regular slots without a subscription. Premium lifts the rule limit.• Media that survives the trip. Photos, videos, albums, a reusable media library, and formatting — bold, italic, links, code, spoilers, custom emoji — is preserved exactly as you sent it.• One list for everything. Edit, move, reschedule or cancel anything before it goes out; afterwards the same entry shows views and delivery status. Search and filters find a post without scrolling.• Posts go out from your own bot. The channel keeps its own name, avatar and posting identity, and co-administrators can schedule too — each with the permissions the owner grants them (Admins &amp; Access).• Plans in one line. Free: 1 channel, 1 sender bot, 100 scheduled posts, 1 recurring rule. Premium: 3 channels, 3 sender bots, unlimited scheduled and recurring posts, longer media, exports and backups. ## What you need before you start • A Telegram channel where you are an administrator — the bot verifies this before it links anything.• A sender bot : your own Telegram bot, created in @BotFather in about two minutes. Every connected channel uses one, and it is the bot that actually publishes. You do not need to write code or host anything. ## The two setup steps, in this order 1. Connect your sender bot. In the bot, tap ➕ Create bot (it opens @BotFather with the name already prepared) or 🔑 I Have a Token if you already own a bot. The token is verified with Telegram and stored. Full detail: Sender Bot First: the New Setup. 2. Open that bot to link the channel and set the time zone. The sender bot opens on an I'm live screen whose first row is a green Add bot to a channel button: it opens Telegram's own channel picker with the bot pre-selected and Post Messages already ticked. After you confirm, the bot re-checks by itself ten seconds later. Then it asks for the zone — a city, your current time, a shared location or 📋 Choose from list — and stores it for that channel . A zone you set for another channel is never overwritten.Forwarding a post from the channel, sending @username or a t.me link, and adding the bot from a private channel's own settings all still work: Connecting a Channel. If the channel already has a sender bot and you are one of its administrators, you do not need the owner — send that bot's @username or token and the bot verifies your rights: Join a Channel That Already Has a Bot. The main bot never needs to be an administrator in your channel. It is your account hub — channels, sender bots, Premium, help. Keeping it as an admin is optional and only matters if you want the stand-in safety net (Main-Bot Stand-In). ## What the first-run tutorial actually shows After /start and the terms screen, the bot introduces itself — what it does, why it is worth using, and what the two steps are — then asks for the sender bot. That is the whole tutorial in the main bot; the channel and the time zone are handled inside the sender bot, where the actual publishing lives. Every screen can be skipped safely: nothing is deleted, and the step-by-step walkthrough picks up wherever you left off. ## Your very first post Open the sender bot → 📅 Schedule a Message and send the date and the text in one message: 25.12.2026 10:00 Happy holidays from our channel! To queue several at once, separate the pairs with one empty line: 24.12.2026 18:00 Christmas Eve: doors open at 18:00 25.12.2026 12:00 Today's menu and the holiday playlist 26.12.2026 09:00 Thank you for the year — see you in January The bot shows a review card per message with the channel, the time and a preview. Check it, confirm, and the queue is built. Media, buttons and the per-post options are explained in Send Your First Post. ## If something does not work • "A sender bot is required" — that channel has no bot yet: Connecting a Bot.• The channel looks locked in a picker — it is managed by its sender bot; tap it and choose 🤖 Open Sender Bot , scheduling happens there.• "Bot is not an admin" — promote the sender bot in the channel with Post Messages: Channel Permissions.• Post went out at the wrong hour — the channel's own time zone is used: Why Was My Scheduled Post Published at the Wrong Time? ## Where to go next • Every Menu and Button: the Interface Map — what each screen opens, written so a person or an AI assistant can follow the exact path. • Media Modes Explained — Normal, Random, Sequential and Skip. • All Commands — every command the bot accepts. • Admins &amp; Access — letting a co-administrator schedule safely.

Q: Do I need to know how to code to use Fast Scheduler?
A: No. You create a bot in @BotFather by tapping a few buttons, and the bot walks you through the rest. Nothing is hosted, installed or programmed by you.

Q: How many posts can I schedule for free?
A: One channel, one sender bot, 100 scheduled messages and one recurring rule. Premium raises this to three channels, three bots and unlimited scheduled and recurring posts.

Q: Can I schedule a whole week at once?
A: Yes — send date + text pairs separated by an empty line and every pair becomes its own scheduled post with its own time.

Q: Does the main bot need to be an administrator in my channel?
A: No. Publishing runs through your sender bot. Adding the main bot as an admin is optional and only used for the stand-in when your sender bot breaks.

## Sender Bot First: the New Setup
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/sender_bot_setup.html

The setup now starts with the bot that actually does the work: your sender bot . The main bot is no longer a channel administrator, and you never have to add it to the channel just to get started. ## Why the order changed Making the main bot a channel admin was a detour: it does not publish, it does not hold the channel's settings, and its only job in the old flow was to verify rights so it could hand the channel to a sender bot. Now the sender bot verifies itself, in its own chat, and the main bot stays a chat with a menu. ## Step 1 — connect a sender bot On the first /start , after the welcome screen, the bot asks for a sender bot and nothing else: • ➕ Create bot opens @BotFather with a name already prepared; • 🔑 I Have a Token accepts a token you already have. The token is verified with Telegram, stored, and the bot answers with a green Open @your_bot button. One sender bot serves exactly one channel. ## Step 2 — add it to the channel from inside itself Open the sender bot and it shows the "I'm live" screen. The first row is a green ➕ Add bot to a channel button: 1. Tap it. Telegram's own channel picker opens with the bot pre-selected as an administrator and Post Messages already ticked. 2. Pick the channel and confirm. 3. The bot re-checks by itself after 10 seconds and continues to the time zone when the rights are there. You do not have to press anything. ## The five-a-day rule That automatic re-check is capped at 5 taps per day per account, because each one is a real Telegram API call and the button is easy to hammer. The 6th tap still opens the picker — it just stops auto-checking, and the screen says so. Use 🔄 Check Again afterwards; manual checks are unlimited. ## Other ways to connect • Forward any post from the channel to the sender bot. • Send the channel's @username or a t.me link. • Private channel? Add the sender bot as an administrator from the channel's own settings; the bot picks it up through Telegram's update, no link needed. • The channel already has a sender bot and you are a co-admin? Send that bot's @username or token — see Join a Channel That Already Has a Bot. ## Step 3 — the time zone belongs to the channel The last screen asks for a zone and accepts a city ( London ), your current time ( 15:30 ), a shared location, or a pick from the list. The zone is stored for that channel only . Your account default is filled in only if you never set one, so channels you configured earlier keep exactly the zone they had. Nothing is applied to all channels behind your back. ## The main bot is optional — but it earns its place You can delete it from the channel list and everything keeps working; publishing, statistics, backups and admin management all live in the sender bot. The reasons to keep it as an administrator anyway: • Stand-in during an outage. If your sender bot's token is revoked or it loses rights, the main bot can deliver the scheduled post once and offer to keep posting for a bounded window (3 days by default). It needs Post Messages for that, and it never starts on its own. See Main-Bot Stand-In. • Support and expiry notices arrive in the main bot chat. • Recovery — if you lose the sender bot entirely, the main bot is where you reconnect a new one. ## Adding more channels later ➕ Add New Channel in the main bot no longer asks for a channel link first. It lists your idle sender bots; pick one and it opens with the connect flow already running. No idle bot? Create or connect one right there. A channel connected without a sender bot stays locked, by design. ## Troubleshooting • "@bot is not an administrator yet" — tap the green Add button and make sure Post Messages is ticked, then Check Again. • Auto-check paused — you used today's five. Tap Check Again after adding the bot. • Wrong time zone — change it per channel in the sender bot; it does not touch other channels. • Channel already managed — the bot names the existing sender bot and explains the @username/token route. ## Related The First-Run Tutorial, Join a Channel That Already Has a Bot, Main-Bot Stand-In, Add a Sender Bot.

Q: Do I still have to add @FastSchedulerBot to my channel?
A: No. Publishing, scheduling, statistics and settings all run through your sender bot. The main bot only needs Post Messages if you want the optional stand-in during an outage.

Q: Why does the bot wait ten seconds instead of continuing instantly?
A: Because Telegram delivers the "bot promoted to administrator" update on its own schedule; a second is often not enough. Ten seconds is a compromise between a silent wait and a screen that lies about the result.

Q: What happens after the five automatic checks?
A: The button still opens the channel picker, but the bot stops watching for the promotion. Finish adding the bot, come back, and press Check Again — that path is not limited.

Q: Does the time zone I set change my other channels?
A: No. It is saved for that channel only. The account default is written only if it is still empty, so previously configured channels are never rewritten.

Q: Can I connect a channel without a sender bot?
A: You can attach it in the main bot as an escape hatch, but scheduling stays locked: posts go out through a bot, and every channel needs its own. See Posting as Your Bot.

## Every Menu and Button: the Interface Map
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/interface_map.html

This page is the map of the bot. It lists the real buttons in the order you see them and says what each one opens. Use it to follow a guide, to explain the bot to someone else, or to give an AI assistant the exact path instead of a guess. ## Two chats, two jobs Fast Scheduler uses two chats, and mixing them up is the most common source of confusion: • @FastSchedulerBot (the main bot) — your account hub. It holds the channel list, the bot list, language, help, referrals, premium and data import/export. On a fresh account it also shows scheduling. • Your sender bot — the bot you created in @BotFather. It posts to one channel and holds that channel's scheduling: Schedule a Message, Recurring Messages, Message List, Statistics, Calendar, and the channel Settings menu. As soon as a channel is connected to a sender bot, its management moves to that bot. The main bot then shows a compact hub. That is not a downgrade or an error — it is how per-channel isolation works. ## Main menu, page 1 The menu is two pages; ➡️ Next and ⬅️ Previous switch between them. • 📅 Schedule a Message — opens the scheduling flow: you send the date/time and the post, then review and confirm. Requires a connected channel with a sender bot. Guide: One-Time Schedule. • 🔄 Recurring Messages — creates a repeating post (daily, weekly, chosen weekdays) instead of a one-time one. Guide: Recurring Messages. • 📢 Channels (N) — opens the channel overview: every connected channel, add a channel, and per-channel actions. Guide: Manage Channels. • 🤖 Bots (N) — opens the sender-bot list with each bot's channel and a ⚙ Manage menu. Guide: Manage Sender Bots. • 📋 Message List — the queue. It first asks which list: Scheduled messages (N) or Recurring messages (N) , then shows each message with its ID and controls (preview, edit, delete). Guide: Message List. • 💾 Media Storage — your reusable media library: boxes, files, previews. Only visible when storage is enabled. Guide: Storage Boxes. • ⭐ Upgrade to Premium (or ⭐ Premium: Active ) — plans, prices, payment in Telegram Stars, promo codes, cancel. Guide: Buy Premium. • ➡️ Next — page 2. ## Main menu, page 2 • 🔍 Search — finds messages by text, channel, date phrase or status, with filters. Guide: Searching Messages. • 📊 Statistics — per-channel performance and leaderboards. Guide: Statistics Dashboard. • 📅 Calendar — a month view of what is queued, sent or failed, with day drill-down. Guide: Calendar View. • 🎁 Referral Program (BETA) — your invite link, earned Premium days, history. Guide: How Referrals Work. • 🗂 Data — export and import. It contains exactly two actions: 📤 Export and 📥 Import . Backups are separate (see below). Guide: Export Data and Importing Your Data. • ❓ Help — opens a short page that sends you to @FastSchedulerSupport_bot , which serves the full help tree, the AI topic finder and human support. Guide: /help. • ⚙️ Settings — on page 2 of a sender bot there are two Settings entries side by side: the left one is the channel's settings, the right one is your account's settings. On the main bot account settings are reached with /settings . • 🔧 Admin Panel — only for the bot's administrators. It is not part of the normal user interface. ## Channel Settings (in the sender bot) Left ⚙️ Settings opens Channel Settings for that bot's channel: • 🔒 Hide channel from strangers / 🔓 Show channel to strangers — controls whether people who start your sender bot see your channel name. Guide: How Posting Works: Sender Bots. • 👥 Admins — owner only; adds co-admins with per-area rights and handles permission requests. Guide: Permissions & Requests. • 🏠 Open @FastSchedulerBot — jumps back to the main bot. • ❌ Back — returns to the menu. ## Account Settings Right ⚙️ Settings (or /settings ) opens: • 🌐 Language — the bot's language. Guide: Change Language. • 🕐 Time Zone — where the bot thinks you are. Guide: Set Time Zone. • 💾 Media Storage — the storage library. • 📝 Signature — the automatic footer added to posts (Premium). Guide: Signatures (Premium). • ⭐ Upgrade to Premium — plans and payment. • 🎁 Referral Program — invite link and rewards. • 📮 Feedback — opens the feedback entry point; the actual support conversation happens in @FastSchedulerSupport_bot. Guide: Send Feedback. • 📋 All commands — the same list as /commands . • ❌ Back — main menu. ## The Channels screen 📢 Channels (N) shows every connected channel with its time zone, sender bot and counts. From here you can add a channel and open a channel's card. The card shows the channel, its sender bot, its time zone, scheduled/recurring counts, and buttons: • 🕐 Time Zone: … — change this channel's zone. • 👥 Admins — owner only, in the sender bot. • 🔄 Change Channel — move the sender bot to another channel you own. • 🔗 Disconnect Channel — removes the connection after a confirmation that counts the affected posts. Queue entries are not deleted; they stay keyed to that channel and simply stop sending until you reconnect it. Guide: Unlink vs Delete. When you pick a channel for an action (schedule, recurring, messages, stats, calendar), managed channels appear as 🤖 Managed: … in red. Tapping one does not fail silently: it explains that the channel is managed by its sender bot and offers 🤖 Open Sender Bot . Free channels appear as 🆓 Free: … and open the action directly. ## The Bots screen 🤖 Bots (N) lists your sender bots. Each row opens ⚙ Manage @yourbot , which contains: • 🔑 Change token — the bot was revoked in @BotFather; paste the new token for the same bot. • 🔁 Replace bot — swap this bot for a different one; data moves over. • 🔀 Switch channel — attach this bot to another channel you own. • ⇄ Swap bots — exchange the channels of two of your bots. • 🗑 Remove bot — detach the bot from its channel. Guides: Manage Sender Bots, Rotate Token, Remove a Sender Bot. ## The scheduling flow, screen by screen 1. Tap 📅 Schedule a Message . The prompt explains the format and shows an example. 2. Send DD.MM.YYYY HH:MM and the post text in one message. You can send several posts separated by blank lines. 3. If media is allowed, choose a mode: 📷 Normal , 🎲 Random , 🔀 Sequential , ⏭ Skip Photos , or 💾From storage . Then send the files and finish with ✅ Done (N) . 4. The Review card appears: channels, time, preview, media count, inline-button count. Buttons: ✏️ Edit , 💾 Change media , 📢 Change channel , 📢 Choose channels (multi-channel, Premium), ✅ Schedule . 5. After confirmation the post is queued and appears in 📋 Message List and 📅 Calendar . Every step has its own article — start at Send Your First Post or jump to Media Modes Explained. ## Things that are easy to miss • Backups are not in 🗂 Data. Use /backup for the backup menu and /export for selective exports. Guide: Create Backup. • Deleting is not in 🗂 Data either. Use 📋 Message List → a message → 🗑 Delete , or /delete for the delete menu (including 🗑 Delete by ID ). Guide: Delete Messages. • Help is duplicated in the support bot. @FastSchedulerSupport_bot serves the same articles, plus human support and the AI assistant. Guide: Support. • Premium is paid in Telegram Stars , and the price shown in the in-bot checkout is the authoritative one. Guide: Telegram Stars.

Q: Where is the button for X?
A: Use this page as the index: page 1 holds scheduling, channels, bots, the message list, storage and Premium; page 2 holds search, statistics, calendar, referrals, data, help and settings. If a feature is channel-specific, it lives in the sender bot, not the main bot.

Q: Why are there two Settings buttons in my sender bot?
A: One configures the channel (Hide channel, Admins), the other configures your account (language, time zone, signature, commands). The left button is the channel, the right one is the account.

Q: Why is a channel shown in red as “Managed”?
A: That channel already has a sender bot, so its scheduling and settings live there. Tap the channel and the bot offers 🤖 Open Sender Bot; the main bot intentionally does not duplicate channel controls.

Q: Does the bot have a web dashboard?
A: No. Everything is done in Telegram: the main bot for account-level actions and the sender bot for a channel. The website only hosts documentation, legal pages and the blog.

## The First-Run Tutorial, Step by Step
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tutorial_walkthrough.html

The tutorial is the shortest path from an empty chat to a working channel. It runs once, after /start , and has two screens in the main bot: connect your sender bot , then open it . The channel and the time zone are set inside the sender bot, in one short flow — the main bot never has to be a channel administrator. ## Before the first screen Have these ready and the whole thing takes about two minutes: • You are an administrator of the channel (not just its owner in name — Telegram must list you as an admin). You do not need to add @FastSchedulerBot anywhere. • You can open @BotFather in another chat, because step 3 creates a bot there. ## Screen 0 — Welcome The bot explains what it does and offers: • 📡 Connect a Channel — starts step 1. • Help Center — opens the in-bot help instead of the tutorial. • ⏭ Skip tutorial — asks for confirmation; ✅ Yes, skip ends the tutorial, ❌ No, continue returns to the exact screen you left. If you skip, nothing breaks. The channel list simply stays empty until you add one from 📢 Channels . ## Step 1/3 — Connect Your Channel The screen reminds you that the bot must be an admin with Post Messages . Then send one of: • the channel link, e.g. https://t.me/yourchannel or @yourchannel ; • any forwarded post from the channel; • the numeric channel ID (starts with -100 ). What success looks like: the bot confirms the channel and shows ▶️ Next . What failure looks like and the fix: • "Bot is not an admin" — open the channel → Administrators → Add Administrator → @FastSchedulerBot → enable Post Messages. Then send the link again. • "Channel not found" — the username is wrong or the channel is private. Forward a post from it instead of typing the username. • Nothing happens — you may have sent the link while the bot was waiting for something else. Tap ❌ Cancel , reopen the tutorial, and send it again. Full reference: Step 1: Connect a Channel and Connecting a Channel. ## Step 2/3 — Time Zone Setup Send a city name ( London , New York , Tokyo ), your current time ( 15:30 ), or a location . The bot proposes a zone and you confirm. If detection fails, tap 📋 Choose from list and pick your zone from the grid. What success looks like: "Time zone set to …" and the sender-bot step appears. What failure looks like: the message "Couldn't detect your time zone from that" — this is not an error state, just a miss; try a bigger city name or the list. You can always change it later in ⚙️ Settings → 🕐 Time Zone . ## Step 3/3 — Connect a Sender Bot Two buttons: • ➕ Create New Bot — opens @BotFather with instructions. Send /newbot , choose a display name and a username ending in bot , then copy the token (looks like 1234567890:ABCdef… ). • 🔑 I Have a Token — paste an existing token. After pasting the token the bot asks you to make that bot an administrator of the channel with Post Messages, and offers 🔄 Check Again . Press it once you have added the bot. When verification passes, the tutorial ends with "Tutorial Complete" and a button to open the sender bot. Common failures, in order of frequency: • "Invalid token" — a partial copy. Copy the entire line from @BotFather, including the colon. • Token belongs to another bot — the bot tells you which username the token belongs to; use the matching token or create a new bot. • "Bot is not admin" — add the sender bot (the one you just created) to the channel as an administrator. The main bot being admin is not enough for this check. • You already sent a token for another bot — the bot asks whether to cancel the old bot and connect the new one. Choose ✅ Cancel @old & connect @new only if you really want to replace it. Reference: Step 2: Connect a Sender Bot and Add a Sender Bot. ## After the tutorial The channel is now managed by its sender bot. Open it with 🤖 Open Sender Bot and tap 📅 Schedule a Message . The main bot keeps 📢 Channels , 🤖 Bots , language, help, referrals and Premium. ## Starting the tutorial again Send /start . If your account is already configured, the bot skips the setup screens and shows the normal menu — that is expected. To redo a single step, use the menus instead: 📢 Channels → 📢 Connect Channel , ⚙️ Settings → 🕐 Time Zone , 🤖 Bots → 🔑 I Have a Token .

Q: I skipped the tutorial. How do I get it back?
A: Send /start. On an already-configured account the tutorial does not repeat, because there is nothing left to set up. Use 📢 Channels → 📢 Connect Channel, ⚙️ Settings → 🕐 Time Zone and 🤖 Bots to finish the same three steps manually.

Q: The tutorial is stuck on step 1 and my channel is fine.
A: Cancel the current screen with ❌ Cancel, then start again. If it still refuses, forward a post from the channel instead of sending its username — forwarding proves the channel and your admin rights at the same time.

Q: Can I connect a channel someone else owns?
A: Only if they add you as an administrator, and only the channel owner can connect it to their account. If the channel is already configured, the bot detects the existing sender bot and says so instead of asking you to create another one.

Q: Do I have to create the sender bot during the tutorial?
A: You can paste an existing bot token with 🔑 I Have a Token, but you cannot skip the step entirely: scheduling needs a sender bot for every connected channel.

## Tutorial Step 1: Connect Your Sender Bot
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/onboarding_step1.html

The tutorial starts with the bot that will actually publish, not with a channel link. You do not need a channel yet, and you do not need to make @FastSchedulerBot an administrator anywhere. ## The screen It explains that a sender bot is your own Telegram bot, then offers: • ➕ Create bot — opens @BotFather with a name and username already prepared. Confirm in BotFather, copy the token it prints, come back. • 🔑 I Have a Token — paste a token from a bot you already created. • ⏭ Skip tutorial — asks for confirmation and ends the tutorial. You can connect a sender bot later from 🤖 Bots . ## What a token looks like 1234567890:ABCdefGhIJKlmNoPQRsTUVwxyZ — one line, a number, a colon, then letters and digits. If the bot says the token is invalid, the copy was truncated; copy the whole line again. ## What success looks like The bot verifies the token with Telegram and answers with Token saved for @your_bot plus a green Open @your_bot button. Tap it: the channel and the time zone are connected there, inside the sender bot. The tutorial on the main-bot side is finished at that point — there is no third step here to come back for. ## If it fails • Invalid token — truncated copy, or a token that was already revoked. • That is the main bot's token — create your own bot; the shared bot cannot post as you. • Limit reached — the Free plan allows 1 sender bot; see Sender Bot Limit. • Nothing happens — make sure you are in a private chat with the bot, not a group. ## Related Sender Bot First: the New Setup, Add a Sender Bot, Tutorial Step 2: Channel and Time Zone.

## Tutorial Step 2: Channel and Time Zone (in the Sender Bot)
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/onboarding_step2.html

Once the sender bot is connected, open it with the green button. It shows the "I'm live" screen, because it has no channel yet. ## Connect the channel 1. Tap the green ➕ Add bot to a channel row. 2. Telegram opens its channel picker with the bot pre-selected as an administrator and Post Messages ticked. Choose the channel and confirm. 3. The bot re-checks on its own after 10 seconds (5 automatic checks per day) and continues automatically. Forwarding a post, sending @username or adding the bot from a private channel's settings works just as well. ## Set the zone The link confirmation asks for the zone straight away: a city ( London ), the current time ( 15:30 ), a shared location, or a pick from the list. It is saved for this channel ; your other channels keep theirs, and the account default is filled only if it was never set. ## Done The last screen is All set — your time zone with a dashboard button. Scheduling, statistic, backups and admin management all live here from now on. ## Related Tutorial Step 1: Connect Your Sender Bot, Sender Bot First: the New Setup, Set a Time Zone.

## After the Tutorial: Your Sender Bot Dashboard
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/onboarding_step3.html

The first-run tutorial is two steps now — sender bot, then channel and time zone inside it. There is no third on-screen step to hunt for; this article covers where the rest of the old flow went. ## What you land on After the time zone is saved the sender bot shows the dashboard: 📅 Schedule , 🔁 Recurring , 📋 Messages , 📊 Statistics , ⚙️ Settings (admins, backups, hide channel) and 🌐 Language . Rows disappear for anyone without the matching permission, so a co-admin sees a shorter, honest menu. ## Where old Step 3 went The old third step asked you to promote the sender bot in the channel and press Check Again. That is now part of the "Add bot to a channel" button inside the sender bot: the picker grants the rights, and the automatic 10-second check replaces the manual verification. If you added the bot by hand, the screen still offers 🔄 Check Again . ## Adding people Settings → 👥 Admins is where co-admins are added, limited and removed. Read Admins & Access before handing out delete or export rights; the defaults are deliberately conservative. ## Related Sender Bot First: the New Setup, Admins & Access, Schedule Your First Post.

## Glossary
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/glossary.html

Most confusion in Fast Scheduler comes from six words. Here they are, with a link to the full article for each. • Channel — the Telegram channel your posts go to. The bot must be an administrator there. Channel. • Sender bot — your own Telegram bot that delivers the posts. One per channel, required before scheduling. Sender Bot. • Scheduled message — a one-time post queued for an exact date and time. One-Time Schedule. • Recurring message — a post on a repeating pattern (daily, weekly, chosen weekdays) until paused or deleted. Recurring. • Signature — a footer added to every post in a channel (Premium). Signature. • Premium — the paid plan: more channels and bots, unlimited queues, bigger media and storage. Premium. The remaining terms you will meet in menus: • Normal / Random / Sequential / Skip — how media is attached to posts. Media Modes Explained. • Storage box — a folder in Media Storage that holds reusable files. Storage Boxes. • Export — a file with your data that you can re-import. Export. • Import — loading such a file back into an account. Import. • Feedback — a ticket to support, sent from the support bot. Feedback.

Q: What is the difference between a channel and a sender bot?
A: The channel is where readers are; the sender bot is the author that publishes there. Fast Scheduler connects the two, which is why both must be set up.

## Channel
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/glossary_channel.html

A channel is the Telegram destination for your posts: subscribers read it, and only administrators can publish. For Fast Scheduler a channel becomes usable when three things are true: you are an administrator, the bot is an administrator with Post Messages , and the bot has resolved the channel identity. Then the channel appears in 📢 Channels with its own time zone, queue and sender bot. A channel is not a group. Groups have members who can write; channels have subscribers and a posting admin list. The bot's permission checks differ, which is why some actions (like inline buttons) behave differently. Read more: Connecting a Channel, Channel Permissions.

## Sender Bot
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/glossary_sender.html

A sender bot is a Telegram bot created by you in @BotFather and connected to exactly one channel. It is the visible author of your posts. Without a sender bot the channel cannot be scheduled — the button stays locked and the bot explains why. With one, posts carry your bot's name and photo, arrive faster, and unlock per-channel statistics and settings. One bot per channel. Free allows one bot, Premium three. Losing or revoking the token does not lose data: paste the new token under ⚙ Manage → 🔑 Change token . Read more: Connecting a Bot, Manage Sender Bots.

## Signature
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/glossary_signature.html

A signature is text automatically added to the end of every post in a channel — a handle, a slogan, a link line. It is a Premium feature and belongs to a channel, so two channels can have different signatures. Set it in ⚙️ Settings → 📝 Signature . The signature is applied when the post is sent, so changing it affects future posts rather than rewriting history. Keep it short: it consumes part of the caption limit and is repeated on every post. Read more: Signatures (Premium), Signature Position.

## Recurring
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/glossary_recurring.html

A recurring message repeats automatically: every day at a time, certain weekdays, or another pattern the bot offers. You write it once; the scheduler keeps publishing it. Each occurrence is created from the same template, so editing the recurring message changes future occurrences. Pausing stops new sends without deleting the rule; resuming continues from the next matching slot. Free accounts can keep one recurring message, Premium unlimited. Recurring rules also count toward the channel's scheduled-message accounting. Read more: Recurring Messages, Pause & Resume.

## Premium
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/glossary_premium.html

Premium is the paid tier: up to 3 channels and 3 sender bots instead of 1, unlimited scheduled and recurring messages, larger uploads (up to 100 MB, video up to 50 MB), 20 storage boxes with 500 items, signatures, multi-channel targeting, advanced statistics and protected backups. It is paid in Telegram Stars. Monthly and yearly options exist; the exact price is always the one shown in the in-bot checkout. Promo codes are applied in the same purchase flow. Premium follows your account, not a single channel. If it lapses, channels beyond the free limits become frozen rather than deleted, and you choose what to keep. Read more: Premium Features, Compare Plans, Buy Premium.

## Import
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/glossary_import.html

Import reads a file produced by Fast Scheduler — a JSON export, a .fsback backup or a password-protected .fspback — and recreates its messages, channels and bots in your account. You choose between overwrite existing and add all . Overwrite replaces matching data; add keeps everything and can therefore create duplicates. Limits apply on import: messages beyond your plan's cap are refused and the import is cancelled rather than half-applied. Open it from 🗂 Data → 📥 Import or /import . Read more: Importing Your Data, Supported Import Formats.

## Export
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/glossary_export.html

Export writes your data to a file: JSON/CSV/TXT/RTF/ODT for messages, or the full backup formats .fsback (plain) and .fspback (password-protected). A full export includes messages, channels, bots and settings. If the selection includes sender bot tokens, the bot automatically switches to Protected Backup and asks for a password — tokens are never exported unencrypted. Start it from 🗂 Data → 📤 Export or /export . Read more: Export Data, Create Backup.

## Storage
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/glossary_storage.html

Media Storage is a library of files you can attach to posts repeatedly without re-uploading them. Files live in boxes ; you can preview, rename, move, copy, replace or delete items. It is useful for logos, banners, price cards and recurring creatives. Free allows 1 box with 100 items and no stored video; Premium allows 20 boxes with 500 items and video up to 50 MB. Open it with 💾 Media Storage , /storage , or 💾From storage during scheduling. Read more: Storage Boxes, When to Use Storage.

Q: What is media storage?
A: Media storage keeps your photos/videos in named boxes so you can reuse visuals across messages without re-uploading them.

## Feedback
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/glossary_feedback.html

Feedback is the support ticket system. Tickets are sent from @FastSchedulerSupport_bot , not from the main bot, and can carry text plus photos or video. The main bot's 📮 Feedback button and /feedback redirect you to the support bot. There you choose a category, write the message, optionally attach media, and submit. You can follow the ticket's status and read replies in the same bot. Read more: Send Feedback, Support.

## SetDate Integration
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/setdate.html

SetDate is a companion bot for the one job that is painful in a chat: turning a list of posts into a dated schedule. It is @SetDate_bot . ## When to use it • You have 20–100 posts to queue. • You want a repeating rhythm (three posts a day at 09:00, 14:00, 18:00). • Your posts already exist as a text file. For one or two posts, the normal scheduler is faster. ## The flow 1. Start scheduling in Fast Scheduler and choose the Open SetDate option when offered, or open @SetDate_bot directly. 2. Set the start date and how many posts per day. 3. Define the times, e.g. 09:00 , 14:00 , 18:00 . 4. Send the texts — one per block separated by blank lines, or one by one, or upload a .txt file. 5. Generate the schedule. SetDate shows a summary with dates and totals and lets you download .txt , .csv or .json . 6. Tap Import to Fast Scheduler . You return with all messages pre-loaded. 7. Choose media options and confirm. ## Formats and details • Times accept 08:00 , 2:00 PM and similar variants. • Dates accept European and American orders. • Inline button markup ( &lt;inline&gt;… ) carries over. • Media is not uploaded in SetDate; you attach it during import in Fast Scheduler. ## Language Both bots share your language preference; changing it in one offers to sync the other. ## Limits The imported messages count toward the same Fast Scheduler limits as manually scheduled ones (Scheduled Limit). If the batch would overflow the queue, reduce the batch or upgrade. Related: Import From Storage, Bulk Tips.

Q: Do I need SetDate to schedule many posts?
A: No. You can send many dated blocks in one message, separated by blank lines, or upload a .txt file. SetDate is a convenience for large batches and time grids.

Q: Does SetDate post anything itself?
A: No. It only builds the schedule; publishing always happens through Fast Scheduler and your sender bot.

## Advertising & Promotion
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/advertising.html

## Advertising in the bot Fast Scheduler does not run a self-serve ad platform. Placements for the bot's own audience are arranged directly: contact @MaximalXP to discuss formats and availability. ## Promoting your channel The bot does not buy ads for you. For paid reach on Telegram, the official Telegram Ads platform is available for eligible public channels; for cross-promotion with other channels, agree terms directly with their owners. ## Free promotion through referrals The cheapest promotion is the referral program: invite another channel owner, and when they connect a channel and create at least one message, both sides earn Premium days. Your link is in 🎁 Referral Program (BETA) or /referral . Rules: How Referrals Work. ## Being promoted by us If you want your channel featured, the same contact applies. There is no automated purchase flow and no guarantee of placement — everything is agreed manually.

Q: Can I buy advertising inside the bot?
A: No. Advertising is arranged by contacting @MaximalXP; the bot itself has no ad marketplace.

Q: Is there a referral reward for inviting channels?
A: Yes — 3 Premium days per qualifying invite, bankable up to 15 invites. The program is in beta.

# Scheduling Messages

## Scheduling Messages
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/scheduling.html

A scheduled message is a post that waits for its moment. You create it once; the bot publishes it at the chosen time in the channel's time zone, even when your phone is offline. ## The basic flow in six steps 1. In the sender bot for your channel, tap 📅 Schedule a Message (or send /schedule ). 2. Send the date/time on the first line and the post below it. 3. Choose how media is attached: 📷 Normal , 🎲 Random , 🔀 Sequential , ⏭ Skip Photos or 💾From storage . 4. Send the media files, then tap ✅ Done (N) . 5. Check the Review card — channel, time, preview, media and button counts. 6. Tap ✅ Schedule . The post is queued and gets an ID. ## What you can schedule Text, photos, videos, animations, documents, voice and audio, locations, stickers, polls and quizzes, and albums of up to 10 items. Formatting, links, spoilers and inline buttons survive the trip. The exact support matrix is in Supported Content Types. ## What you cannot do • Premium/custom emoji are stripped (the text stays). • Telegram date formatting and rich Articles are not rendered. • Checklists are unsupported. • Polls must be anonymous — that is a Telegram rule for channels. • Scheduling needs a connected channel with a sender bot . Without one the button explains what is missing. ## Managing the queue Everything you queue appears in 📋 Message List and 📅 Calendar . From there you can preview, edit, delete, pause a recurring rule, or find its ID. The list is the source of truth — a post exists until it is sent or deleted. ## The rest of this section • Media Modes Explained — the four modes, with examples. • Review Before Sending — what the review card checks. • Edit Messages and Delete Messages — change or remove queued posts. • Find and Delete Duplicate Posts — clean up copies safely. • Recurring Messages — daily, weekly, monthly or cron. • Multi-Channel Scheduling — one post, several channels.

Q: Where does scheduling happen — main bot or sender bot?
A: In the sender bot for that channel. The main bot shows the channel as managed and offers a button to open its sender bot. This is per-channel isolation, not a restriction you can remove.

Q: Can I schedule while my phone is off?
A: Yes. The queue lives on the server. Close Telegram, switch off the phone — the post is still delivered at the chosen time as long as the channel and its sender bot remain connected.

## One-Time Schedule
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/schedule_one_time.html

A one-time message is published once, at one exact moment. It is the default kind of post and the simplest thing the bot does. ## Create it 1. Open the sender bot for the channel and tap 📅 Schedule a Message . 2. Send the date line and the content: 25.12.2026 10:00 Happy holidays from our channel! 3. Choose media or tap ⏭ Skip Photos . 4. Review the card and tap ✅ Schedule . ## Several posts at once Separate blocks with a blank line. Each block starts with its own date: 25.12.2026 10:00 First post 26.12.2026 10:00 Second post The bot counts them and creates one job per block. You can keep sending more blocks before confirming. ## What you get back A confirmation with the job ID(s) and the send time. The post now appears in: • 📋 Message List → Scheduled messages , with 👁 preview, ✏️ edit and 🗑 delete; • 📅 Calendar , on its day, marked as scheduled. ## Before it sends Everything stays editable: text, time, media, target channel. Use ✏️ Edit in the list or /edit ID . To copy a post to another moment, /dub ID creates a duplicate one day later. ## When it sends The queue entry disappears from the scheduled list and the post appears in the channel. Statistics for the channel update. If delivery fails, the calendar marks it ❌ Failed and the bot reports why — see Common Errors. ## Choose the right tool • One moment → this article. • Repeats on a pattern → Recurring Messages. • Many posts generated from a list → SetDate Integration or a .txt upload (Advanced Scheduling). • Same post to several channels → Multi-Channel Scheduling.

Q: Can I edit a post after it was sent?
A: Only if it is still in the queue. Once published, the bot can no longer change it from the scheduler; edit it in Telegram itself if your admin rights allow it.

Q: What happens if the bot is offline at send time?
A: Delivery is attempted by the scheduler when the moment arrives. A transient failure is reported and can be retried from the failure notice; a channel that lost the bot as admin fails permanently until the permission is restored.

## Text Posts
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/schedule_text.html

Text is the default content type: everything below the date line becomes the post. ## Formatting that works Telegram's markdown-style markup is converted when the post is sent: • **bold** • __italic__ • ___underline___ • ~~strikethrough~~ • ||spoiler|| • `inline code` and triple-backtick blocks • [label](https://example.com) for links The full syntax, including nested combinations, is in Formatting & Inline Buttons. ## Length Telegram caps a text message at 4096 characters and a caption at 1024. Long text is rejected rather than silently truncated, so if a post is cut off in the review, shorten it or split it into two dated blocks. ## Buttons Add clickable buttons with: &lt;inline&gt;Read more&lt;link="https://example.com"&gt; Each button on its own line; -- keeps two on one row, // starts a new row. Colours: style="success" , style="primary" , style="danger" . The markup lines are removed from the published text. ## Unicode and emoji Standard emoji work. Premium/custom emoji are not supported and are stripped, leaving the surrounding text. Armenian punctuation and mixed scripts are normalised so dates and commands still parse. ## What to avoid • Sending the text before the date line — the first line is parsed as the date. • Blank lines inside one post — that starts a new message block. • A pasted date in a different order without a separator; use DD.MM.YYYY or ISO. Related: Captions & Formatting, Supported Content Types.

Q: Can I send a text-only post?
A: Yes. Choose ⏭ Skip Photos at the media step, or simply do not attach files. The queue stores it as a text post.

## Photo & Video Posts
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/schedule_media.html

Media turns a text post into a visual one. The bot attaches files at send time, so the file you pick now is what is published later. ## After the text, pick a mode • 📷 Normal — one file attached to every message in the batch. Good for a logo, watermark or brand frame. • 🎲 Random — send several files; each post gets a random one. Good for variety. • 🔀 Sequential — files are assigned in order, one per post, repeating when the list ends. Order can be 📅 By Date or 📤 By Sent Order . • 💾From storage — reuse files saved in Media Storage. • ⏭ Skip Photos — no media. Then send the files and tap ✅ Done (N) . The counter confirms how many were accepted. ## Captions The text you wrote becomes the caption when media is attached. Keep captions within Telegram's caption limit (1024 characters); longer text is better as a text post with a separate media post. ## Size and compression Free plan: photos up to 10 MB, video up to 25 MB. Premium: up to 100 MB, video up to 50 MB. Photos and videos are compressed for delivery (Free compresses harder); Premium keeps more detail. Files are validated when you send them, so an oversized video is refused immediately. ## Mixed types Random mode accepts a mix of photos, videos, documents and other supported media; each pick is sent with the method that matches its type. Sequential mode works the same way across types. ## What can go wrong • "Only media files are allowed here" — you sent text while the bot waited for files. Send the file or press Done/Cancel. • Video refused — over the plan limit; compress it or upgrade. • Nothing attached — the batch may have been created before the files were confirmed. Check the review card's media count. Comparison of all modes: Media Modes Explained.

Q: Can each post in a batch get a different photo?
A: Yes — use Sequential mode with several files. First post gets the first file, second gets the second, and the list repeats when it runs out.

Q: Is the original quality preserved?
A: Not exactly. Photos and videos are compressed before sending, more aggressively on Free than Premium. Documents are sent without compression.

## Video Posts
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/schedule_video.html

Videos are attached like photos but have stricter limits and more ways to look wrong. ## Limits • Free: up to 25 MB per video. • Premium: up to 50 MB per video. Formats: MP4, MOV, AVI and other common containers. The bot validates size when you send the file, so oversized videos are refused before scheduling. ## Inline video vs document Telegram decides how a video is displayed from its metadata and size. A video that Telegram cannot stream reliably arrives as a file attachment instead of a playable bubble. If that matters, export as MP4/H.264 with standard dimensions and keep the file well under the limit. ## Compression The bot compresses videos for delivery. Free uses a smaller maximum dimension and higher compression; Premium keeps more detail and allows 4K sources. If the result looks soft, upgrade or upload a shorter clip. ## Captions and buttons A video can carry a caption with formatting and inline buttons, exactly like a photo. The caption limit is 1024 characters. ## Animation and video notes GIF-style animations and round video notes are separate content types — see GIFs and Voice Messages. ## Common failures • Too large — over the plan limit; compress or upgrade: Media Limit. • Wrong format — re-export as MP4. • Sends as a file — metadata/dimensions; re-encode. Related: Media Compression & Retention.

Q: Can I upload a 4K video?
A: Premium accepts 4K sources and keeps more detail; Free downsizes. In both cases the file must stay within the plan’s megabyte limit.

## Document Posts
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/schedule_document.html

Anything that is not a photo, video or special media type can be sent as a document: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, ZIP, TXT, APK — Telegram accepts any file type. ## How to schedule one During the media step, send the file as a document (the paperclip → File). The bot counts it like any other media item. Finish with ✅ Done (N) , review, confirm. ## What is different • Documents are not compressed , so the recipient gets the exact bytes. • They show as a file card with the file name and size. • A caption and inline buttons are supported. • Preview is limited — Telegram does not render the contents in the chat. ## Limits The plan's maximum media size applies: 10 MB on Free, 100 MB on Premium. A document over the limit is refused when you send it. ## Good uses Price lists, press kits, menus, templates, event programmes. For things people should read inline, prefer a photo or a PDF with a clear first page — documents require a tap to open. Related: Supported Content Types, Media Modes Explained.

Q: Are documents compressed like photos?
A: No. Documents are delivered byte-for-byte. Compression applies to photos, videos, audio and voice.

## Albums
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/schedule_album.html

An album is several photos or videos published as one grouped post. Telegram allows up to 10 items in a group. ## How to create one 1. Start the scheduling flow. 2. During the media step, send the items together as an album (select several and send in one go). 3. The bot answers "Album received (N item(s)). Now send the date and time" — send the date line. 4. Review the card; the media line shows the album, then confirm. If you send more than ten, the bot warns that a Telegram album can hold at most 10 items and skips the extras. ## Caption The caption rides on the album as a whole, not per photo. Write the text you want under the group; the same limits as a photo caption apply (1024 characters). ## Storage albums In 💾From storage mode, selecting more than one photo/video sends them as one album instead of separate posts. ## Albums vs sequential mode • Album — one post with several files at one time. • Sequential — several posts, each with a different single file. Choose by whether the group belongs together. ## Limitations Albums cannot mix in documents, polls or text-only items. Telegram will reject unsupported combinations, so keep an album to photos and videos. Related: Media Modes Explained, Photo & Video Posts.

Q: Why did my 12 photos become 10?
A: Telegram caps an album at 10 items. The bot skips the extras and tells you; split the rest into a second album or a second post.

Q: Can an album carry different captions per photo?
A: No. Telegram albums have one caption for the whole group. Use sequential mode with one file per post if each item needs its own text.

## Polls
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/schedule_poll.html

Polls are scheduled like other content, but they are created in Telegram first. ## The reliable method 1. Create the poll in any Telegram chat (Saved Messages works). 2. Start scheduling in the sender bot and forward that poll to the bot. 3. Pick the date/time if the bot asks for it, review and confirm. The bot copies the poll's question, options and settings into the scheduled post. At send time it is published as a native Telegram poll in your channel. ## Anonymous only Channels can only host anonymous polls — Telegram does not allow named-voter polls in channels. If you forward a non-anonymous poll, it must be changed before it can be published. ## Quizzes Quizzes are polls with a correct answer and an explanation. They work the same way: create, forward, schedule. See Quiz Polls. ## What does not work • Typing "question + options" into a normal scheduled text — that becomes plain text, not a poll. • Non-anonymous polls in a channel. • Polls created by other bots that cannot be forwarded. ## Related Quiz Polls, Supported Content Types.

Q: Can I create a poll directly in the bot?
A: The supported path is to create the poll in Telegram and forward it during scheduling. A dedicated poll prompt exists, but forwarding is the method that reliably preserves the poll settings.

Q: Why is my poll with named voters rejected?
A: Telegram forbids non-anonymous polls in channels. Recreate it as an anonymous poll and schedule that.

## Forwarding
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/schedule_forward.html

Forwarding is the shortcut for re-posting something that already exists. ## How it works During scheduling, forward a message from any chat to the bot. It copies the text, media, formatting and poll data into the new post; you then choose the date and confirm. ## What is copied • text and caption, including entities (bold, links, spoilers); • one photo, video, animation or document; • poll question, options and settings; • inline buttons are not forwarded by Telegram — recreate them with the &lt;inline&gt; markup. ## What is not copied • the "forwarded from" header — the post is published as your channel's own message; • reactions, views, comments; • Premium/custom emoji. ## Typical uses • Re-running your best post at a better hour. • Reposting an announcement into a second channel (or use Multi-Channel Scheduling). • Scheduling a poll you already built. ## Forward vs copy The bot creates a new post; it does not create a Telegram "forward" with a visible source. That is intentional: your channel should look like the original author. Related: Supported Content Types, Advanced Scheduling.

Q: Can I forward from a channel I do not own?
A: Yes, if Telegram lets you forward the message — protected content cannot be forwarded. You are responsible for having the right to republish it.

## Captions & Formatting
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/schedule_caption.html

When a post has media, the text becomes its caption instead of a separate message. ## Rules • Caption limit: 1024 characters (text-only posts allow 4096). • Formatting is preserved: bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, spoiler, code, links. • Inline buttons work under a caption too. • The caption sits under the media; long captions get collapsed behind "more" on mobile. ## Practical advice • Put the hook in the first line — that is all most readers see before tapping. • Keep captions under ~600 characters for readability. • If you need long text, publish a text post and a media post as two dated blocks. ## Formatting that survives Markdown-style markup and Telegram entities are converted at send time. Custom emoji are stripped. Telegram date formatting and Articles are not rendered — see Supported Content Types. ## Signature interaction If the channel has a signature (Premium), it is appended to the caption. Leave room for it: a 1000-character caption plus a signature can exceed the limit. Related: Formatting & Inline Buttons, Signatures (Premium).

Q: Why was my caption cut?
A: Telegram rejects captions over 1024 characters. The bot validates length; shorten the text or move part of it into the post body.

## Formatting & Inline Buttons
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/formatting.html

The scheduler keeps Telegram formatting and adds one extra layer: inline buttons written as text. ## Text formatting **bold** → bold __italic__ → italic ___underline___ → underline ~~strikethrough~~ → strikethrough ||spoiler|| → hidden until tapped `code` → inline code ```block``` → code block [label](https://example.com) → link Nesting works the way Telegram expects: bold inside a link label, italic inside bold, and so on. Unclosed markup is sent literally, so check the preview. ## Inline buttons There is no button builder in the bot; buttons are typed into the post text, usually at the end. One button &lt;inline&gt;Read more&lt;link="https://example.com"&gt; Several buttons, one per row &lt;inline&gt;Catalog&lt;link="https://shop.com"&gt; &lt;inline&gt;Support&lt;link="https://support.com"&gt; Side by side with -- &lt;inline&gt;Buy&lt;link="https://shop.com"&gt; -- &lt;inline&gt;Info&lt;link="https://info.com"&gt; New row with // &lt;inline&gt;Catalog&lt;link="https://shop.com"&gt; // &lt;inline&gt;Support&lt;link="https://support.com"&gt; Colours Add style="success" (green), style="primary" (blue) or style="danger" (red): &lt;inline&gt;Buy&lt;link="https://shop.com" style="success"&gt; Unknown styles are ignored. ## Rules and validation • Use full URLs with https:// . • Keep labels to a few words so they fit on phones. • Each button tag must have a &lt;link="…"&gt; . • The bot validates the markup before scheduling and refuses to save a post with broken button syntax, so you fix it instead of publishing raw tags. • Markup lines are removed from the published text; buttons appear below it. ## Callback buttons Buttons that trigger bot actions use a &lt;callback="data"&gt; attribute. They only make sense for bots that handle that callback; for channel posts a link button is the safe choice. ## What is not supported Premium/custom emoji, Telegram date formatting, Articles and checklists. Standard emoji and all the markup above are fine. Related: Text Posts, Supported Content Types, Captions & Formatting.

Q: Why were my buttons rejected?
A: The validator found broken syntax — a missing link, an unclosed tag, or a link without https://. Fix the line it points to and schedule again.

Q: Do buttons work in albums?
A: Yes, buttons attach to the album as a whole, like the caption.

## Supported Content Types (Free Plan)
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/content_types.html

## Text • Plain and formatted text (bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, spoiler, code, links). • Inline buttons with the &lt;inline&gt; markup. • Text-only posts with no media. ## Photos • JPEG, PNG and other Telegram-supported image formats. • Single photos with a caption. • Albums of up to 10 photos or videos. • Random mode (one random file per post) and sequential mode (one file per post, in order). ## Videos • Up to up to 25MB per file on Free (up to 50MB on Premium). • MP4, MOV, AVI and other common containers. • With or without a caption. ## Files and audio • Documents of any type: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, ZIP, TXT. • Animations (GIF/MP4). • Voice messages (OGG). • Audio files (MP3 and similar). ## Special types • Polls and quizzes — anonymous only (Polls). • Locations and venues (Location Posts). • Stickers (Stickers). ## Not supported (any plan) • Premium/custom emoji — stripped, text preserved. • Telegram date formatting ( tg://time ). • Rich Articles. • Checklists. • Non-anonymous polls in channels (Telegram rule). ## Premium-only • Videos larger than up to 25MB. • Uploads up to 100 MB. • Video in Media Storage. • More than 1 storage box and 100 stored items. • Signatures, multi-channel targeting, protected backups, advanced statistics. Everything else works on Free — with the Free plan's queue limits: 100 scheduled messages and 1 recurring message. Related: Free Plan Limits, Media Modes Explained.

Q: Can I post a poll on the Free plan?
A: Yes — anonymous polls and quizzes work on every plan. Only non-anonymous polls are impossible in channels, by Telegram’s rule.

Q: Do documents count toward the media size limit?
A: Yes. The plan’s maximum media size applies to each file, including documents.

## Media Modes Explained
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/media_types.html

After the text, the bot asks how media should be attached. The choice changes what each post in the batch looks like, so it is worth understanding before sending files. ## 📷 Normal — the same file on every post You send one file; every post in the batch gets that exact file. Use it for: a logo, a watermark strip, a price card that should appear under every announcement, a consistent visual identity. Example: three posts scheduled for Friday, Saturday and Sunday, each with the same brand banner. Watch out: Normal keeps exactly the single file that belongs to the post. If you need different images across posts, use Random or Sequential instead of sending several files here. ## 🎲 Random — a different file each time You send a set of files; each post gets a random one from the set. Mixed types are allowed: a photo, a video and a document in one set all work, and each is sent with the right method. Use it for: quote channels, meme pages, photo dumps, any feed where repetition looks lazy. Example: 20 quote images and 30 posts — every post gets one, with repeats only when the set is small. Watch out: random means random; you cannot pin a specific image to a specific post in this mode. ## 🔀 Sequential — files in order, one per post Files are assigned in sequence: first file → first post, second → second, and so on. If you have more posts than files, the extra posts are sent as text only — the list does not loop. Use it for: story arcs, tutorials (step 1, step 2, step 3), daily series, numbered tips. Example: ten "day 1 … day 10" images and ten dated posts — they line up exactly. Order choice: the bot asks for 📅 By Date (upload date) or 📤 By Sent Order (the order you send them). Use By Sent Order when the sequence matters and you send them deliberately. ## 💾From storage — reuse saved files Pick files from Media Storage instead of uploading again. Selecting more than one photo or video creates an album post. Use it for: recurring creatives, seasonal banners, the same product shots every week. Storage has its own limits: Storage Boxes. ## ⏭ Skip Photos — text only No media at all. Use it for announcements, text updates and anything that reads better as plain text. ## Albums are a different thing An album is one post with several files (up to 10); the modes above describe how files are attached across several posts. Send the files together as an album when you want a grouped post — see Albums. ## Common mistakes • Sending files before choosing a mode — the bot asks for the mode first; choose it, then send. • Forgetting ✅ Done (N) — without it the batch never leaves the media step. • Expecting Normal mode to cycle through files — it repeats one file. • Using Random while needing exact order — that is Sequential. • Mixing up "album" and "sequential" — one post with many files vs many posts with one file each. ## What happens at send time The scheduler resolves the mode per post: Normal uses the stored file, Random picks from the set, Sequential takes the next index, Storage resolves the stored reference, Skip sends text only. If a file became unavailable, the bot reports the failure for that post instead of silently posting text. Related: Photo & Video Posts, Supported Content Types, Media Limit.

Q: Can I use different modes for different posts in one batch?
A: No. One mode is chosen per scheduling batch; it applies to every post in it. Run the flow again with another mode for a different treatment.

Q: Does Random repeat files?
A: It can. Random picks independently for each post, so a small set will repeat. Sequential cycles in order and is predictable.

Q: What does “By Sent Order” mean in Sequential?
A: The order in which you sent the files to the bot, not their upload date. It is the right choice when you deliberately send step 1, step 2, step 3.

## Review Before Sending
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/schedule_review.html

The review card is the last checkpoint before a post enters the queue. It exists because fixing a typo here costs nothing; fixing it after publishing costs a delete and an apology. ## What the card shows • Channels — every destination, by name. • Time — the exact date and time, in the channel's zone. • Preview — the post as readers will see it, including formatting. • Media — the mode and the number of attached items. • Inline buttons — how many were parsed from the markup. • For a package: how many messages are included. ## Your buttons • ✅ Schedule — commit and queue. • ✏️ Edit — replace the text; the flow also lets you change the time. • 💾 Change media — swap or add files. • 📢 Change channel — send to another channel you own. • 📢 Choose channels — several destinations at once (Premium). • ❌ Cancel — abort without saving. ## Three checks worth doing 1. Time zone. The time is interpreted in the channel's zone. If the channel is set to another country, "10:00" is that country's 10:00. 2. Buttons. If the count is 0 but you wrote markup, the syntax did not parse — go back and fix it. 3. Media. A count of 0 when you expected files means the Done step was missed. ## After confirming The bot returns the job ID and time. The post is now in 📋 Message List and 📅 Calendar , still editable until send time. Related: One-Time Schedule, Edit Messages, Multi-Channel Scheduling.

Q: Can I review a post again later?
A: Yes. Open 📋 Message List, find the post and tap 👁 to preview it. Editing is available there too until it is sent.

## Edit Messages
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/edit.html

A queued post is not frozen. You can change it any time before it is sent. ## Two ways in • 📋 Message List → find the post → ✏️ Edit . • /edit ID — for example /edit s482913_7 . If you do not know the ID, the list shows it; /list opens the list. ## What you can change • Text — send the new version; it replaces the old content. • Date/time — reschedule by sending a new date line. • Media — attach new files or keep the current ones. • Channel — choose a different destination at the end of the flow. The message keeps its ID, so links, notes and habits around that ID keep working. ## Editing a recurring message Changing a recurring rule affects future sends only; already published posts stay as they are. You can change the time, the weekday, the monthly day or the pattern. ## Duplicating instead of editing If you want a second, separate post, use /dub ID . It copies the message and moves the date forward by one day. Editing changes the original; duplicating creates another. ## Limits on edit A new time must be in the future and must respect the channel's scheduled-message cap. If the channel is full, the edit is refused with the same limit message as scheduling. Related: Message List, Delete Messages, Find and Delete Duplicate Posts.

Q: Does editing reset the message ID?
A: No. The same job keeps its ID; only its content, time, media or channel change.

Q: Can I edit a post that was already published?
A: Not from the scheduler. Once sent, it leaves the queue; edit it in Telegram if your admin rights allow it.

## Delete Messages
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/delete.html

Deleting removes a post from the queue so it will never be sent. It is permanent; there is no undo. ## Delete one post 1. Open 📋 Message List (or /list ). 2. Choose Scheduled messages or Recurring messages . 3. Find the post and tap 🗑 . 4. Confirm. ## Delete several by ID /delete opens the delete menu with: • Scheduled messages (N) — pick from the list; • Recurring messages (N) — pick from the list; • 🗑 Delete All — every scheduled and recurring message on the account, after a confirmation that shows the count; • 🗑 Delete by ID — send one ID or several separated by commas, e.g. s482913_7, s482913_12 . Only those entries are removed. ## What deleting does • Scheduled — the job is removed from the queue and will not be sent. • Recurring — the rule is stopped and removed; no future occurrences. • Already sent — nothing. Sent posts are in the channel and are not managed by the queue. • Media storage — unaffected. Deleting a post does not delete stored files; use the storage screens for that. ## Delete All is account-wide It is not scoped to one channel. On a multi-channel account it removes everything, so read the confirmation count before tapping. ## Removing a channel is different Disconnecting a channel pauses its queue but keeps the posts. Deleting posts removes them. Use the right tool: Unlink vs Delete. Related: Find and Delete Duplicate Posts, Message List.

Q: Can I recover a deleted post?
A: No. Deletion is permanent. A backup made before the deletion can restore the data, but only as a restore operation, not an undo button.

Q: Does Delete All remove sent posts from the channel?
A: No. It only clears the queue. Posts already published stay in the channel.

## Find and Delete Duplicate Posts
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/duplicates.html

Duplicates are two or more queue entries with the same content and time. They are rarely a bug — usually one of four things created them. ## Where duplicates come from • Restoring a backup with "Add to existing data". When you send a .fsback file the bot asks for a restore mode. ➕ Add to existing data keeps what is already in the queue and adds the backup's messages next to it, so restoring the same backup twice leaves two of everything. This is the most common cause. • Importing the same text, CSV or JSON file twice. Every imported message becomes a new queue entry with a new ID; the importer does not check whether that post is already there. • /dub ID . The duplicate command copies a post and schedules it one day later; run it twice and you have two copies. • Sending the scheduling text twice. If the bot was waiting for a date and you resend a block, both can be accepted. • Reconnecting a channel. Reconnecting normally resumes the existing queue; importing or restoring data on top of it can double entries. ## How to spot them Open 📋 Message List → Scheduled messages . Entries are listed with their ID and time. Duplicates share text and often differ only by ID or by a minute. The 📅 Calendar shows them stacked on the same day. For a text match, use 🔍 Search : send a distinctive phrase from the post. Results show every message that contains it, including duplicates. See Searching Messages. ## Delete the copies, keep the original 1. Note the IDs of the entries you want to remove. The original is usually the one with the earliest created/scheduled ID — keep that one. 2. Open /delete → 🗑 Delete by ID . 3. Send the IDs separated by commas, exactly as they appear in the list, e.g. s482913_9, s482913_12 . 4. The bot confirms each deletion. Only the entries you listed are removed. You can also delete one at a time from the list with 🗑 . ## Prevent them • When restoring a backup, choose 🔄 Overwrite existing data unless you deliberately want the two sets side by side. • Do not re-import the same backup after restoring it. • Check the queue after reconnecting a channel. • Use /dub once, then edit the copy instead of duplicating again. ## If both copies already sent Deleting the queue entry does nothing — the posts are in the channel. Delete the unwanted message in Telegram (you or the sender bot need Delete Messages permission there). Related: Delete Messages, Importing Your Data, Message List.

Q: Why did importing create duplicates?
A: The import offered “Add all (keep duplicates)” and that option was chosen. Re-import with “Overwrite existing”, or delete the extra copies by ID.

Q: Does /dub create a duplicate at the same time?
A: No. It creates a copy scheduled one day after the original, so both can publish. Delete the copy if you only wanted a template.

Q: Can I delete all duplicates at once?
A: Not selectively — Delete All clears everything. Delete by ID is the safe way to remove only the copies.

## Recurring Messages
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/recurring.html

A recurring message publishes the same content on a repeating pattern. Write it once; the bot keeps sending it. ## Create one 1. In the sender bot, tap 🔄 Recurring Messages (or /recurring ). 2. Send the message text (and optional inline buttons). 3. Choose the pattern: 📅 Daily , 📅 Weekly , 📅 Monthly or a custom cron rule. 4. Set the time: 09:00 for daily, Monday 09:00 for weekly, 15 09:00 for monthly. 5. Choose the start date — From today , From tomorrow , or a date. 6. Optionally add a signature (Premium). 7. Review and confirm. ## Patterns in practice • Daily — a quote, a digest, a daily tip. • Weekly — a Monday roundup or Friday recap. • Monthly — a report on the 1st or 15th. • Custom cron — anything else, expressed as a cron expression. ## Limits and lifetime Free: 1 recurring message. Premium: unlimited. A recurring rule expires after 365 days ; recreate or extend it before then if the series should continue. ## Managing it Recurring entries live in 📋 Message List → Recurring messages . You can preview, edit, pause, resume or delete. Pausing stops sends without losing the rule: Pause & Resume. ## What it counts against Each recurring rule counts toward the channel's scheduled-message accounting and the plan's recurring limit. Duplicating with /dub also counts as a new rule. Related: How You Can Use Recurring Messages, Recurring Limit.

Q: Can I run different content every day with one recurring rule?
A: No — a recurring rule repeats the same content. For a different post each day, schedule individual posts (or import a batch from SetDate).

Q: What happens when a recurring rule expires?
A: It stops producing new sends after 365 days. The rule stays visible in the list; recreate or replace it to continue the series.

## How You Can Use Recurring Messages
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/recurring_uses.html

## Daily digest Pattern: Daily at 09:00 . Content: a short roundup with a link. Keep it under 600 characters so it fits on one screen. ## Event reminders Pattern: Daily or a one-time series. Build three posts — a week before, a day before, an hour before — each with an "Add to calendar" link button. Recurring is useful for the weekly version of the event. ## Weekly roundup Pattern: Weekly on Monday 10:00 . Content: last week's best posts, a link to the archive, one call to action. ## Evergreen promo Pattern: Weekly on Friday 18:00 . Content: the offer with a style="success" button. Rotate the creative in Media Storage rather than editing the text every week. ## Daily quote or tip Pattern: Daily at 08:00 . Attach a random image set in Random mode so the visual varies while the text stays stable. ## Monthly report Pattern: Monthly on 1 10:00 . Content: the previous month's numbers with a link to the full stats. ## Rules that keep recurring content healthy • Review the text every few weeks; stale evergreen content reads worse than no post. • Pause during holidays instead of deleting — Pause & Resume. • Keep one recurring slot for the essential (a daily digest) so a bad week still publishes something. • Check the expiry date if the series must run longer than 365 days. Related: Recurring Messages, Recurring Tips.

Q: How many recurring messages should a channel run?
A: Two or three slots are usually enough: one essential daily post and one or two weekly features. More than that and the channel feels automated.

## Pause & Resume
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/recurring_pause_resume.html

Pausing is the middle ground between "keep posting" and "delete the rule". The message stops sending, but nothing is lost. ## Pause 1. Open 📋 Message List . 2. Choose Recurring messages . 3. Find the rule and tap the ⏸ button. 4. Confirm. The rule is marked paused and produces no new sends. ## Resume 1. Same list, same rule. 2. Tap ▶ . 3. The next send happens at the next matching time — not immediately. ## What pause does not do • It does not delete the rule, its content, media or buttons. • It does not change the schedule pattern. • It does not affect posts already published. ## When to pause instead of delete • Seasonal content (holiday posts out of season). • A vacation or a quiet period. • Testing a new creative before committing. • A temporary clash with another campaign. Deleting is the right choice when you will never reuse the rule; pausing is right when you will. ## If resume does nothing • The rule may have expired (365 days) — recreate it. • The channel may have lost its sender bot — reconnect before resuming. • The plan's recurring limit may have changed — check Recurring Limit. Related: Recurring Messages, Message List.

Q: Does resuming send the missed posts?
A: No. Paused occurrences are skipped, not queued. The next send is the next scheduled time after resuming.

## Multi-Channel Scheduling
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/multichannel.html

Premium allows up to 3 channels. Multi-channel scheduling lets one post land in several of them without rebuilding it. ## Send to several channels 1. Build the post as usual. 2. On the review card tap 📢 Choose channels . 3. Tick every destination. On the Free plan selecting a second channel replaces the first, so the target is always exactly one. 4. Confirm and tap ✅ Schedule . Each copy is delivered by that channel's own sender bot , so it appears from the right name and avatar — never from the channel you happened to schedule in. ## Time zones and signatures Each channel keeps its own time zone and signature. A "10:00" post arrives at 10:00 local time in each destination, signed the way that channel is configured. The calendar shows every copy under its channel. ## Add a channel mid-flow If a destination is missing, tap ➕ Add New Channel in the picker.
