You are taken to the main bot to authorise the channel; once connected it appears in the picker without losing the draft. ## Limits and failures • The plan's channel cap applies; the add action is limit-checked. • A channel at its scheduled-message cap is skipped with a warning, and the other copies still go out. • A channel without a working sender bot cannot receive the copy — reconnect it first. ## Duplicate and edit The same multi-channel targeting is available when duplicating or editing a post, which is useful for seeding a new channel from a template or correcting a message everywhere it was published. Related: Premium Features, How Posting Works: Sender Bots, Channel Limit.

Q: Does multi-channel work on the Free plan?
A: No. Free targets one channel at a time. Premium unlocks selecting several destinations up to the channel limit.

Q: Which bot posts the copy in each channel?
A: That channel’s own sender bot, always. This keeps each channel’s author identity intact.

## Advanced Scheduling: Edit, Delete, Polls & More
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/schedule_advanced.html

Beyond "date + text + confirm", the scheduler handles a set of practical cases. ## Editing and deleting A queued post stays editable until send time: open 📋 Message List → the post → ✏️ Edit , or use /edit ID . Delete from the same list or with /delete . Details: Edit Messages, Delete Messages. ## Batches from a text file Upload a .txt with the same blank-line rule as typed blocks: a date line, the post, a blank line, the next date line. The bot parses the whole file at once. This is the fastest way to queue a month without a companion bot. ## Anything forwardable Forward a message from any chat and the bot copies its text, media and poll into your post. Polls and quizzes must be anonymous to publish in a channel. See Forwarding and Polls. ## Special content • Locations and venues — Location Posts. • Voice messages — Voice Messages. • GIFs / animations — GIFs. • Stickers — Stickers. • Albums — Albums. ## Time zones Every date is interpreted in the channel's time zone. A channel for another country should have its own zone so "19:00" means local evening. Set it on the channel card or with /timezone . ## Bulk creation with SetDate For large calendars, the companion bot @SetDate_bot builds a dated schedule from a list and imports it in one click: SetDate Integration. ## What the scheduler will refuse • Past dates. • Broken inline-button markup. • Messages over the plan's queue limit or the channel's cap. • Media over the plan's size limit. • Non-anonymous polls. Each refusal explains the reason and leaves the flow open where possible, so you can correct and retry.

Q: Can I schedule a month of posts at once?
A: Yes — send many dated blocks separated by blank lines, upload a .txt with the same structure, or generate the schedule in SetDate and import it.

## Edit Scheduled
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/schedule_edit.html

Editing changes the existing job rather than creating a new one. Open 📋 Message List → the post → ✏️ Edit , or send /edit ID . The bot asks for the new version: text, a new date line, or both. Media can be kept or replaced. The preview is shown again before saving. The job keeps its ID. If the new time exceeds the channel's scheduled cap, the edit is refused with the limit message. Recurring rules can be edited too; changes apply to future sends. Related: Edit Messages, Message List.

## Delete Scheduled
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/schedule_delete.html

Deleting removes a job from the queue so it never publishes. From the list: 🗑 → confirm. From the menu: /delete → Scheduled messages , Recurring messages , 🗑 Delete All , or 🗑 Delete by ID with one or more IDs separated by commas. Delete All is account-wide and asks for confirmation with the exact count. Deletion is permanent; already published posts are not affected. Related: Delete Messages, Find and Delete Duplicate Posts.

## Location Posts
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/schedule_location.html

A location post publishes a map pin in the channel. It is useful for events, shops, meetups and offices. During scheduling, send the location from Telegram's attachment menu (Location). The bot accepts it as the post's content or as media alongside a caption. Choose the date and confirm; at send time the pin appears as a native Telegram location. Venues include a name and address; plain locations show only coordinates. For a venue, pick an existing place in Telegram rather than dropping a raw pin. Limits: the location counts as the post's media, so it cannot be combined with a photo or video in the same post. It can carry a caption and buttons. Related: Supported Content Types, Advanced Scheduling.

## Quiz Polls
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/schedule_poll_quiz.html

A quiz is a poll with one correct option, an optional explanation and a hint that appears after answering. Create it in any Telegram chat: attach → Poll → enable Quiz mode , mark the correct answer, add an explanation. Then forward it to the sender bot during scheduling and pick the date. Telegram requires channel polls to be anonymous; quizzes follow the same rule. The correct answer is revealed after a vote, not before. Quizzes are a strong engagement format because they give readers a reason to tap. Keep options short (they truncate on phones) and explanations under two sentences. Related: Polls, Forwarding.

## Voice Messages
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/schedule_voice.html

Voice messages (the round, recorded kind) and audio tracks (music files) are both supported. Record or forward the voice message to the bot during scheduling, or send an MP3/OGG as audio. A voice message has no caption in Telegram; if you need text, schedule a second text post next to it. Audio and voice are compressed for delivery. Free compresses harder; Premium keeps more bitrate. Very long recordings can exceed the plan's media size limit. Voice is personal and hard to skim — use it for short announcements, not for information people need to search later. Related: Supported Content Types, GIFs.

## GIFs
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/schedule_animation.html

Animations (GIFs) play automatically and loop without sound. Telegram converts uploaded GIFs to MP4 internally, so quality and size matter. Send the GIF to the bot during scheduling; it is stored as an animation and published as one. A caption and inline buttons are supported. Because Telegram re-encodes GIFs, colours may shift slightly. For precise visuals, send an MP4 as a video instead. Size limits follow the plan's media cap. A long, high-resolution GIF can exceed it quickly — keep loops short. Related: Video Posts, Supported Content Types.

## Stickers
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/schedule_sticker.html

Stickers can be scheduled like any other content. Send the sticker to the bot during scheduling; it is published as a native sticker. Stickers have no caption field in Telegram. If you want text with a sticker, the bot publishes the sticker and then the text as a separate message so the meaning is not lost. Animated and video stickers work. Premium/custom emoji inside text do not — they are stripped. Stickers are best for reactions and tone, not for announcements: they are small, silent and easy to miss in a busy feed. Related: Supported Content Types, GIFs.

## Scheduling Time Zone
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/schedule_timezone.html

Every scheduled date is interpreted in the channel's time zone, not your phone's and not UTC by default. ## What that means If the channel is set to Europe/Berlin and you schedule 19:00 , the post publishes at 19:00 Berlin time — whatever zone you are in when you type it. ## Where to check it • Channel card: 📢 Channels → the channel → 🕐 Time Zone: … . • Account default: ⚙️ Settings → 🕐 Time Zone (or /timezone ). A channel without its own setting inherits the account zone. ## How to change it Open the channel card and tap the time zone button, then pick the zone from the grid. Changes apply to new schedules; existing queued posts keep the moment they were created for, so review them in the calendar. ## Wrong-hour checklist 1. Open the channel card and read the zone. 2. Compare it with the time you intended. 3. Check the queued post's time in 📅 Calendar . 4. If needed, edit the post's time or change the channel zone and reschedule. A post that arrives an hour off is almost always a daylight-saving or wrong-zone issue, not a scheduler bug. Related: Set Time Zone, Why Was My Scheduled Post Published at the Wrong Time?.

## Date & Time Formats
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/dates.html

The bot accepts dates and times in the message you send, in a flexible set of formats. Everything is read in the selected time zone — see Scheduling Time Zone. ## Dates • 25.12.2026 , 25/12/2026 , 25-12-2026 — day first. • 25.12.26 — a two-digit year becomes 2026. • today , tomorrow , day after tomorrow — also understood in Russian. If the first number is above 12 it is always the day; otherwise the bot reads day-first, so 05.06.2026 is 5 June. ## Times • 19:00 — 24-hour. • 7:30 PM , 7:30pm — 12-hour with AM/PM. • A time without AM/PM in the morning range is read sensibly: if 10:05 has already passed this morning but 22:05 has not, it means 22:05. ## Missing parts • A date with no time — the bot asks for the time. • A time with no date — today (or tomorrow if that time already passed, depending on the flow's prompt). ## Several posts at once You can send several date lines in one message; the bot creates one post per date and asks which content goes with each. That is the fast way to fill a week without repeating the flow. ## Formatting the text The content and the date can arrive in either order during scheduling; the bot recognizes the date line and keeps the rest as content. Inline buttons and polls are handled separately — Formatting & Inline Buttons. ## If a date is rejected • A past date cannot be scheduled — the bot asks for a future one. • An impossible date such as 31.02 fails. • A date outside the supported range (far future) may be refused by the queue limits. Related: One-Time Schedule, CSV Import.

## Adding Photos & Videos
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/add_photo.html

Media can be attached at two points in the scheduling flow, and the bot holds it until the post is complete. ## Send it with the content Send the photo or video together with (or instead of) the text. If you add a caption in Telegram, that caption becomes the post text. ## Send it before the date Send the media first, then the date and time. The file stays pending and is attached when the post is created. This is the normal way to schedule a picture-only post. ## Send it after the date If you already sent the date, the bot still accepts media as the next message and attaches it to the pending post. ## Albums Send several photos or videos as one Telegram album and they are scheduled as a media group, with the caption from the album. Up to ten items per album — see Albums. ## From storage Instead of uploading again, choose From Storage at the media step and pick a saved item — Using From Storage. ## What happens to the file Photos and video are compressed on upload to your plan's limits — Media Compression &amp; Retention. Documents and stickers are stored as-is. ## Limits • Size and format limits depend on the plan — Media Limit. • Captions have a smaller character limit than text posts — Captions &amp; Formatting. If an upload is refused, the reason is shown immediately; a retry with the same file will fail the same way.

## Can I Edit a Scheduled Post After Scheduling It?
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_edit_scheduled_post.html

Nothing about a scheduled post is carved in stone. Until the moment Telegram accepts the send, every part of it can change — that is the whole point of keeping a queue instead of posting immediately. What you can change Text and formatting — fix a typo, rewrite the hook, add links. Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, spoilers and code all survive edits. Media — swap the image, replace the video, add or remove an album item. Send time — move the post earlier or later, or to another day entirely. Target channel — re-point a post to a different connected channel. Open the Message List (or /list ), tap the post, choose 🔄 Replace . The familiar schedule flow reopens with the post's current content pre-filled — change what you need and confirm. What editing cannot do Change a post that already published. Once the sender bot delivers the message to Telegram, it is a normal Telegram message — edit it with Telegram's own tools, not here. Edit recurring posts “in place”. A recurring rule is a single template that fires on its pattern — there are no separate per-day copies. Edit the rule so all future sends change. A workflow that actually works Channel operators who stay sane usually: schedule the week on Sunday, review the Calendar Monday, and treat edit as the normal verb — improving copy as the news moves. Edits are free, instant, and never notify subscribers. The only deadline is the send time itself.

Q: How late can I edit a post?
A: Any time before the send moment. If the bot is mid-delivery, the edit may not apply — that is the only race. For a post due within seconds, delete and reschedule instead.

Q: Can I edit a post that already went out?
A: Not from the bot — it is a regular Telegram message now. Telegram itself lets admins edit posted messages in channels; use Telegram for that.

Q: Does editing reset the monthly send counter?
A: No. The counter counts actual sends, not edits. Editing costs nothing.

## Schedule Many Telegram Posts at Once (Batch Format)
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_schedule_many_at_once.html

You do not have to schedule posts one at a time. Send Fast Scheduler a single message that contains several blocks: every block becomes its own scheduled post. A block is a date and time on the first line , then the post text on the lines below. One blank line separates one block from the next. The same text works as a .txt upload when the batch is longer than one Telegram message. Copy-paste example: five posts in one message today 10:23 Morning news digest: three stories worth your time &lt;inline&gt;Read more&lt;link="https://example.com/news"&gt; tomorrow 7:24 PM Poll day — which topic should we cover next? &lt;inline&gt;Vote&lt;link="https://t.me/yourchannel/12"&gt; 12.12.2026 18:28 New drop is live. Limited stock, 24 hours only. &lt;inline&gt;Shop now&lt;link="https://example.com/shop" style="success"&gt; -- &lt;inline&gt;Details&lt;link="https://example.com/faq"&gt; 23-10-2027 15:34 Reminder: the community call starts in 30 minutes. 14/04/2027 4:05 PM Weekend recap: the five most-read posts this week. &lt;inline&gt;Open the channel&lt;link="https://t.me/yourchannel"&gt; Every block follows the same rule: first line = when , everything after it = what . The blank lines are what split the message into five separate posts, and you can send batches like this as often as you like. Accepted date and time formats Relative — today 10:23 , tomorrow 7:24 PM , day after tomorrow 09:00 . Full date — 12.12.2026 18:28 , 12/12/2026 18:28 , 12-12-2026 18:28 , or ISO 2026-12-12 18:28 . A two-digit year works too ( 12.12.26 18:28 ). Time only — 18:28 schedules the next time that clock shows 18:28: today if it is still ahead of you, otherwise tomorrow. 12-hour clock — add AM or PM to any of the above, e.g. 4:05 PM . A bare hour that already passed today is read as PM when that reading is still ahead. Separators — dots, slashes and dashes are interchangeable; hours and minutes may be separated by : or . . Seconds are not accepted. When both numbers in a date could be a month, Fast Scheduler reads them as day.month (European order). A number above 12 settles it either way: 14/04/2027 and 04/14/2027 are both 14 April 2027. Multi-line posts and inline buttons Every line after the date belongs to the post, and line breaks are preserved. Do not leave a blank line inside a post: a blank line is the separator between two posts. Inline buttons are written inside the post they belong to: &lt;inline&gt;Button Text&lt;link="https://example.com"&gt; — a URL button. &lt;inline&gt;Action&lt;callback="confirm_action"&gt; — a callback button handled by the bot. -- between two buttons puts them on the same row; // starts a new row. A button on its own line also starts a new row. style="success" (or primary , danger ) colours the button; without it the default style is used. Long batches: send it as a file A Telegram message is capped at 4,096 characters, so a month of posts will not fit in the chat box. Put the exact same text in a .txt file (UTF-8 encoding, one blank line between posts) and attach it while scheduling. Fast Scheduler parses the file with the same rules, previews every post, and queues them together. .md files are accepted too, and /import takes .txt , .md , .rtf and .odt . Limits and validation Both plans accept batches. The ceiling is the pending queue: 100 scheduled messages on Free, unlimited on Premium. If a batch would go over it, nothing is scheduled and the bot tells you how many slots remain. Each individual post must still fit Telegram: 4,096 characters of text, or 1,024 for a media caption. Blocks without a readable date/time are reported with their first line; readable blocks in the same batch are still scheduled, so check the warning list. Malformed &lt;inline&gt; markup, or a callback the bot does not recognise, stops the batch with an explanation instead of publishing raw markup. After scheduling, open Message List or Calendar to review the batch — every post can still be edited or deleted before it goes out.

Q: Can I schedule several posts in one message on the Free plan?
A: Yes. Batch messages and .txt uploads work on Free and Premium alike; the only difference is the pending queue (100 on Free, unlimited on Premium).

Q: Can one post in a batch contain a blank line?
A: No. A blank line separates two posts, so it ends the current one. Use single line breaks inside a post and keep blank lines strictly between posts.

Q: What happens if one block in the batch has a wrong date?
A: That block is reported by its first line while the readable blocks in the same batch are still scheduled. Fix the line and resend just that block.

Q: Can a batch message be longer than one Telegram message?
A: The chat message itself cannot exceed 4,096 characters. For longer batches, save the same text as a UTF-8 .txt file and upload it during scheduling.

## How to Automate Recurring Posts in Telegram (Daily Digests, Weekly Roundups)
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_recurring_guide.html

Anything your channel repeats should never be scheduled by hand twice. Recurring rules encode the pattern once — “daily at 9:00”, “every Monday 18:30”, “every 6 hours” — and the bot keeps generating posts on time, forever (or until the rule expires). Creating a rule 1. Tap 🔄 Recurring Messages in the bot (or send /recurring ) and follow the flow. 2. Compose the message — text, media, the works — exactly like a normal post. 3. Pick the pattern: daily, weekly (with weekday picker), or custom interval. 4. Set the time in the channel's time zone and confirm. The rule's future posts expand in the Calendar like any others, and the rule itself is listed with your recurring messages — so there is always a truthful picture of what will publish. Expiry — the part people forget On Free , the single recurring rule runs for 365 days , then expires with a notice — create a new rule to continue. It is the anti-zombie mechanism: dead rules can't silently post forever. Premium rules never expire, and you can run unlimited rules — one per content type is the usual pattern. Patterns that work in real channels Daily digest — a template message (“Top 3 of the day”) with the signature carrying credit; edit the rule weekly, not daily. Weekly roundup — Monday 9:00 rule; combine with the calendar to dodge holidays. Scheduled reminders — every-6-hours service posts for community managers; Premium's unlimited rules shine here. Editing and stopping Rules are editable — change text, time, or pattern, and future instances follow. Pause or delete when a campaign ends. Deleting a rule never deletes already-posted messages.

Q: Why did my recurring rule stop working?
A: On Free, rules expire after 365 days and you get an expiry notice — create a new rule to continue. Premium rules never expire. Also check the sender bot is still admin — a failed delivery stops the chain.

Q: Can two rules post at the same time?
A: Yes, and they will — in the order created. If they are too close together, Telegram may throttle the burst; space rules by a few minutes.

## What Types of Content Can You Schedule With Fast Scheduler?
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_media_types.html

A scheduling bot is only as good as the content it can carry. Fast Scheduler handles the full Telegram media palette, so your editorial plans never have to shrink to fit the tool. Everything you can attach to a scheduled post Photos — compressed automatically for fast delivery without visible quality loss. Videos — including size limits that scale with your plan (up to 25MB on Free, up to 50MB on Premium). Video notes (round videos) and voice messages . Audio files — full tracks with cover art preserved. Documents — PDFs, archives, anything Telegram accepts. Animations — GIFs and MP4 loops. Stickers — from any of your packs. Polls and quizzes — scheduled like any other post. Locations and venues — supported for per-post content. Albums and media groups Multiple photos or videos sent together are scheduled as one album and publish as a single media group — exactly how your followers expect it. You can also build a randomized pool : attach a mix of photos, videos, documents or any files and let the scheduler pick one per send, which is perfect for daily wallpaper or quote channels where variety matters. Text always travels with media Captions keep their formatting (bold, italic, links, spoilers) and your configured signature is appended to media posts as well. Inline URL buttons attach to media posts too, so a &ldquo;Read more&rdquo; button under a photo works out of the box. Limits that matter Max media size: up to 10 MB on Free, 100 MB on Premium. Videos: up to 25MB on Free, up to 50MB on Premium. Media Storage boxes: 1 box with 100 items total on Free — Premium raises this to 20 boxes with 500 items total across the account, so reusable assets live in the bot instead of your camera roll. Anything Telegram itself refuses (for example, a corrupted file) is rejected at scheduling time with a clear message — never discovered silently on the day of publishing.

Q: Can I schedule Telegram polls with Fast Scheduler?
A: Yes. Polls and quizzes are scheduled like any other message and publish through your sender bot at the set time.

Q: Can I schedule an album of photos?
A: Yes. Photos and videos sent together are scheduled as one media group. You can also attach a pool of mixed files and let the scheduler pick one randomly per send.

Q: What is the maximum video size for scheduled messages?
A: Videos up to 25MB on the Free plan and up to 50MB with Premium, in line with Telegram bots own upload limits.

## How Do I Format Telegram Posts? (Bold, Italic, Links, Spoilers and Buttons)
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_formatting.html

Formatting is what separates a channel that looks professional from one that looks like a group chat. Fast Scheduler keeps every bit of it intact between scheduling and publishing. Rich text survives the whole pipeline Write a message anywhere — bold headlines, italic asides, underlined warnings, struck-through corrections, monospace code — and schedule it. Formatting is stored as Telegram entities , not flat text, so what publishes is pixel-identical to what you wrote: no mangled asterisks, no lost links, no broken emoji. Spoilers Wrap part of the text in spoiler markup and it publishes as a real Telegram spoiler — blurred until a reader taps it. Perfect for giveaways, answers, and sensitive details. The bot validates spoiler markup while you type, so unclosed pairs are caught at scheduling time, not in front of your audience. Inline URL buttons Add tappable buttons to any post with one syntax: [Button Text](https://example.com) . Use them for call-to-action links — &ldquo;Read the guide&rdquo;, &ldquo;Buy now&rdquo;, &ldquo;Join the chat&rdquo;. Buttons attach to text posts and to media posts alike. Keep button labels short (two or three words read best) and test one post before scheduling a whole campaign. Custom emoji Premium Telegram emoji in your drafts are preserved on publish, so your brand&rsquo;s custom smileys do not degrade into defaults. Signatures: formatting that stamps itself Configure a signature once — a footer with your links, hashtags or contact — and every scheduled post carries it automatically, on text and media alike. Signatures keep their own formatting, and you can override the signature per post when a particular message should go out clean. A checklist for polished posts One bold hook line first — most readers see only it in notifications. Links as buttons where possible; they out-click inline links. Spoilers for anything the reader should opt into. A signature so every post quietly advertises your next channel.

Q: Does Telegram formatting survive scheduling in Fast Scheduler?
A: Yes. Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, code, links, spoilers and custom emoji are stored as Telegram entities and publish exactly as written.

Q: How do I add buttons to a scheduled Telegram post?
A: Use the syntax [Button Text](https://your-link.com) in the message. The bot converts it into a tappable inline URL button on the published post.

Q: Can every scheduled post have an automatic signature?
A: Yes. Create a signature once and it is appended to every scheduled and recurring post automatically, keeping its own formatting. Individual posts can override it.

# Channels

## Channels
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/channels.html

A channel is the destination. Everything else in Fast Scheduler exists to publish into it reliably. ## What a connected channel means Three conditions are true: you are an administrator, @FastSchedulerBot is an administrator with Post Messages , and the channel is linked to your account. Then it appears in 📢 Channels with its own time zone and sender bot. ## Channel vs sender bot The channel is where readers are; the sender bot is the author that publishes there. One sender bot per channel. Fast Scheduler connects the two, which is why both must be configured before scheduling works. ## What you can configure per channel • Time zone — what "19:00" means for this channel. • Sender bot — the bot that publishes. • Signature — an optional footer (Premium). • Admins — co-managers with limited rights (inside the sender bot). • Queue — scheduled and recurring messages, visible in the list and calendar. ## Limits Free: 1 channel. Premium: up to 3 . Each extra channel needs its own sender bot. ## Start here • Add a Channel — the connection procedure. • Channel Permissions — what to grant. • Manage Channels — the list and the channel card. • How Posting Works: Sender Bots — who publishes and why. • Remove a Channel and Unlink vs Delete — removal without data loss. @FastSchedulerBot and every sender bot share one rule: they must remain administrators. Removing them from the channel stops delivery until they are re-added.

Q: Can the bot post to a channel without being an admin?
A: No. Telegram requires posting rights for any bot that publishes to a channel. Grant at least Post Messages.

Q: Do I need a different bot for every channel?
A: Yes. One sender bot serves exactly one channel; a second channel needs a second bot.

## Add a Channel
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/channel_add.html

## Before you start You must be an administrator of the channel, and the sender bot that will serve it must be an administrator there with Post Messages . The main bot does not need any rights in the channel. ## Connect it 1. Open 📢 Channels → 📢 Connect Channel . The bot lists your idle sender bots — pick one and it opens with the connect flow already running. You can also use ➕ Add New Channel inside a scheduling channel picker. 2. Send the channel identity: @yourchannel , a https://t.me/… link, an invite link, a forwarded post, or the numeric ID -100… . 3. The bot verifies admin rights and adds the channel to your list. ## After connecting If you picked a sender bot, the channel is linked to it and the time zone is the last step. If you connected the channel without a bot (the escape hatch), scheduling stays locked until you attach one — every channel needs its own sender bot. ## Limits Free: 1 channel; Premium: up to 3. Adding past the limit shows an upgrade prompt. ## If it fails • Bot is not an admin — tap the green ➕ Add bot to a channel button inside the sender bot, or promote it by hand with Post Messages . • Channel not found — wrong username or a private channel; forward a post. • Invalid format — send the link alone. • Already connected — open it from the list instead of adding it twice. Related: Connecting a Channel, Channel Permissions.

Q: Can I add a channel from a different account?
A: The channel is linked to the account that connects it. Other people can be added as channel admins inside the sender bot, with permissions you choose.

## Connect the Bot
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/channel_connect.html

Only one bot does the work: your sender bot . ## Your sender bot (required) Needs to be an administrator with Post Messages to actually publish. This check is separate because Telegram reports rights per bot. ## Recommended extra rights • Edit Messages — lets the bot correct a post it published. • Delete Messages — lets it remove a post when you delete from the queue before sending or clean up. ## Verify After granting rights, return to the bot and press 🔄 Check Again where it waits. The check is live, so no restart is needed. If a channel loses the bot's admin rights later, delivery fails and the bot reports it. Restore the permission and the queue continues. Related: Channel Permissions, Bot Permissions.

## Manage Channels
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/channel_manage.html

Everything about a channel is split between the 📢 Channels list and that channel's card. ## The list 📢 Channels (N) shows every connected channel with its time zone and sender bot. From here you add channels and open a channel's card. ## The channel card Tap a channel to see its role, sender bot, time zone, and how many scheduled and recurring messages it holds. Buttons: • 🕐 Time Zone: … — set this channel's own zone. • 👥 Admins — owner only, in the sender bot. • 🔄 Change Channel — move the sender bot to another channel you own. • 🔗 Disconnect Channel — unlink the channel; queued posts are preserved. ## Change Channel vs Disconnect • Change Channel moves the bot; the old channel loses its publisher and the new one gains it. • Disconnect removes the channel entirely from the account. Posts stay stored and can reattach after reconnecting. ## Managed vs free channels In action pickers a channel with a sender bot appears as 🤖 Managed: … . Tapping it explains that the channel is managed by its bot and offers 🤖 Open Sender Bot . A channel without a bot appears as 🆓 Free: … and opens the action directly. ## Multi-channel Each channel is configured independently: time zone, bot, signature, admins, queue and stats. Use the picker before scheduling to choose the destination. Related: Add a Channel, Remove a Channel, Multi-Channel Scheduling.

Q: Why does the main bot refuse to schedule for a managed channel?
A: Because that channel’s scheduling lives in its sender bot. The “managed” screen offers a button to open it — this keeps each channel’s data isolated.

## Channel Permissions
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/channel_permissions.html

Only your sender bot needs ordinary administrator rights in the channel; the main bot needs none. Fast Scheduler never asks for your Telegram password or a login code. ## Required Post Messages — publish posts. Without it every send fails with a "bot is not admin" style error, and the bot refuses to unlock scheduling. ## Recommended • Edit Messages — correct a published post. • Delete Messages — remove a post when needed. ## How to grant them Channel → Channel Info → Administrators → Add Administrator → choose @FastSchedulerBot or your sender bot → enable the rights → save. Do this for both bots where relevant. ## After changing rights Press 🔄 Check Again if the bot is waiting for verification. Rights are read live from Telegram, so no restart is needed. ## What the bot cannot do It cannot read private messages, post as you personally, or bypass Telegram's channel rules (for example, non-anonymous polls in channels). It also cannot keep posting after you remove it from the admin list. ## Common errors • "Bot is not an admin" — the bot is in the channel but not an administrator, or the permission is off. • "Not enough rights to send" — Post Messages is missing. • Silent failure after a Telegram update — re-check the admin list; Telegram sometimes drops rights when a channel changes ownership. Related: Connect the Bot, Permission.

## How Posting Works: Sender Bots
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/channel_posting.html

Every post is delivered by a sender bot — the bot you created for that channel. This is a hard requirement, not a cosmetic option. ## Why Telegram requires a bot with Post Messages rights in the channel it publishes to. Fast Scheduler could post from one shared bot, but then every channel would share one author identity, one rate limit and one failure domain. A per-channel bot fixes all three. ## What readers see Posts appear from your bot's name and avatar. The channel looks like it is run by your brand, not by a scheduling service. Inline buttons, polls and media all come from that bot. ## One bot, one channel A sender bot serves exactly one channel. For a second channel, create a second bot. Free allows 1; Premium 3. ## Where management lives When a channel gets its bot, its scheduling, message list, statistics, calendar and channel settings move inside that bot. The main bot keeps account-level actions. A channel shown as 🤖 Managed is not broken — it is isolated on purpose. ## Public Mode In Channel Settings → 🔒 Hide channel from strangers , the bot stops showing your channel name to strangers who start it. They see a generic welcome and an Open Main Bot button. Toggle it back with 🔓 Show channel to strangers . ## If the token breaks If a sender bot's token becomes invalid, Fast Scheduler falls back to the main bot where it can so a post is not lost, and warns you. Restore the token with ⚙ Manage → 🔑 Change token . ## What happens if you remove the bot from the channel Delivery fails for that channel until the bot is re-added as an administrator. The queue is preserved; it resumes when rights return. Related: Connecting a Bot, Manage Sender Bots, Channel Permissions.

Q: Can I post as the main bot instead?
A: Scheduling requires a sender bot for every channel. The main bot is the account hub, not the publisher.

Q: Do subscribers see the scheduling bot anywhere?
A: No. The post is published by your sender bot. With Hide channel enabled, even people who open the bot do not see the channel name.

## Permanent Link
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/channel_link.html

A channel link is both an address for readers and a way to identify the channel to the bot. ## Public channels The permanent link is t.me/yourchannel . It never expires and can be shared anywhere. Send it to the bot to connect the channel. ## Private channels There is no public link. Use one of these instead: • forward any post from the channel to the bot while it waits; • send an invite link ( t.me/+… ); • send the numeric channel ID, e.g. -1001234567890 . ## Which to use when connecting Forwarding is the most reliable for private channels; a username is fastest for public ones. Invite links work but may expire if they were created with a limit. ## Editing the link The username is managed in Telegram (Channel Info → Edit → Channel Link). Changing it does not disconnect the channel from Fast Scheduler, but any old link stops working. ## If the link is taken Telegram usernames are global. Choose another; the channel itself is unaffected. Related: Connecting a Channel, Add a Channel.

## Unlink vs Delete
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/channel_unlink.html

These two actions sound similar and behave very differently. ## Unlink a channel Removes the channel from your account. The bot stops publishing there. Scheduled and recurring messages are not deleted: they stay stored against that channel and reattach when you reconnect it. While the channel is disconnected nothing is published there. Reversible. Where: channel card → 🔗 Disconnect Channel → confirm. ## Delete messages Removes queue entries permanently. They will never be sent. Not reversible (except by restoring a backup). Where: 📋 Message List → 🗑 , or /delete → 🗑 Delete by ID / 🗑 Delete All . ## Which one do you need? • Moving to a new channel? Change Channel on the card, not unlink. • Pausing everything for a while? Disconnect the channel; reconnect later. • Cancelling specific posts? Delete those messages, keep the channel. • Leaving Telegram entirely? Disconnect channels and delete your data (Delete Account). ## What unlink does not do It does not delete your account, your media storage, your other channels, or your plan. It also does not remove the bots from Telegram's admin list — do that in the channel if you want them fully gone. Related: Remove a Channel, Delete Messages.

## Remove a Channel
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/channel_remove.html

## Disconnect 1. Open 📢 Channels . 2. Open the channel's card. 3. Tap 🔗 Disconnect Channel . 4. Confirm with ✅ Yes . Only the channel owner can disconnect it. ## What happens to the queue Scheduled and recurring messages for that channel are not deleted. The confirmation tells you how many scheduled messages are affected, warning that they will be "removed or reassigned"; the entries stay stored against the channel, do not send while it is disconnected, and reattach when you reconnect the same channel. They are not copied to another channel automatically. If you want them elsewhere, use 🔄 Change Channel on the card instead of disconnecting. ## What happens to the sender bot If the bot served only this channel, it is left without a channel and the bot tells you. It stays in your bot list; attach it to another channel with 🔀 Switch channel or remove it. ## What happens to admins The channel's admin records and permission state are cleared, so a future reconnect starts fresh. Co-admins lose access with the channel. ## After disconnecting The channel disappears from the list and its time zone/signature stop applying. The bots remain administrators in Telegram until you remove them there. Related: Unlink vs Delete, Manage Sender Bots.

Q: Do my scheduled posts get deleted when I remove a channel?
A: No. They are paused and kept against the channel. Reconnect it and they resume. Deleting is a separate action.

## Signature
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/channel_signature.html

A signature is text added to a post at send time — a handle, a slogan, a link line. It is a Premium feature and belongs to a channel. ## Create one 1. Open ⚙️ Settings → 📝 Signature , or send /signature . 2. Tap ➕ Add Signature . 3. Send the signature text. 4. Choose the position: 📝 Start or 📝 End . 5. Choose how many lines separate it from the content. 6. Pick the channel it applies to, and whether it should be added automatically. ## Manage them Saved Signatures lists every signature. You can edit the text, change the position or lines, toggle it, or delete it. Deleting warns you if scheduled or recurring messages currently use it. ## At send time The signature is appended when the post goes out, so stored content stays clean. Changing a signature changes future sends, not past posts. ## Limits Free accounts can try the feature once; after that it is Premium. Signature length counts toward the caption limit, so keep it short. ## Preview Use 👁 Preview with sample text to see the result before saving. Related: Signature Position, Signatures (Premium), Signature.

Q: Can different channels have different signatures?
A: Yes. A signature is attached to a channel, so each channel can have its own footer and position.

## Signature Position
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/channel_signature_position.html

The position decides whether the signature reads as a header or a sign-off. ## End (default) The signature appears under the content, separated by the number of blank lines you chose. This is the classic sign-off: a handle, a site, a short credit. ## Start The signature appears first, then the content. Useful for a recurring label such as "Weekly digest" or a sponsorship line. ## Line spacing Choosing 1–2 lines keeps it visually separate from the body. More lines waste space on mobile; 0 lines makes it read as part of the post. ## Preview Always preview with sample text: the same signature can read well at the end and awkwardly at the start, especially if it ends with a link. ## Interaction with captions Signatures are added to captions too. A long caption plus a signature can exceed Telegram's caption limit, so trim the text. Related: Signature, Captions & Formatting.

## Channel Stats
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/channel_stats.html

Channel statistics answer one question: which posts are worth repeating? ## What is measured • views per post; • reactions, grouped by type; • comments, when the channel has a discussion group; • totals and averages for the period you choose. ## Where to find it 📊 Statistics on main menu page 2 (or /stats ). Pick a channel to open its overview; each channel row can also deep-link into the sender bot that posts there. ## Leaderboards (Premium) Inside a channel's stats, Leaderboard ranks top posts by 👁 views, 💬 comments or ❤️ reactions. Filter by period (today, week, month, year, all) and page size (10, 25, 50). ## Comment attribution To see who comments, add the bot to the channel's linked discussion group. Until then the leaderboard shows a tip explaining how to enable it. ## What it does not measure Only posts sent through Fast Scheduler. Posts published manually in Telegram are not in these numbers. Views are Telegram's own counters, so they can lag by a few minutes. Related: Statistics Dashboard, Channel Stats & Leaderboards, Leaderboard.

Q: Why are views missing for a recent post?
A: Telegram updates view counters periodically. Wait a few minutes and refresh the stats.

## Signatures (Premium)
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/signature.html

Add a custom signature — for example "Posted by @yourbot" — to every post on the channels you choose. How to set up: 1. Tap 📝 Signature on the main menu or send /signature. 2. Use Add Signature and send your signature text (bold, italic, code and links work). 3. Pick the position — start or end of the post — and how many blank lines separate it. 4. Enable auto-add and select the channels it should attach to; or add it per message from the signature list. Good to know: • Signatures are appended at send time — your stored messages stay clean. • They never take over your inline button rows. • Free users can try signatures once; after that it is a Premium feature. When Premium expires: auto-add stops once Premium is gone, and signature settings are deleted when the expiry process fully completes. Reactivate Premium to keep everything.

## How to Connect a Telegram Channel to Fast Scheduler (Full Walkthrough)
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_add_channel_guide.html

Connecting a channel is a two-part handshake: the bot needs admin rights in the channel , and the channel needs to be registered in the bot . Here is the whole dance, including the steps people miss. Part 1 — make the bot an admin of your channel 1. Open your channel in Telegram → Manage Channel → Administrators → Add Admin . 2. Search for @FastSchedulerBot and add it. 3. Give it at least Post Messages . If you plan to schedule on behalf of other admins or use anonymous admin, keep the defaults sane. Part 2 — register the channel in the bot 1. In the bot, tap Connect Channel . 2. Give the bot what it asks for — any of these works: the channel's @username for public channels, a forwarded message from the channel, an invite link ( t.me/+… or t.me/joinchat/… ) for private channels. 3. Confirm. The bot verifies that it really is an admin there. Part 3 — pair the sender bot (mandatory) Every channel needs a sender bot — your own bot created via @BotFather — before anything can be scheduled. This is not optional: the sender bot is the account that actually publishes your posts, under its name. Fast Scheduler's main bot coordinates the schedule; the sender bot delivers. The in-bot wizard creates and pairs one in a minute; see the sender-bots guide for the detailed flow. The classic errors, decoded “Channel not found” — typo in the username, or the bot was not added as admin before you tried to connect. Add first, then connect. “Not an admin” — the admin rights were granted to a different bot than the one you connected. “Invalid token” — the sender-bot token got truncated on copy. Copy the whole thing: digits, colon, the rest.

Q: Can I connect a private channel?
A: Yes — via invite link or by forwarding any message from the channel during connection. Public username is not required.

Q: Why do I need my own bot just to post?
A: Telegram architecture: messages in a channel are sent by a bot account, not by your user account. Pairing your own sender bot also means posts appear under your brand, not a generic one.

Q: The channel connects but posts fail. First checks?
A: Sender bot still admin? Post Messages permission on? Bot not revoked in @BotFather? Those three cover nearly all post failures.

## How Do I Connect a Private Telegram Channel to Fast Scheduler?
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_private_channel_connect.html

Private channels are fully supported — the bot never needs to be able to search your channel, it only needs to be inside it as an admin. There are four accepted ways to point Fast Scheduler at a private channel, and at least one of them will take you under a minute. Before you start: give the bots admin rights Open your private channel → Administrators → Add Admin . Add @FastSchedulerBot with the Post Messages permission. That single permission is enough to schedule and publish. Then, inside Fast Scheduler, pair a sender bot and make it an admin of the same channel. This step is mandatory: every scheduled post is published through your sender bot , never through the main bot, so nothing in the scheduling flow unlocks until each connected channel has one. Four ways to connect the channel Open the bot → Channels → Connect Channel , then send whichever of these is easiest for you: @username — private channels have no @username, so this one is mostly for public channels. Forward any post from the channel to the bot. This is the fastest way for private channels: open the channel, long-press any message, Forward → Fast Scheduler Bot. The bot reads the source channel from the forward. An invite link — copy Invite Link from the channel menu and paste it into the chat. The channel ID — the numeric -100… identifier (e.g. -1001234567890 ) if you know it from another tool. Why the invite-link and forward methods are equivalent Both simply resolve your private channel to its internal ID. Fast Scheduler stores that ID plus your admin status; the channel&rsquo;s privacy settings never matter again after the connection is made. You can rename the channel, change its link, or toggle &ldquo;slow mode&rdquo; — the connection survives all of it. If connecting fails Bot is not an admin — re-check step one; the permission check runs live against Telegram. Invite link revoked or set to &ldquo;join request&rdquo; — regenerate the link, or forward a post instead. You are not the owner — the connector must hold admin rights in the channel under the account that talks to the bot. Free plan: 1 channel. Premium raises this to 3, each with its own sender bot, time zone and statistics.

Q: Can Fast Scheduler post to a private channel?
A: Yes. Private channels are connected by forwarding a post from the channel, pasting an invite link, or sending the -100 channel ID. The channel being private does not affect scheduling in any way.

Q: Does the sender bot also need admin rights in a private channel?
A: Yes. The main bot needs Post Messages to verify and manage, and your sender bot needs Post Messages because it is the account that actually publishes every scheduled post.

Q: How many channels can I connect on the Free plan?
A: Free includes 1 channel with 100 sent messages per month. Premium raises the limit to 3 channels with unlimited sends.

# Sender Bots

## Sender Bots
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/bots.html

A sender bot is a Telegram bot you own, connected to exactly one channel, that publishes your posts under its own name. ## Why it is required Telegram needs a bot with Post Messages rights in the channel. Using your own bot also gives your channel a stable author identity, lower sending delays and per-channel statistics. ## The lifecycle 1. Create it in @BotFather. 2. Connect its token in 🤖 Bots . 3. Assign it to a channel. 4. Promote it in that channel with Post Messages. 5. Manage it later: change token, replace, switch channel, swap, remove. ## Limits Free: 1 bot. Premium: up to 3 . One bot per channel. ## Start here • Add a Sender Bot — creation and connection. • Manage Sender Bots — the Manage menu. • Sender Bot Management — what moves inside the bot. • Bot Permissions and Bot Status — rights and health. • Rotate Token — after a leak or a reset. • Remove a Sender Bot — detach without losing posts. Never share a token: anyone holding it can post as your bot.

Q: Can one sender bot serve several channels?
A: No, not simultaneously. Use the Manage menu’s Switch channel to move it, or run separate bots.

## Add a Sender Bot
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/bot_add.html

## 1. Create the bot Open @BotFather → /newbot → display name → username ending in bot . Copy the token it returns. ## 2. Connect it 🤖 Bots → 🔑 I Have a Token → send the token. The bot verifies it and shows the bot's username. ## 3. Assign a channel Pick the channel this bot should publish to. One bot per channel. ## 4. Promote it Channel → Administrators → Add Administrator → your bot → Post Messages . Return and press 🔄 Check Again if asked. ## Limits Free: 1 bot. Premium: 3. ## Common failures • Invalid token — incomplete copy. Copy the whole line, including the colon. • That is the main bot's token — create your own bot. • Bot is not admin — promote your bot in the channel. • Limit reached — remove a bot or upgrade: Sender Bot Limit. Related: Connecting a Bot, Step 2: Connect a Sender Bot.

## Manage Sender Bots
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/bot_manage.html

🤖 Bots (N) lists every sender bot with its channel. Open a bot's ⚙ Manage menu to act on it. ## The five actions • 🔑 Change token — the bot was revoked in @BotFather. Paste the new token for the same bot; the channel, queue and settings stay. • 🔁 Replace bot — a different bot takes over this channel. Data moves; the old bot is detached. • 🔀 Switch channel — point this bot at another channel you own. The bot keeps its token; the channel keeps its data. • ⇄ Swap bots — exchange the channels of two bots. Schedules and settings stay with the channels; only the bots move. • 🗑 Remove bot — detach the bot from its channel. The queue pauses; posts are not deleted. ## What stays and what moves The rule is simple: data belongs to the channel , identity belongs to the bot. Moving a bot does not move its queue; replacing a bot does not lose it. ## After a token change Nothing else needs to be redone. Scheduled posts resume automatically once the token is valid. ## If a bot has no channel It remains in the list and can be attached with 🔀 Switch channel , or removed. Related: Add a Sender Bot, Rotate Token, Remove a Sender Bot.

Q: What is the difference between Replace and Switch?
A: Replace swaps the bot for a different one on the same channel. Switch keeps the bot and moves it to a different channel.

## Sender Bot Management
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/sender_bot_management.html

A sender bot is not only a publisher; it is the control room for its channel. ## What moves in automatically Scheduling, recurring messages, the message list, statistics, the calendar and channel settings. No extra setup: when the bot is connected, these screens live there. ## The Channel Settings menu Left ⚙️ Settings in the sender bot opens Channel Settings : • 🔒 Hide channel from strangers / 🔓 Show channel to strangers — Public Mode. When hidden, people who start the bot see a generic welcome and an Open Main Bot button instead of your channel name. • 👥 Admins — owner only. Add co-admins and choose exactly which areas they can use. • 🏠 Open @FastSchedulerBot — back to the account hub. • ❌ Back . ## Account settings stay separate Right ⚙️ Settings (or /settings ) is your account: language, time zone, signature, storage, commands. It is not channel-specific. ## What remains in the main bot Channels, bots, language, help, referrals, premium, import/export. This split is deliberate: account-level actions should not depend on a channel. ## If the bot's token breaks Fast Scheduler falls back to the main bot where possible so a post is not lost, and notifies you. Restore the token with ⚙ Manage → 🔑 Change token . Related: Manage Sender Bots, Permissions & Requests, How Posting Works.

Q: What does Hide channel actually hide?
A: Your channel name and identity from strangers who start the sender bot. Your subscribers and admins are unaffected.

## Bot Permissions
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/bot_permissions.html

A sender bot publishes only while it is an administrator of its channel. ## Required Post Messages . Without it, every send fails and Fast Scheduler reports the channel as unavailable. ## Recommended Edit Messages — correct a published post. Delete Messages — remove posts during cleanup. ## Granting them Channel → Administrators → Add Administrator → your bot → enable rights → save. Repeat after moving the bot with 🔀 Switch channel . ## Verifying Press 🔄 Check Again in the bot when it asks. Rights are checked live, so a fix is recognised immediately. ## What breaks • Removing the bot from admins stops delivery. • A channel ownership change can drop bot rights. • A revoked token makes the bot unreachable — rotate it. The queue is preserved in every case; restore the rights or token and it continues. Related: Channel Permissions, Bot Status, Permission.

## Posting as Your Bot
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/bot_sender.html

When your sender bot publishes, the post carries its name and avatar. ## Why that matters • A consistent author identity for your channel. • Inline buttons and polls belong to your bot. • Per-channel statistics are attributed correctly. • No shared queue with unrelated channels, so delivery is faster. ## What readers do not see They do not see @FastSchedulerBot in the post. The scheduling service is invisible. If someone opens your sender bot directly, Public Mode can hide the channel name. ## Which bot posts where Each channel's copy is delivered by that channel's own bot, including in multi-channel scheduling. A post scheduled from channel A but sent to B and C appears from B's and C's bots. ## When a post comes from the main bot Only in a fallback situation where the sender bot's token cannot be used. It is a safety net so content is not lost, and the bot warns you to fix the token. Related: How Posting Works, Bot Permissions.

## Bot Status
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/bot_status.html

The 🤖 Bots (N) list is the status board: each row shows the bot's username and the channel it serves. ## Healthy The bot shows its channel and opens its Manage menu without warnings. Posts are delivered normally. ## Needs attention • No channel — attach it with 🔀 Switch channel or remove it. • Token invalid — rotate it: Rotate Token. • Not admin — restore Post Messages in the channel. • Channel frozen — the plan lapsed and the channel is beyond the free limit; choose what to keep: Frozen Assets. ## What happens to queued posts They wait. A temporary failure is retried; a permission failure pauses the channel until fixed. The bot reports the reason rather than dropping posts. ## Checking from the channel side Open the channel card: it shows the sender bot assigned to that channel. If the field is empty, no bot is attached. Related: Manage Sender Bots, Channel Errors.

## Channel Stats & Leaderboards
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/bot_stats.html

Statistics are per channel and cover only posts sent through Fast Scheduler. ## Open them 📊 Statistics on main menu page 2, or /stats . Pick a channel to see totals and averages for views, comments and reactions, plus top reactions. ## Leaderboards (Premium) Inside a channel's stats, tap Leaderboard to rank top posts by 👁 views, 💬 comments or ❤️ reactions. Filters: today / week / month / year / all, and 10 / 25 / 50 rows per page. ## Comment attribution Add the bot to the channel's linked discussion group. Then comments are attributed to their authors and a top-commentators ranking becomes available. ## Why numbers look low Only scheduler-sent posts count. Manual posts, deleted posts and posts from before you connected the bot are not included. Telegram's counters also lag a few minutes. ## Use them to decide Repeat formats that win on reactions, move announcements to the hour with the most views, and retire formats that consistently underperform. Related: Statistics Dashboard, Channel Stats, Leaderboard.

## Rotate Token
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/bot_rotate.html

A token is the password of your bot. If it leaks, anyone can post as you until it is revoked. ## Revoke in @BotFather Open @BotFather → /mybots → your bot → API Token → Revoke current token . BotFather returns a new token and the old one stops working immediately. ## Update it in Fast Scheduler 🤖 Bots → your bot → ⚙ Manage → 🔑 Change token → paste the new token. The bot, its channel, its queue and its settings stay exactly as they are. Scheduled posts resume automatically. ## If you paste the wrong token The bot tells you which username the token belongs to and refuses. Use 🔁 Replace bot if you actually want a different bot. ## Prevention • Never share a token in chat, screenshots or public repos. • Fast Scheduler never shows the token back in full. • Exports containing tokens are always encrypted as a Protected Backup ( .fspback ). ## If the bot was deleted in BotFather A deleted bot cannot be restored. Create a new bot and use 🔁 Replace bot to take over the channel; data moves over. Related: Token Safety, Manage Sender Bots.

Q: Do I need to re-add the bot as admin after rotating the token?
A: No. It is the same bot with a new password; its admin rights in the channel are unchanged.

## Remove a Sender Bot
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/bot_remove.html

Removing a bot disconnects it from Fast Scheduler but keeps your content. ## How 🤖 Bots → the bot → ⚙ Manage → 🗑 Remove bot → confirm. ## What happens • The token is deleted from your account. • The bot is detached from the channel. • Scheduled and recurring posts for that channel are paused, not deleted. • The channel returns to the "connect a sender bot" state. ## What does not happen The bot is not deleted in Telegram. Remove it from the channel's admin list there if you want it gone entirely. ## Replacing it Connect a new bot to the same channel and the queue resumes. If you only want to change the token of the same bot, use 🔑 Change token instead of removing. ## Freeing a slot On the Free plan this frees your single bot slot, so you can connect a different bot. See Sender Bot Limit. Related: Manage Sender Bots, Remove a Channel.

## Bot Fleet
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/bot_fleet.html

A fleet is simply several sender bots, each bound to one channel. Premium allows up to 3; Free allows 1. ## Why a fleet • One author identity per channel. • Independent rate limits and failure domains. • Per-channel statistics and settings. • Clean handover: a bot can be replaced or moved without touching another channel. ## Keeping it organised • Name each bot after its channel. • Keep its profile photo and description consistent with the channel. • Use ⇄ Swap bots when two bots should trade channels. • Remove bots you no longer use to free slots. ## Permissions Every bot in the fleet must be an administrator of its own channel with Post Messages. A bot that loses rights pauses only its channel. ## Security Each token is a separate key. Rotate a leaked one immediately; the others are unaffected. Related: Manage Sender Bots, Sender Bot Limit, Token Safety.

## Main-Bot Stand-In
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/main_bot_stand_in.html

A sender bot can stop working at the worst moment: token revoked in @BotFather, removed from the channel, or Telegram refusing its rights. The stand-in is the safety net — and it is deliberately narrow. ## What triggers it Only a sender authentication or permission failure : revoked or invalid token, bot removed from the channel, missing Post Messages . Content errors, timeouts, rate limits and channel-level restrictions never trigger it, because the main bot would hit exactly the same wall — resending those would only produce duplicates or a second failure. ## What you see 1. The post is delivered once by the main bot, so a scheduled message is not silently lost. 2. Immediately afterwards the bot asks, once: keep posting from the main bot for up to N days while the sender bot is broken? 3. Yes enables the stand-in for that channel for the current window. No records the refusal — the channel will not be asked again, and failed posts are reported as errors. ## The window The default is 3 days per activation. The operator can change the default and set a per-sender-bot override; the range is 1 hour to 30 days. When the window ends the stand-in stops by itself, the next failure is reported normally, and the message says the window is over. There is no "renews automatically". ## Who can enable it The channel owner, or an admin holding settings_change_permissions . Nobody else — it is a channel-wide decision that changes who publishes, not a personal preference. ## Guards against abuse • Opt-in, never automatic. Delivering the first lost post is a rescue; continuing is a choice. • Toggle-off-then-on cannot extend the deadline. Re-enabling inside the cooldown keeps the original expiry. • One prompt per channel per cooldown window — no notification spam while an owner is already fixing the bot. • Bounded window , clamped server-side, never "forever". • Audited. Enable, decline, revert and expiry are all written to the log with the actor. • Global kill switch. The operator can disable stand-ins for every channel at once, for example during an incident. ## Ending it early The confirmation message carries ⛔ Stop the stand-in now . You can also open the channel's settings screen: the active window is shown with the remaining time and the same button. Ending it does not delete anything — the queue simply goes back to failing loudly if the sender bot is still broken. ## What it is not It is not a second scheduler, it does not post from your sender bot's name (posts appear from the main bot, and readers can tell), it does not fix the token, and it does not bypass your channel's permissions. It buys time to fix the real problem — nothing more. ## For operators The /fallback command controls the feature: /fallback shows the current default, overrides and active stand-ins; /fallback on|off switches it globally; /fallback days 72h sets the default window; /fallback @bot 12h sets a per-bot override; /fallback reset @bot drops it; /fallback revert all stops every active stand-in. It is restricted to the bot's operators. ## Related Sender Bot First: the New Setup, Bot Permissions, "Bot Is Not an Admin" Errors, Admins & Access.

Q: Will readers know the main bot posted instead of my bot?
A: Yes — the author of a Telegram message is the bot that sent it. That is the honest trade-off: a post from a bot your readers do not follow, instead of no post at all.

Q: Does the stand-in start without me saying yes?
A: Only the first rescue post is automatic, and that is what saves the scheduled message. Everything after it waits for an explicit yes.

Q: I tapped No — can I change my mind?
A: Yes, by enabling it from the channel settings screen. The refusal only means the bot stops asking on its own.

Q: Why did it stop in the middle of an outage?
A: The window ended. It is a fixed duration from the moment you enabled it, not a countdown that pauses while you are busy. Fix the sender bot and the queue resumes.

## Do You Need a Sender Bot to Schedule Posts? (Yes — Here Is Why)
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_sender_bot_required.html

Short answer: yes — a sender bot is required for scheduling and sending. The scheduling menu stays locked until every connected channel has one paired. Here is the why and the 60-second setup. Why the main bot cannot just post itself Two reasons, one technical and one yours: Architecture: channel posts are delivered by a bot account with admin rights. If @FastSchedulerBot delivered them, every message on every customer channel would carry the same name — and one bot hitting rate limits would slow thousands of channels. Your brand: with your own sender bot, posts appear from your bot's name and avatar. Subscribers see your brand, and your bot's admin rights are yours to revoke. Creating one in 60 seconds 1. Open @BotFather → /newbot → pick a name and username. 2. Copy the token (digits, colon, letters — the whole string). 3. In Fast Scheduler: Bots → ➕ Add Another Bot , pick the channel when asked, paste the token. Pairing is automatic. 4. Make the new bot an admin of the channel with Post Messages permission — or let Fast Scheduler promote it automatically when it can. Scheduling unlocks instantly. The in-bot wizard walks these exact steps and checks each one, so you cannot get the order wrong. Security, briefly Your token is stored encrypted and used only to deliver your posts. You can rotate it any time via @BotFather ( /revoke ) and update it in the bot — or remove the bot entirely, which deletes the token from Fast Scheduler's storage. If a token leaks, revoke it in BotFather first; a revoked token is dead everywhere. One bot per channel (Premium: 3×3) Free pairs 1 sender bot with 1 channel; Premium allows 3 bots across 3 channels. Multiple channels can share one sender bot, but the clean setup — one bot per channel — keeps branding separate and failures isolated.

Q: Can one sender bot serve two channels?
A: Yes, a sender bot can be paired with multiple channels you own. One bot per channel is still recommended for cleaner branding and simpler troubleshooting.

Q: What happens if I remove the sender bot from the channel?
A: Scheduling locks (no sender paired for that channel) and queued sends fail until you re-add the bot as admin. The schedules themselves stay saved.

Q: Is my bot token safe with Fast Scheduler?
A: Tokens are stored encrypted and never displayed in full after saving. Rotating the token in @BotFather instantly invalidates the old one everywhere.

## How to Manage Your Sender Bots: Rotate, Rename, and Keep Them Healthy
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_bot_management.html

Your sender bot is the public face of every post, so a little hygiene goes a long way. Everything below lives in Sender Bots (or /bots ) in Fast Scheduler. Check status before you check anything else The bots screen shows each bot's connection state and which channels it serves. If a send ever fails, this is the first screen: a bot showing disconnected means a revoked token or a BotFather change — fix it there, not in the schedule. Rotating a token (the right way) 1. @BotFather → /mybots → your bot → Revoke current token . 2. Copy the new token. 3. Fast Scheduler → Bots → 🔁 Replace Token under the bot → paste. The swap is instant and schedules keep running. Do it the other way around (revoke and forget) and every send fails until you paste the new token. Rename = rebrand A bot's public name and avatar come from @BotFather ( /setname , /setuserpic ) — change them there and every future post instantly carries the new look. No re-pairing needed; Fast Scheduler stores the token, not the cosmetics. Fleet hygiene One bot per channel keeps branding separate and failures isolated (Premium: up to 3 bots). Remove bots you no longer use — removal deletes the token from storage; the bot account itself lives on in BotFather. After any BotFather change, glance at the status screen once — 10 seconds that prevent a silent failed-post day.

Q: Can I use the same bot for multiple channels?
A: Yes — a sender bot can serve several of your channels. Separate bots per channel remain the cleaner default for branding and debugging.

Q: I deleted a bot in BotFather. What happens in Fast Scheduler?
A: Its sends fail with an invalid-token error and the status screen shows it disconnected. Remove the bot from Sender Bots and pair a replacement.

# Admins & Access (RBAC)

## Admins & Access (RBAC)
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/admins.html

Admins are other Telegram accounts that work on your channel without owning it. Access is decided in two layers: Telegram says who may administer the channel, and Fast Scheduler decides what each of those people may do inside the bot. Both layers must agree — a Telegram administrator with no bot permissions can open the sender bot and see only the features granted to them. ## The three roles • Main Owner — the account that set the channel up. Has every permission, cannot be limited, and is the only role that can change permissions, remove admins or transfer ownership. There is exactly one per channel. • Admin — a Telegram administrator of that channel who was added to the bot. Works with the 15 permissions listed in Permissions & Requests; new admins start with scheduling, recurring messages, message list, preview, edit, search and statistics on, and everything else off. • Revoked — someone the owner removed. Their record is kept (with who removed them and when) so they cannot quietly re-add themselves; only the owner can restore them. ## Two ways to become an admin 1. The owner adds them. Open the channel's sender bot → ⚙️ Settings → 👥 Admins . The bot syncs Telegram's administrator list and creates a record with the default permissions. Nothing is shared between channels. 2. A co-admin proves channel rights. If the channel already has a sender bot, any existing Telegram administrator can send that bot's @username or token to the bot. The bot asks Telegram, through that sender bot, whether the requester is an administrator of its channel; if yes, the default permissions are granted and the owner is notified. Full walkthrough: Join a Channel That Already Has a Bot. ## Where it lives, and why Admin management lives inside the sender bot of that channel , never in the main bot. A sender bot runs exactly one channel, so a permission record has exactly one scope. The main bot knows nothing about who helps you. ## Scope: one channel, nothing else An admin record is bound to one channel id. An admin of channel A cannot see channel B — not in the channel list, the message list, the statistics, the media storage, the bots menu, the export menu or any notification. They cannot see the owner's other channels either, and they never receive the owner's payment or expiry messages. ## Enforcement is server-side, at click time Every button, every typed step and every deep link re-checks the permission when it is used, not when the keyboard was drawn. If a permission is taken away while an old message is still on screen, pressing its button answers "you do not have permission" and offers Request permission from the admin — it never performs the action. Telegram keyboards are just JSON in an old chat message; they are never trusted as proof of anything. ## Privacy: Hide channel from strangers When the owner enables Hide channel from strangers , every non-owner — including co-admins and anyone verifying their rights with an @username — sees the channel as this channel . No title, no @username, no t.me link, no numeric id, in confirmations, refusals, owner notifications or audit screens. The owner always sees the real name. This setting is itself a permission ( settings_hide_channel ), so an admin cannot turn it off to look around. ## Audit trail Every grant, permission save, revoke, restore, self-attach and ownership transfer is written to the RBAC audit log with the actor, the target, the channel, the timestamp and a short reason. "Who gave this person delete rights?" has an answer. ## Automatic revocation On every sync the bot re-reads the channel's administrator list. If an admin was removed in Telegram, lost Post Messages , or was blocked by the owner, their bot access is revoked automatically — no manual cleanup, and no window in which a removed person keeps working from an old keyboard. ## What an admin can never do • Take ownership without the owner starting a transfer and the target accepting it. • See or use the owner's sender bot token, or add/remove/rename bots. • Reach another channel of the same owner. • Grant permissions (unless the owner granted settings_change_permissions ). • Delete the channel, its data or its audit history. • Enable the main-bot stand-in for a channel they do not control (owner or the settings permission only). See Main-Bot Stand-In. ## Related Join a Channel That Already Has a Bot, Permissions & Requests, How Admins Share Limits, Ownership Transfer, Sender Bot First: the New Setup.

Q: Can an admin take over my channel?
A: No. Ownership only moves when the current Main Owner starts a transfer, types the confirmation phrase, and the target accepts it within 24 hours. An admin cannot start that flow and cannot grant themselves the permission to do it.

Q: Why does the main bot no longer need to be a channel administrator?
A: Because it no longer touches the channel. Your sender bot publishes, and the main bot only talks to you. The one exception is the optional stand-in: if you enable it and your sender bot breaks, the main bot posts on your behalf for a bounded window, and for that it needs Post Messages like any other bot.

Q: An admin says the bot refuses them, but they are an administrator in Telegram.
A: Check three things: that they opened the sender bot of that channel (not the main bot), that their Telegram rights include Post Messages , and that they were not revoked by the owner. A revoked admin stays blocked until the owner restores them from Settings → Admins → Revoked.

Q: Can two people manage the same channel without sharing a login?
A: Yes — that is exactly what admins are for. Each person connects their own Telegram account, gets their own permissions, and every action is attributed to them in the audit log. Nobody shares a token or a password.

Q: Do admins share the channel's message limits?
A: Yes. Scheduled slots, monthly sends, recurring rules and media storage belong to the channel, so every admin draws from the same quota. See How Admins Share Limits for the counters that reset and the ones that do not.

Q: How do I remove someone completely?
A: Settings → Admins → their profile → Remove. Their access ends immediately and the record moves to Revoked with the reason and timestamp. Queued posts stay with the channel — they belong to the channel, not to the person who typed them.

## Join a Channel That Already Has a Bot
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/admins_attach.html

A channel can only have one sender bot. If you are a newly added Telegram administrator and the channel is already managed here, you do not need the owner to do anything: prove your rights once and the bot grants you the default admin permissions itself. ## What to send Send either of these as a normal message to the bot: • the sender bot's @username — for example @My_Channel_Bot ; or • the sender bot's token — the 1234567890:ABCdef… line from @BotFather. You can send it to the main bot or to the sender bot itself; both understand it. Do not press any menu button first — the message alone is the request. ## What happens next 1. The bot resolves the username (or calls getMe on the token) and finds which channel that sender bot serves. 2. It asks Telegram, through that sender bot , what your status is in that channel. 3. If Telegram reports administrator or creator , you are added with the default permissions: scheduling, recurring messages, message list, preview, edit, search and statistics — everything else stays off until the owner grants it. 4. The owner receives a notification naming you (and naming the channel only if it is not hidden), so access is never silent. 5. You get a green Open @bot button that drops you straight into the sender bot. ## If it is refused • "I couldn't confirm you as an administrator" — Telegram does not list you as an administrator of that channel, or your account is not the one sending the message. Ask for the administrator role first, then retry. • "Access was revoked" — the owner removed you on purpose. Only the owner can restore you (Settings → Admins → Revoked). • "That bot isn't connected to a channel yet" — the sender bot exists but was never attached; ask the owner to connect it first. • "Too many attempts" — the verification endpoint is rate-limited to a handful of tries per hour per account, because it is probeable. Wait an hour; nothing is lost. ## Privacy when the channel is hidden If the owner enabled Hide channel from strangers , the confirmation you receive says this channel and never shows the title, @username, link or numeric id. That is not a bug and not a sign of a wrong bot — it is the owner's setting, and it applies to admins too. Your access is still real; ask the owner for the link if you need it. ## About the token Sending a bot token to the bot you are trying to join is how the verification reads your rights through that bot. It is used for the check and is not echoed back. Still treat a token like a password: send it only inside a private chat with the bot, never in a group, a comment thread or a screenshot. If you are not comfortable sending it, the @username is enough — the bot can resolve it from its own records. ## Permissions you get, and changing them The defaults are intentionally conservative. Everything is listed in Permissions & Requests, and the owner can change each one individually.
