If you need more, use Request permission from the admin on any refusal screen instead of asking the owner in a private chat — the request carries the exact permission and lands in the owner's queue. ## Related Admins & Access, Sender Bot First: the New Setup, Channel Permissions.

Q: Do I need to know the owner's Telegram account?
A: No. The bot resolves the channel from the sender bot itself and notifies the owner on its own. You never have to find or message them.

Q: Will the owner see that I joined?
A: Yes, immediately — with your name, the bot you used, and the channel unless it is hidden. Every attach is also written to the audit log.

Q: Can I do this if I am not a Telegram administrator yet?
A: No, and it is not a bug. The bot only mirrors rights Telegram already granted; it does not create channel administrators. Ask an owner to promote you first.

Q: The @username is right but the bot says it is not connected.
A: That sender bot exists but has no channel attached yet. Ask the owner to finish its setup — the bot cannot grant access to a channel it does not serve.

## Permissions & Requests
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/admins_permissions.html

The Main Owner controls exactly what each admin can do. There are 15 independent permissions; nothing is bundled behind a vague "manage" switch, and nothing is granted implicitly. ## The full list • schedule — create scheduled messages. On by default. • recurring — create recurring messages. On by default. • message_list — open the message list. On by default. • message_preview — preview a message before it goes out. On by default. • message_edit — edit a queued message. On by default. • message_change — move a message to another channel. Off by default. • message_delete — delete a queued message. Off by default. • message_search — search the channel's messages. On by default. • stats_view — view statistics for the channel. On by default. • leaderboard_view — view the channel leaderboard. Off by default. • data_export — export the channel's data. Off by default. • data_import — import messages into the channel. Off by default. • data_backup — create a backup of the channel. Off by default. • settings_hide_channel — turn "Hide channel from strangers" on or off. Off by default. • settings_change_permissions — change other admins' permissions. Off by default. ## Grouped in the interface, separate in the database The editor groups them to keep the keyboard readable — Messages (list, preview, edit, change, delete, search), Statistics (stats, leaderboard), Data (export, import, backup), Settings (hide channel, change permissions). Tapping a group opens its individual switches. Saving the group saves each switch exactly as shown; there is no hidden "group unlock". ## Changing them Owner → ⚙️ Settings → 👥 Admins → pick the admin → toggle. Changes accumulate as a draft; Save Changes applies them and shows a summary of what changed. Leaving with unsaved toggles asks whether to save or discard, so a half-configured admin is never applied silently. ## Effect is immediate Disabled features disappear from that admin's keyboard on the next screen. If they press an old button from chat history, the bot refuses with "you do not have permission" and offers Request permission from the admin . The check happens when the button is pressed, not when it was drawn. ## Requests An admin who lacks a permission can request it, optionally with a one-line reason. The owner receives the request with Grant / Deny (and can reply when denying). Anti-spam: one request per permission per user per channel per week . A granted request is a normal permission change and appears in the audit log; a denied one does not block asking again after the cooldown. ## Removing and restoring Removing an admin revokes access at once and stores the record in Revoked with the reason, the actor and the timestamp. A revoked person cannot re-attach themselves through the @username path — only the owner can restore them. Queued posts stay with the channel; deleting an admin never deletes content they created. ## Automatic revocation from Telegram Rights Telegram takes away, the bot takes away: losing the administrator role or the Post Messages right revokes bot access on the next sync. The reverse is not automatic — becoming a Telegram administrator does not grant bot permissions; the owner or the self-attach flow does. ## What cannot be granted Ownership, the owner's bot token, adding or renaming bots, other channels, payment and billing data, and the RBAC audit log are never delegable. If an admin needs something that is not in the list above, the answer is a different role, not a wider permission. ## Related Admins & Access, Join a Channel That Already Has a Bot, Ownership Transfer, Bot Permissions.

Q: What exactly does a brand-new admin get?
A: Seven permissions on: schedule, recurring, message list, preview, edit, search and statistics. Everything else — move, delete, leaderboard, export, import, backup, hide channel, change permissions — stays off until the owner grants it.

Q: How often can an admin ask for a permission?
A: Once per permission per week per channel. The cooldown is per permission, so asking for export does not delay a later request for statistics.

Q: Why did a granted permission stop working by itself?
A: Either the admin lost the Telegram side (administrator role or Post Messages), or the owner saved a new permission set. Both are recorded in the audit log with the time and the actor.

Q: Does "change permissions" let an admin promote themselves?
A: No. settings_change_permissions lets them edit other admins' switches, but never their own record and never ownership. Only the Main Owner can edit the owner record.

Q: Can I give someone temporary access?
A: Yes, in practice: grant the permissions, and remove them when the work is done. Removal is immediate, and the restored-then-revoked history stays in the audit log.

## How Admins Share Limits
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/admins_limits.html

All message limits are per channel . Every admin of that channel draws from the same quota, which is the whole point: a channel cannot multiply its allowance by adding people. ## What is shared • pending scheduled messages (100 on Free per channel); • sends per month (100 per channel on Free); • active recurring rules (1 on Free); • the channel's media storage and its per-file size cap; • the channel's bot slots (one sender bot per channel). ## What that means in practice If the channel's pending cap is 100 and one admin queues 90, the other admin has 10 left. The limit message does not care who filled the queue, and neither does the counter. ## Monthly counter It counts messages actually sent , not created. Deleting a queued post does not refund a send; the counter resets on the 1st of the next month, or when Premium activates for the channel. ## Premium Premium is bought per account, but its allowances apply to the channels that account owns. A co-admin does not bring their own Premium to someone else's channel — and cannot be charged for it either. If the channel needs more, the owner upgrades. ## Planning with several people Keep the Message List open: it is the shared source of truth for what is queued. Delete by ID is the safe way to remove a specific post without touching anyone else's work. Two admins scheduling the same slot is allowed — the bot does not deduplicate, and both posts will be sent. ## Related Limits Overview, Permissions & Requests, Scheduled Limit.

Q: Do admins each get their own monthly allowance?
A: No. One channel, one allowance. Adding admins adds hands, not quota.

Q: If an admin deletes a queued post, is the send refunded?
A: No. The monthly counter tracks sends performed, not messages sitting in the queue. Deleting before the send time removes the post and frees a queue slot, but the counter only moves when something is actually delivered.

## Ownership Transfer
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/admins_transfer.html

Transferring ownership is deliberately hard to do by accident — and impossible to do alone. ## Preconditions • The target must already be an admin of the channel in the bot . Add them first. • The target must still be a Telegram administrator with Post Messages ; the bot re-checks this at every step. • Only one transfer can be pending per channel. Cancel the current one before starting another. ## The flow 1. Owner opens the target admin's profile → 👑 Make Main Owner . 2. The bot asks the owner to type an exact confirmation phrase naming the channel and the target. A copy-paste of a different phrase is rejected. 3. A final confirm button appears; no request exists before it is pressed. 4. The target receives the request and must accept or decline . ## While it is pending The current owner can cancel at any time. The request expires after 24 hours , and an expired request changes nothing. During this window the current owner keeps full rights — there is no half-transferred state. ## On acceptance The target becomes Main Owner. The previous owner stays as a regular admin with full permissions — they do not lose access, but they can no longer change permissions or start another transfer. Both sides are notified, and the change is written to the audit log. ## If it goes wrong Before acceptance: cancel. After acceptance: the new owner can transfer it back with the same flow, which is why the typed phrase exists — it is a speed bump against a rushed handover, not a lock. ## Why so many steps Ownership controls permissions, exports, backups and the stand-in decision. A single mis-tap that silently handed that to the wrong account would be unrecoverable without support, so the design pays for itself the first time someone fat-fingers a keyboard. ## Related Admins & Access, Permissions & Requests, Main-Bot Stand-In.

Q: Does the old owner lose access?
A: No. They become a regular admin with every permission on. They lose only the owner-only powers: editing permissions, removing admins and starting transfers.

Q: What if the target never answers?
A: The request expires after 24 hours and nothing changes. Start a new one when both people are online.

Q: Can I transfer to someone who is not an admin yet?
A: No. Add them as an admin first, let them open the sender bot once, then start the transfer.

# Premium

## Premium
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/premium.html

Premium is the paid plan. It lifts the caps that stop a growing channel: more channels, more bots, unlimited queues, bigger files, storage, signatures and full statistics. ## What it changes • 3 channels and 3 sender bots instead of 1/1. • Unlimited scheduled, recurring and sent messages. • Uploads up to 100 MB; video up to up to 50MB; 4K allowed. • 20 storage boxes with 500 items and stored video. • Signatures, leaderboards, multi-channel targeting, protected backups. ## How payment works Premium is paid with Telegram Stars — in-app, instant, no card details. Monthly auto-renews; 3-month, 6-month and yearly are one-time purchases. ## What happens when it ends Nothing is deleted on day one. A grace period lets you choose what to keep; later stages pause, then disconnect excess assets. Full timeline: Premium Expiry. ## Related Premium Features, Compare Plans, Buy Premium, Premium Status.

Q: Is Premium per account or per channel?
A: It is bought for the account and raises that account’s allowances. Channel admins do not bring their own Premium to someone else’s channel.

## Premium Features
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/premium_features.html

## Capacity • 3 connected channels and 3 sender bots (Free: 1/1). • Unlimited pending scheduled messages, recurring messages and monthly sends. ## Media • Uploads up to 100 MB, video up to up to 50MB. • 4K sources allowed; lighter compression. • 20 storage boxes with 500 items, video up to up to 50MB. ## Publishing • Signatures — a footer or header on every post, per channel. • Multi-channel targeting — one post to several channels with 📢 Choose channels . • Sender-bot management: Hide Channel (Public Mode), Admins. ## Data and insight • Full channel statistics and leaderboards (views, reactions, comments, top commentators). • Unlimited report schedules. • Full export and password-protected .fspback backups. ## What stays free Scheduling, all supported content types, media modes, search, the calendar, import/export basics and the help center. Related: Compare Plans, Premium Plan Limits.

## Compare Plans
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/premium_compare.html

The authoritative comparison is the table in the Premium menu — it is generated from the same values the bot enforces. The short version Channels: 1 → 3 Sender bots: 1 → 3 Scheduled messages: 100 → Unlimited Recurring messages: 1 → Unlimited Sent messages: 100 → Unlimited Media storage: 1 box / 100 items → 20 boxes / 500 items Video: up to 25MB → up to 50MB Max media: 10 MB → 100 MB Beyond numbers Premium adds signatures, multi-channel targeting, leaderboards, unlimited reports and protected backups. Price Monthly $6.83; yearly $68.03. Prepaid 3- and 6-month plans exist with a discount. The checkout screen shows the final Stars price. Related: Buy Premium , Limits . ## Buy Premium
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/premium_buy.html

## 1. Open Premium ⭐ Upgrade to Premium in the menu, or /premium . ## 2. Choose a plan • Standard monthly — auto-renews every 30 days; cancel anytime. • 3 months — prepaid, discounted, one-time. • 6 months — prepaid, bigger discount, one-time. • Yearly — best per-month price, one-time. ## 3. Pay with Telegram Stars Confirm the native Telegram payment sheet. The bot never sees your card, because there is no card. ## 4. Activated Premium activates immediately after confirmation. Reopen /premium to see the new plan and expiry date. ## Promo codes Apply one before paying — it changes the price immediately: Promo Codes. ## Referral days Earned referral days are separate from a paid plan and are activated from the referral menu: Activate Days. ## If the price looks different The in-bot checkout is authoritative. Prices can vary by region and by plan length; the screen before payment is the final word. Related: Telegram Stars, Premium Status, Failed Payment.

Q: Can I switch plans later?
A: Yes. Buy the plan you want when the current one ends, or renew early with another duration; the new period extends access.

## Payments
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/payment.html

Premium is paid in Telegram Stars — Telegram's in-app currency. No cards, no external checkout, no stored payment details. ## What renews • Monthly — a Stars subscription, renews every 30 days until cancelled. • 3-month, 6-month, yearly — one-time purchases. They do not auto-renew; you choose again when they end. ## Where to check ⭐ Premium / /premium shows plan, status and expiry. Stars purchases also appear in Telegram's own Stars settings. ## Related Telegram Stars, Confirmation, Payment Status, Failed Payment, Refunds.

## Telegram Stars
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/payment_stars.html

Telegram Stars are Telegram's in-app currency, bought inside Telegram itself. The bot only requests the amount. ## Pay 1. /premium → choose a plan. 2. Tap ⭐ Telegram Stars . 3. Confirm in the native payment sheet. 4. Return to the bot; Premium activates immediately. ## Renewal rules • Monthly: auto-renews every 30 days. Cancel from the Premium menu; access continues to the end of the paid period. • 3/6-month and yearly: one-time. No auto-renew, no surprise charge. ## Refunds Stars purchases are final under Telegram's rules, and Premium is non-refundable once it has been delivered. The only exception is non-delivery . See Refunds. ## If nothing happens Wait two minutes, reopen /premium , then check your Stars balance. If you were charged and Premium is still off after five minutes, contact support with the transaction ID: Confirmation. Related: Payments, Cancel Premium.

## Crypto
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/payment_crypto.html

Crypto payment is not available . The CryptoBot option was retired, and any crypto buttons that still appear only show a "Stars only" notice. ## What to use Telegram Stars — choose any plan in /premium and confirm the invoice. It is instant and needs no external wallet. ## If you saw a crypto invoice before Those invoices are no longer valid. Start a new purchase from /premium . Do not send funds to an old address; the bot cannot credit them. Related: Telegram Stars, Payments.

## Currencies
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/payment_currencies.html

The product is priced in Stars. Telegram converts the displayed price into your local currency where it shows one, using its own rates. ## Where the final price appears In the payment sheet, before you confirm. That amount is the authoritative one; the website and help pages cannot know your regional Stars price. ## No hidden charges The bot does not add fees. Telegram's own terms may apply taxes or store rules depending on your platform. Related: Telegram Stars, Buy Premium.

## Pay Invoice
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/payment_invoice_pay.html

An invoice is the payment request Telegram shows when you choose a plan. ## Pay it Open the invoice message → Pay → confirm in the native sheet. Premium activates after confirmation. ## Expired invoice Invoices can expire. Do not try to reuse an old one — open /premium and start a fresh purchase. ## Wrong plan? Cancel the invoice and choose the plan you actually want. Paying an old invoice buys the plan it was created for. Related: Telegram Stars, Failed Payment.

## Confirmation
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/payment_confirm.html

Normally Premium activates within seconds of the payment sheet closing. ## If it does not 1. Wait 2–3 minutes — Telegram occasionally confirms late. 2. Reopen /premium to refresh the status. 3. Check your Stars balance for the purchase. 4. If five minutes pass, contact support with your user ID, plan and transaction ID. ## Do not pay twice A double charge takes manual work to refund. If you are unsure whether the first payment went through, check the status before buying again. Related: Failed Payment, Premium Troubleshooting.

## Payment Status

Use it when support asks for a transaction ID. ## Status meanings • Active — Premium works. • Cancelled — no renewal, access until the period ends. • Expiring — inside the reminder window. • Pending — payment not confirmed yet. ## Apply Promo

The discount is reflected in the invoice immediately. Codes are case-sensitive and single-use per account. ## If it fails • Invalid — check spelling and case. • Expired — the campaign ended. • Already used — one use per account. Related: Promo Codes, Buy Premium.

## Failed Payment
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/payment_failed.html

## Common causes • Not enough Stars in the balance. • The payment sheet was closed or interrupted. • A store-level billing hiccup (rapid retries make it worse). • An expired invoice. ## What to do 1. Check your Stars balance. 2. Wait a minute, open /premium and start a fresh invoice. 3. Never retry the exact same expired invoice. ## Charged but not activated Contact support with the receipt and transaction ID. Do not buy again first: duplicates are refunded manually and take longer. Related: Confirmation, Refunds, Premium Troubleshooting.

## Trial
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/premium_trial.html

Fast Scheduler does not run a standing free trial of Premium. Trial access appears in three ways: • Promo bonuses — codes that grant days or a discount. See Promo Codes. • Referral days — earned by inviting channel owners: Referral Rewards. • Occasional campaigns — announced in the bot. Trial and referral Premium behave exactly like paid Premium for their duration: limits are raised and features unlock. When the days end, the normal expiry process applies. ## Signature trial (different thing) The signature feature has its own one-time free trial for Free accounts. It is separate from Premium trials and is consumed once. Related: Premium Expiry, Welcome to Premium.

## Welcome to Premium
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/premium_welcome.html

Your limits are already raised — no restart needed. ## Check what changed • /premium — plan and expiry. • 📢 Channels — add up to 3. • 🤖 Bots — connect up to 3. • 💾 Media Storage — more boxes and video. • ⚙️ Settings → 📝 Signature — create a footer. ## Good first moves 1. Connect the second and third channels you have been holding back. 2. Create a signature so every post carries your handle. 3. Try multi-channel targeting on the next announcement. 4. Open 📊 Statistics and look at the leaderboard. 5. Make a protected backup with /backup . ## Manage it Cancel, renew or apply a promo any time from /premium . Related: Premium Features, Buy Premium.

## Promo Codes
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/promocode.html

Promo codes are campaign codes: a discount, extra months, or trial days. ## Redeem a discount 1. /premium → choose a plan. 2. On the payment screen tap Apply promo code . 3. Send the code. The price updates immediately. The code stays attached to the purchase for its duration and can be removed before paying. ## Rules • Case-sensitive. • One use per account. • May have an expiry date. • Some codes apply to specific plans only. ## Where codes come from Official announcements and seasonal promotions. Codes shared by strangers may be fake or already used; the bot will refuse them. Related: Apply Promo, Trial.

## Cancel Premium
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/premium_cancel.html

Cancelling stops the next charge. It does not cut access immediately. ## How 1. /premium → ❌ Cancel Premium . 2. Optionally choose a reason. 3. Confirm with ✅ Yes, Cancel Premium . ## What happens • Monthly: auto-renew turns off; Premium stays active until the period ends. • Prepaid 3/6-month and yearly: nothing to cancel — they never auto-renew; they simply end. ## Changed your mind? Open /premium and buy a plan again; Premium is restored immediately. If you cancelled during a paid period, buying again starts a new period. ## After the period ends The expiry pipeline begins with a grace period and a keep-selection: Premium Expiry. Related: Premium Status, Renew.

Q: Do I lose my data when I cancel?
A: No. Cancelling only stops renewal. Data is preserved through the expiry pipeline, and nothing is deleted on day one.

## Premium Status
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/premium_status.html

/premium shows: • plan (monthly, 3-month, 6-month, yearly, referral); • status (active, cancelled, expiring, pending); • expiry date; • auto-renew state; • your user ID for support. ## What the states mean • Active — full access. • Cancelled — no renewal; access until expiry. • Expiring — inside the reminder window (7, 3 and 1 day). • Pending — a payment is being confirmed. ## If it looks wrong Reopen the menu to refresh. If it still disagrees with your Stars receipt, contact support with the transaction ID. Related: Payment Status, Premium Expiry.

## Premium Expiry
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/premium_expiry.html

Nothing is deleted on the day Premium ends. The bot runs a staged pipeline so you can choose what matters. ## Before expiry Reminders at 7, 3 and 1 days left. ## Day 0 — choose what to keep A menu appears: keep up to 1 channel, 1 sender bot, 1 recurring message and one storage box. You can change the choice for the next few days. ## Days 1–2 — everything still works All channels keep publishing while you decide. ## Day 3 — final warning and a backup The bot warns you and sends an automatic .fsback backup of your data. ## Day 4 — non-kept channels stop Messages to channels you did not keep stop sending. Your kept channel continues normally. Scheduled messages for non-kept channels can still be exported. ## Day 17 — non-kept storage boxes Storage boxes you did not keep are deleted. Choose the box to keep before this stage. ## Day 35 — disconnect Excess channels and bots are disconnected. Your kept data remains. ## Renew at any point Before the final disconnect, renewal restores everything automatically. After it, reconnect manually. ## Related Grace Period, Renew, Reactivate, Frozen Assets, Refunds.

Q: Will my scheduled posts be deleted?
A: No. They are preserved; sends to non-kept channels stop at day 4. You can export them and re-import after renewing.

Q: What is the automatic backup?
A: A plain .fsback file containing your data, sent on day 3 so you have a copy before the pipeline advances.

## Grace Period
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/premium_grace.html

The grace period is the window after expiry before limits are applied. ## During it • All channels keep publishing. • Nothing is frozen or deleted. • You can still change your keep-selection. • A renewal prompt offers pay again / change plan / cancel. ## Length Three days from expiry, with the day-3 warning marking the end. ## Renew inside it Premium is restored instantly and the pipeline is cancelled. No reconnect and no data loss. Related: Premium Expiry, Renew.

## Renew
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/premium_renew.html

Renewing restores full Premium, usually instantly. ## How 1. /premium . 2. Tap Pay Again or choose a plan. 3. Pay with Stars. ## What is recovered • Before day 4 — everything, nothing was limited yet. • Between day 4 and day 35 — frozen channels and bots are restored automatically. • After day 35 — excess channels and bots were disconnected; reconnect them manually. ## Auto-renew Monthly Stars plans renew automatically. Prepaid plans do not; renew manually before they end. Related: Reactivate, Premium Expiry.

## Frozen Assets
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/premium_freeze.html

When Premium ends, assets beyond the Free limits are frozen before anything is disconnected. Frozen means paused, not deleted. ## What freezes • Channels beyond 1 stop receiving messages after the grace period. • Their sender bots stop publishing. • Recurring messages beyond 1 pause. • Signatures are stripped from outgoing messages. • Storage boxes you did not keep are deleted later in the pipeline (day 17). ## What keeps working Your kept channel, its bot, its scheduled messages, your account, settings, language and help access. ## Unfreeze Renew Premium and everything frozen is restored — before the final disconnect, automatically. After it, reconnect the excess channels and bots manually. ## Choose what to keep The day-0 menu lets you pick the channel, bot, recurring rule and storage box to keep. You can change the choice until the pipeline advances. Related: Premium Expiry, Renew.

## Reactivate
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/premium_reactivate.html

Premium can be reactivated at any point, including after the final disconnect. ## Before the final disconnect Pay from /premium ; everything frozen is restored automatically. ## After it Subscribe again, then reconnect your excess channels and sender bots manually. The bot guides you through it. ## What survived Within the Free limits, nothing was deleted: your kept channel, up to 100 scheduled messages and one recurring message. Your account, settings and language were never touched. Related: Renew, Add a Channel, Connecting a Bot.

## Refunds
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/premium_refund.html

Premium is non-refundable once it has been delivered. The only case we refund is non-delivery , and such a request must reach us within 7 days of that payment . ## What is refunded • you paid and Premium was never activated; • the same period was charged twice. ## What is not refunded • changing your mind mid-period; • an accidental, forgotten or unwanted renewal; • a period you did not use; • cancelling after a renewal — cancellation stops the next charge only. ## How to request Email fastschedulebot@gmail.com with: • the transaction ID (Stars receipt or Settings → Payments); • your Telegram username; • the payment date and what did not arrive. Requests that are not about non-delivery, or that arrive more than 7 days after the payment, are declined. We acknowledge within 7 business days , and approved refunds return through Telegram's payment system. ## Stars rules Stars purchases are final under Telegram's own policy; the non-delivery rule above is the only exception. Related: Failed Payment, Cancel Premium.

## Premium Troubleshooting
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/premium_troubleshooting.html

## Paid but not active • Wait 2–3 minutes. • Reopen /premium . • Check the Stars balance for the purchase. • Still off after 5 minutes: contact support with user ID, plan and transaction ID. ## Reversed payment Premium is revoked automatically and the account may be restricted until resolved. Contact support with the receipt. ## Auto-renew did not charge Only monthly Stars plans auto-renew. Prepaid plans are one-time. If a monthly renewal failed, buy a plan manually to restore access. ## Cancel did not work Check the status line: Cancelled means renewal is off but access continues. If it still shows Active with auto-renew, contact support. Related: Confirmation, Premium Status.

## Referral Program
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/premium_referral.html

Invite another channel owner and both sides earn Premium days once they qualify. ## The rule 3 days per qualifying referral, up to 15 referrals (45 days). A referral qualifies when the invitee connects a channel and creates at least one message. ## Your link /referral , or 🎁 Referral Program (BETA) . It unlocks after your own account has a channel and at least one message. ## Activation Earned days are banked. Activate them from the referral menu; if you already pay, they wait until the paid period ends. ## Beta The program is in beta: reward rules may be tuned, but days already earned are safe. ## Referral Bonus
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/premium_welcome_bonus.html

Referral days are Premium days earned by inviting channel owners. They behave exactly like paid Premium while active. ## If you already pay Earned days stay in your balance until the paid period ends. Then activate them from the referral menu — they do not stack on top of a running paid period. ## If you are on Free Activate them when you need them. Days do not expire while banked. ## Limits 3 days per qualifying referral, up to 15 referrals (45 days). Referral Premium does not auto-renew and cannot be refunded. Related: Referral Rewards, Activate Days.

## Is Fast Scheduler Premium Worth It? An Honest Breakdown
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_premium_worth.html

Premium costs $6.83 a month (or $68.03 a year) and removes the ceiling on almost everything Free limits. Here is an honest map of who needs which part. What Premium changes, concretely 3 channels, 3 sender bots — run a network (main channel, announcements, chat-announcements mirror) from one account. Unlimited scheduled queue and unlimited sends — no 100-post queue, no monthly cap on any channel. Unlimited recurring rules — and they never expire; Free's single rule stops after 365 days. Bigger media : uploads to 100 MB, video to up to 50MB, 20 storage boxes with 500 items total and video allowed , plus 4K-photo handling and higher bitrate media that Free compresses harder. Signatures — a footer (credit, promo, hashtags) auto-appended to every post of a channel. Export &amp; Backup toolkit — .fsback / .fspback backups, JSON/CSV/TXT/RTF/ODT exports: own your content. Who does not need it One channel, a couple of posts a day, no video-heavy content — Free covers that indefinitely. Premium's first meaningful gate for such a setup would be the monthly send cap, and even that takes ~3+ posts/day to hit. Who feels the difference on day one Multi-channel admins — the 3×3 pairing is the headline feature. Video channels — 25MB → 50MB video and video-in-storage change the workflow. Anyone whose content is their business — backups and full exports are the difference between “my queue” and “my archive”. Automation lovers — unlimited recurring rules turn the bot into a true publishing engine. Terms worth knowing Premium attaches to your Telegram account, covers all your channels at once, and can be paid with Telegram Stars. Multi-month terms cost less per month (3/6-month discounts), and if something goes wrong the refund policy is linked in the footer — premium status is visible any time with /premium .

Q: Does Premium apply to all my channels or per channel?
A: Per account. One subscription unlocks the higher limits for every channel you connect while it is active.

Q: What happens to my schedules when Premium expires?
A: Nothing is deleted. Limits revert to Free: extra channels/bots beyond 1×1 stop scheduling until you disconnect them or renew, the queue cap applies again, and recurring rules beyond the first pause.

Q: Can I pay with Telegram Stars?
A: Yes — Stars are billed at the official rate and are currently the only payment method. The Premium menu always shows current prices.

## How to Pay for Fast Scheduler Premium (Stars and What Happens After)
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_pay_stars_crypto.html

Premium attaches to your Telegram account and covers every channel you connect while it is active. Payment lives in the bot's Premium menu and uses Telegram Stars only. Telegram Stars Stars are Telegram's in-app currency. The bot converts the USD price at the official rate and shows the exact Star amount before you confirm — buy Stars in Telegram if your balance is short, approve, and Premium activates the moment the invoice clears. Refunds of Stars purchases follow Telegram's own flow, which is also why the bot asks you to double-check the term before paying. Plan terms The monthly Stars plan renews automatically until cancelled. Prepaid 3-month, 6-month, and yearly plans are one-time purchases (with up-front 3/6-month discounts) and never auto-renew. Right after payment Premium flags appear instantly in the menus; /premium shows status and expiry date. If you paid but see no change: restart the bot with /start — status is refreshed on launch. Still stuck? /feedback with the payment date and method gets a human on it the same day. Terms, renewals, refunds Multi-month terms cost proportionally less (built-in 3/6-month discounts), and expiry is shown everywhere Premium matters. When a prepaid term ends, limits quietly return to Free — nothing is deleted. The refund policy is linked in the site footer; genuine failures (double payment, activation glitch) are refunded by support.

Q: Can I pay for a friend’s account?
A: Premium binds to the Telegram account that activates it. To gift Premium, have them open the Premium menu and pay there, or transfer Stars — the bot cannot attach Premium to a different account after payment.

Q: Will Premium renew automatically?
A: The monthly Stars plan renews automatically until cancelled. Prepaid 3-month, 6-month, and yearly plans never auto-renew — when one ends, limits revert to Free and you can extend any time from the Premium menu.

## Free vs Premium: Which Fast Scheduler Plan Fits Your Channel?
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_which_plan.html

Feature tables tell you what differs; this tells you when it matters . Four questions decide the plan. 1. How many channels do you run? One channel works great on Free (1 channel, 1 sender bot). Two or three channels — or plans to get there — is the cleanest Premium trigger: Premium pairs 3 channels with 3 sender bots from one account. 2. How much do you post? Multiply daily posts by 30. Under ~90 sends/month, Free's 100-per-channel cap rarely bites. A 3+/day cadence, or channels where every send counts (news, trading, drops), wants Premium's unlimited sends and queue. 3. Is your content video-heavy? Free uploads top out at 10 MB with video at up to 25MB, no video in Media Storage, and stronger compression. If your posts live on video, Premium's 100 MB uploads, up to 50MB video, and video-in-storage are not a luxury — they are the workflow. 4. Do you need backups, exports or signatures? The Export &amp; Backup toolkit ( .fsback archives, JSON/CSV exports) and auto-signatures are Premium-only. If the queue is your business — client channels, monetized content — backups stop being optional the first time you restructure a month of posts. The short version Stay Free if: one channel, ≤3 posts/day, text-and-photo content, no archive needs. Go Premium if: 2–3 channels, 3+ posts/day, video content, recurring automation beyond one rule, or you want backups and signatures. Either way : you can start Free and upgrade the moment a limit touches you — nothing you built on Free breaks when Premium ends.

Q: Can I try Premium and go back to Free?
A: Yes. On expiry, limits revert to Free and nothing is deleted — disconnect extra channels if you keep more than one, and the first recurring rule keeps running.

Q: Does Premium change how fast posts send?
A: Send speed is the same — Telegram delivery does not differ by plan. Premium removes quantity limits and media compression, not latency.

## How Do I Get a Refund on My Fast Scheduler Premium Purchase?
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_refund_how.html

Refunds are handled personally, not by a faceless form. If a purchase went wrong — a double charge, an accidental renewal, Premium that never activated — you write one email and a human sorts it out. Here is the whole procedure, step by step. What to send Email fastschedulebot@gmail.com with three things: Your transaction ID — Telegram shows it in the Stars payment confirmation and in Settings → Payments. Your Telegram username (or user ID) so the purchase can be matched to your account. The reason — one honest sentence is enough, plus the purchase date and the account or email used, where applicable. The 30-day window and what happens next Refund requests are accepted within 30 days of the charge. Requests are acknowledged within 7 business days , and approved refunds are returned through the original payment method — for Telegram Stars that means back to your Stars balance. Refunds are discretionary rather than guaranteed for every situation, which is exactly why a short, honest reason helps: accidental purchases and technical failures the team could not fix are the classic approved cases. Cancelling so you are not charged again Monthly Stars plans renew automatically until cancelled. You cancel inside the bot: open /premium → ❌ Cancel Premium . Cancelling stops future billing; the period you already paid for stays active until its end date, and Premium switches off at that boundary rather than mid-plan. The 3-month, 6-month and yearly packs are one-time purchases — they simply expire and never auto-charge. What not to do: chargebacks Opening a card or Apple/Google chargeback instead of emailing is treated as abuse: the account loses Premium immediately and the subscription fee is forfeited. Emailing first is always faster — most refund conversations end within a couple of messages. One more nuance: deleting your data or stopping use of the bot does not automatically refund anything, so if you want both, request the refund before asking for account deletion.

Q: How long does a Fast Scheduler refund take?
A: Requests are acknowledged within 7 business days. Once approved, Stars refunds return to your Telegram Stars balance; the total time depends on Telegram, typically a few days.

Q: Can I cancel Premium and keep it until the period ends?
A: Yes. Cancelling via /premium stops auto-renewal, and Premium stays active until the end of the paid period. Downgrade happens at that boundary, not immediately.

Q: I was charged twice. What do I do?
A: Email fastschedulebot@gmail.com with both transaction IDs and your Telegram username. Duplicate charges are the clearest refund case and are resolved quickly.

# Referrals

## Referrals
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/referral.html

The referral program rewards you for bringing other channel owners to Fast Scheduler. ## The deal Both sides earn 3 Premium days when an invitee connects a channel and creates at least one message. Up to 15 qualifying referrals — 45 days total. ## Your link 🎁 Referral Program (BETA) or /referral . It unlocks only after your own account has a connected channel and at least one scheduled message, so rewards go to real channel owners. ## How days work They are banked, not applied automatically. Activate them when you need Premium; if you already pay, they wait until the paid period ends. ## Beta Rules can be tuned while the program is in beta; days already earned are honored. ## Related How Referrals Work, Your Link, Referral Rewards, Activate Days, Rules, Abuse.

Q: Do I earn days for every person who opens the bot?
A: No. The invitee must connect a channel and create at least one message. Opening the bot alone earns nothing.

## How Referrals Work
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/referral_how.html

## 1. Unlock your link Connect a channel and schedule at least one message. Until then the referral menu explains the requirement and shows a lock. ## 2. Share it Copy the link and send it to a channel owner you know. The message they see explains the offer. ## 3. They qualify They open the bot from your link, connect a channel and create at least one message. Only then does the referral count. ## 4. Days are credited 3 days for you and 3 for them, recorded in the referral history. If you already have a paid plan, the days wait in your balance. ## 5. Activate Use the activate action in the referral menu when you want Premium. Days do not expire while banked. ## What does not count • opening the bot without connecting a channel; • connecting a channel without creating a message; • self-referral; • an account that was already referred. Related: Referral Rewards, Why Verification Is Required.

## Your Link
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/referral_link.html

Your referral link lives in 🎁 Referral Program (BETA) , /referral , and the Premium menu. ## Locked? The menu shows a lock until your account has a connected channel and at least one scheduled message. This prevents empty-account farming. ## Sharing the link 🔗 Send Referral Link sends a ready-made message you can forward; 🔗 Copy Link copies it. Share it in groups, DMs or your channel's admin chat. ## The link is personal It identifies your account. If it stops working, reopen /referral so the bot refreshes its state. Related: How Referrals Work, Why Verification Is Required.

## Share
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/referral_share.html

The referral menu can send or copy a prepared invitation. ## The prepared text It explains that both sides get Premium days and includes your link. You can forward it as-is or add your own context. ## Where it works • DMs with channel owners you know. • Admin chats of channels you collaborate with. • Communities where channel owners hang out — follow their rules about promotion. ## Where it does not Spamming unrelated groups gets the link reported and the account flagged. The program is small and beta; reputation matters. Related: Your Link, Abuse.

## Referral Rewards
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/referral_rewards.html

## The numbers • 3 Premium days per qualifying referral. • 15 qualifying referrals maximum. • 45 days total possible. Both the referrer and the invitee receive 3 days. ## When it counts After the invitee connects a channel and creates at least one message. The referral history shows pending and credited states. ## Using the days Activate them from the referral menu. If a paid plan is active, they wait until it ends. ## Beta The values can change while the program is in beta; days already credited are not reduced. Related: Activate Days, Your Referral Stats.

## Activate Days
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/referral_activate.html

Banked days do not tick down until you activate them. ## Activate Open 🎁 Referral Program → the activate action. The bot reports how many days were applied and the new expiry date. ## If a paid plan is active Activation is refused until the paid period ends; your balance is preserved. The menu shows the remaining balance. ## If activation fails • No days available — the balance is zero. • A paid plan is still running. • A technical error — retry once, then report it via feedback. Related: Referral Rewards, Referral Bonus.

## Your Referral Stats
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/referral_stats.html

The referral screen shows five numbers: • Referred users — how many accounts used your link and qualified. • Max referrals — the cap (15). • Earned days — total days credited. • Used days — days already activated. • Available days — the balance you can activate. ## Pending versus credited A referral is recorded when the link is used but credited only after the invitee connects a channel and creates a message. The list distinguishes the two states. ## Refreshing Reopen the menu after an invitee finishes setup; the numbers update. Related: Referral History, Detailed Stats.

## Referral History
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/referral_history.html

The history records what happened and when: • a referral was recorded; • a referral was credited (3 days); • days were activated; • a referral was rejected (self-referral, duplicate, abuse). ## Why it matters When a number looks wrong, the history shows whether the days were credited or are still pending. Support can use it to trace a ticket. ## Not a wallet The history is a log; the balance lives in the referral stats. Activated days appear on your Premium expiry date. Related: Your Referral Stats, Premium Status.

## Rules
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/referral_rules.html

1. The invitee must be new to the referral program — an account can be referred once. 2. They must connect a channel and create at least one message. 3. Self-referral is blocked. 4. One account per person; duplicate accounts are removed from the program. 5. The cap is 15 qualifying referrals (45 days). 6. Days are banked and activated manually. 7. Beta rules can be tuned; already-earned days are honored. 8. Abuse voids rewards and can restrict the account. Related: Abuse, Beta Program.

## Abuse
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/referral_fraud.html

Referral abuse is treated as account abuse. ## Examples • creating accounts to refer yourself; • inviting accounts that never connect a real channel; • trading referrals with the same people in a loop; • mass-spamming links in unrelated groups; • faking channel connections to trigger credit. ## Consequences Rewards are voided, days can be removed, and the account can be restricted from the program. Repeated abuse can affect access to Premium features. ## Reporting If someone spams your community with a referral link, report it via feedback with a screenshot and the link. Related: Rules, Send Feedback.

## Why Verification Is Required
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/referral_verify.html

A referral link unlocks only after your own account has a connected channel and at least one message. ## Why Without a bar, the program is trivial to farm: create accounts, click links, collect days. Requiring a real channel and a real scheduled post ties rewards to actual usage. ## What counts A connected channel with its sender bot and at least one scheduled or created message. Drafts that were never saved do not count. ## What it means for invitations Your invitee faces the same bar: they must connect a channel and create a message before either side earns. That is why the invitation text explains setup, not just the reward. ## If you think you qualify but the link is locked Check that the channel is still connected and that at least one message exists in the Message List. Reopen /referral to refresh. Related: How Referrals Work, Your Link.

## Beta Program
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/referral_beta.html

The referral program is in beta: it works, but the rules may be tuned. ## What can change • the number of days per referral; • the cap; • qualification details; • anti-abuse checks. ## What cannot change Days already credited are honored. Balances are not reduced retroactively. ## What beta means for you Report anything that looks wrong via feedback — a confusing rule, a referral that stayed pending after the invitee finished setup, or a credit that never arrived. Beta feedback shapes the final rules. Related: Rules, Send Feedback.

## How Crediting Works
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/referral_credit.html

A referral moves through three states. ## 1. Recorded Someone opened the bot from your link. The account is linked to you, but no days are credited yet. ## 2. Qualified The invitee connected a channel and created at least one message. This is the qualifying event. ## 3. Credited 3 days are added to both balances and the history records it. From here the days are safe. ## Why it can stay pending • the invitee never connected a channel; • the channel was connected but no message was created; • the account was already referred by someone else; • anti-abuse checks flagged the pair. ## Checking The detailed stats list shows pending versus credited. If a referral looks stuck after the invitee finished setup, report it with their username. Related: Detailed Stats, How Referrals Work.

## Detailed Stats
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/referral_stats_detail.html

The detailed view lists each referred account with its state. ## What each row shows • the referred user (name or ID); • whether the referral is pending or credited; • the days credited; • the date. ## Why a row is pending The invitee has not yet connected a channel or created a message. It can stay pending indefinitely; nothing is lost if they finish later. ## Privacy You see enough to recognise your invite, not the invitee's private data. Related: Your Referral Stats, Referral History.

# Limits

## Limits
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/limits.html

Plans differ in five numbers: pending scheduled messages, sends per month, recurring messages, channels and sender bots. Storage and media size add a second group. ## Free • 100 pending scheduled messages per channel • 100 sent messages per channel per month • 1 recurring message • 1 channel, 1 sender bot • 1 storage box with 100 items • uploads up to 10 MB, video up to up to 25MB ## Premium • unlimited pending and sent messages • unlimited recurring messages • 3 channels, 3 sender bots • 20 boxes with 500 items • uploads up to 100 MB, video up to up to 50MB ## How counting works Limits are per channel and shared by all admins of that channel. The monthly counter counts messages actually sent and resets on the 1st. `/stats` shows current usage. ## Fixed limits Some things cannot be raised by any plan: one sender bot per channel, anonymous polls only in channels (Telegram's rule), and the maximum album size of 10 items. ## Related Free Plan Limits, Premium Plan Limits, Raise Limits.

Q: Is there a daily send limit?
A: No. Free has a monthly cap per channel and no daily cap. Premium removes the monthly cap too.

## Free Plan Limits
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/limits_free.html

• Channels: 1 • Sender bots: 1 • Pending scheduled messages: up to 100 per channel • Sends per month: 100 per channel • Recurring messages: 1 • Media upload: up to 10 MB • Video: up to up to 25MB • Media storage: 1 box, 100 items, no video • Statistics: averages; leaderboards and reports are Premium • Backups: full export and protected backups are Premium The monthly counter counts sent messages and resets on the 1st. `/stats` shows the current usage. There is no daily cap. Related: Limits, Monthly Send Limit, Compare Plans.

## Premium Plan Limits
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/limits_premium.html

• Channels: 3 • Sender bots: 3 • Pending scheduled messages: unlimited • Sends: unlimited • Recurring messages: unlimited • Media upload: up to 100 MB • Video: up to up to 50MB • Media storage: 20 boxes, 500 items, video up to up to 50MB • 4K media: supported • Statistics: full reports, leaderboards, more detail • Backups: full export and protected backups ## Still capped One sender bot per channel, 10 items per album, anonymous polls only in channels. These are Telegram constraints, not plan limits. ## If Premium lapses Your data is kept. Channels and bots beyond the free allowances become frozen until you choose what to keep or renew: Frozen Assets. Related: Limits, Premium Features, Compare Plans.

## Monthly Send Limit
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/limit_daily.html

There is no daily limit. Free accounts have a monthly send allowance per channel: 100 messages. ## What counts Messages actually sent to the channel. Editing or deleting a queued post does not consume the counter; publishing does. ## Resets On the 1st of the next calendar month. It also clears when Premium becomes active for the channel. ## What happens at the cap Further sends are refused with a limit message and an upgrade prompt. Queued posts remain queued; they will not publish until the counter resets or the plan changes. ## Checking usage `/stats` shows the current usage for the channel. Per-channel numbers are also visible on the channel card. ## Premium Unlimited sends. No monthly counter. Related: Free Plan Limits, Raise Send Limits.

## Scheduled Limit
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/limit_scheduled.html

Free accounts can keep up to 100 scheduled messages pending per channel. Premium is unlimited. ## What counts Every queued one-time message for that channel, regardless of which admin created it. Sent and deleted messages no longer count. ## What does not count Recurring rules have their own limit (Recurring Limit). Media storage and drafts are separate. ## At the cap New scheduling is refused with the limit message and an upgrade prompt. Options: • delete posts you no longer need (Delete Messages); • schedule the next batch after the current one sends; • upgrade for an unlimited queue. ## Checking usage `/stats` shows pending counts; the Message List shows them per channel. Related: Limits, Raise Limits.

## Recurring Limit
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/limit_recurring.html

Free allows 1 recurring message. Premium is unlimited. ## What counts Each active rule, including duplicates created with /dub . Paused rules still count: they occupy a slot until deleted. ## Expiry Recurring rules expire after 365 days . An expired rule stops producing sends and should be recreated if the series continues. ## At the cap Creating another rule is refused with an upgrade prompt. Delete an old rule or upgrade. ## Managing 📋 Message List → Recurring messages : preview, edit, pause, resume, delete. Related: Recurring Messages, Pause & Resume.

## Channel Limit
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/limit_channels.html

Free connects 1 channel. Premium allows up to 3 . ## Each channel needs • the bot as an administrator with Post Messages; • its own sender bot, also an admin; • optionally its own time zone, signature and admins. ## Adding past the limit The connect action is limit-checked and shows an upgrade prompt. Nothing is lost; the new channel simply is not added. ## Downgrading If Premium ends and you have more channels than Free allows, the excess channels become frozen until you choose what to keep: Frozen Assets. ## Counting Channels are counted per account, not per admin. Co-admins do not add channels to the owner's account. Related: Add a Channel, Raise Channels.

## Sender Bot Limit
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/limit_bots.html

Free allows 1 sender bot. Premium allows 3 . ## Two rules 1. A bot serves exactly one channel. 2. The number of bots is capped by your plan. So a Free account with one channel and one bot is at both limits at once. ## At the cap Connecting another bot is refused. Remove an unused bot or upgrade. Removing a bot pauses that channel's queue but keeps the posts. ## Sharing A bot cannot be shared between accounts. Co-admins use the owner's bot through the channel's admin permissions. Related: Add a Sender Bot, Remove a Sender Bot, Raise Bots.

## Media Limit
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/limit_media.html

Every uploaded file must fit the plan's size cap. ## Limits • Max media size: 10 MB on Free, 100 MB on Premium. • Video in a post: up to 25MB on Free, up to 50MB on Premium. • Video in storage: No on Free, up to 50MB on Premium. • 4K sources: — on Free, ✓ on Premium. ## Compression Photos, videos, audio and voice are compressed for delivery. Free compresses harder; Premium keeps more detail. Documents are never compressed. ## If a file is refused The bot rejects it at upload with the applicable limit. Compress the file, trim the video, or upgrade. Waiting does not change the cap. ## Storage vs post limits Storage has its own item count and per-file caps; a file that fits a post may still be too large for storage on Free (video is not stored at all). Related: Media Compression & Retention, Supported Content Types.

## Storage Limit
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/limit_storage_detail.html

Media Storage has three limits: boxes, items and video. • Free: 1 box, 100 items total, no stored video. • Premium: 20 boxes, 500 items total, video up to up to 50MB. ## What counts as an item Each stored file — one photo, one document, one video. Moving or copying an item to another box creates another item, which counts again. ## At the cap Adding more is refused with a quota message. Delete unused items, empty a box, or upgrade. ## Storage menu The storage screen shows current usage and the nearest limit. Boxes can be archived or deleted; deleting a box deletes its items. Related: Quota, Storage Boxes, Raise Storage.

## Raise Limits
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/limit_increase.html

Most limits are raised by Premium. A few are fixed by design. ## Premium raises • channels: 1 → 3 • sender bots: 1 → 3 • scheduled and recurring messages: capped → unlimited • monthly sends: 100 → unlimited • media: 10 MB → 100 MB; video up to 25MB → up to 50MB • storage: 1 → 20 boxes, 100 → 500 items ## Fixed by design • one sender bot per channel; • 10 items per album; • anonymous polls only in channels; • Telegram's own message and caption length limits. ## How to upgrade /premium or ⭐ Upgrade to Premium . Payment is in Telegram Stars; the checkout price is authoritative. Promo codes are applied in the same flow. Related: Buy Premium, Compare Plans.

## Raise Channels
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/limit_raise_channels.html

Free connects 1 channel; Premium up to 3. Each additional channel needs its own sender bot and its own admin grants. After upgrading, add channels from 📢 Channels → 📢 Connect Channel . Going from 1 to 3 is the most common upgrade reason. Before you do, check that you have the time to fill three queues — an empty channel reads worse than one good channel. Related: Channel Limit, Buy Premium.

Q: How do I add more channels?
A: Upgrade to Premium to add more channels. Free plan allows 1 channel. See Premium for current limits.

## Raise Bots
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/limit_raise_bots.html

Free allows 1 sender bot; Premium 3. Because each bot serves one channel, the bot cap follows the channel cap. After upgrading, create bots in @BotFather and connect them from 🤖 Bots → 🔑 I Have a Token , then promote each in its channel. Unused bots still occupy slots — remove them if you are not using them. Related: Sender Bot Limit, Add a Sender Bot.

Q: How do I raise my sender bot limit?
A: Upgrade to Premium to connect more sender bots. Free plan allows 1 bot. See Premium for current limits.

## Raise Send Limits
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/limit_raise_daily.html

Free sends up to 100 messages per channel per month. There is no daily cap. Premium removes the monthly counter entirely. If you consistently hit the cap mid-month, Premium is the only way to raise it. Note that the cap counts sends, not creations: deleting queued posts before they publish does not consume it. Related: Monthly Send Limit, Premium Features.

Q: How many messages can I send per month?
A: Free plan: 100 sent messages per channel per month. Premium: unlimited. There is no daily cap on either plan. See Plan Limits for exact numbers.

## Raise Storage
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/limit_raise_storage.html

Free keeps 1 box with 100 items and no video. Premium raises this to 20 boxes and 500 items, with video up to up to 50MB. Upgrading is worth it if you reuse creatives across weeks; if your library fits in one small box, Free is enough. After upgrading, the new limits apply immediately — existing boxes do not need to be recreated. Related: Storage Limit, Storage on Premium.

Q: Can I raise my storage limit?
A: Yes — Premium increases storage box count and total items. See Media Storage for the current limits.

## What Do I Get With Fast Scheduler for Free? (Exact Limits)
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_free_limits.html

Free is a real plan, not a trial — it never expires and has no daily caps. Here is exactly what you get, with numbers you can plan around. The numbers 1 channel with 1 sender bot . Up to 100 scheduled messages pending at once — your working queue. As posts go out, space frees up; this is not a monthly allowance. 100 sent messages per channel per calendar month — the actual sending quota. Resets on the 1st. 1 recurring message — one repeating rule (daily, weekly, every N hours…). Recurring rules on Free expire after 365 days and need re-confirming. Media Storage: 1 box with 100 items , no video in storage. Uploads up to 10 MB , videos up to 25MB. What “100/month per channel” means in practice If you post 3 times a day, that is ~90 posts a month — Free covers a light daily cadence on one channel. Posting 5+ times a day, or running several channels, is where Premium starts to make sense. The counter counts sends by the sender bot ; edits, previews and deleted schedules are free. There is no daily cap Older versions of the bot had daily limits; they are gone. On Free you can schedule and send every single day — the only quotas are the pending-queue size and the monthly send count. Check both any time with /stats . Hitting a limit gracefully The queue limit blocks new schedules, never deletes old ones; the monthly cap pauses sends until the 1st (the bot tells you). Both warn you in advance with clear messages and a one-tap upgrade path. Nothing is silently dropped.

Q: Do unused sends carry over to next month?
A: No. The monthly counter resets to zero on the 1st; unused sends do not roll over. The pending-queue space is also not a quota to “use up” — it just caps how far ahead you can stockpile.

Q: Is the free plan time-limited or feature-crippled?
A: It never expires. Scheduling, recurring, statistics, search and the calendar all work on Free. Premium removes quantity limits and adds the Export/Backup toolkit, signatures and bigger media.

Q: How do I check my current usage?
A: Send /stats. It shows your queue size, monthly sends, recurring rules and storage at a glance.

# Time Zone

## Time Zone
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/timezone.html

Time zones decide what the numbers in your schedule mean. Get this right once and scheduling becomes predictable. ## Two levels • Account zone — the default, set in ⚙️ Settings → 🕐 Time Zone or with /timezone . • Channel zone — optional per channel, set on the channel card. It overrides the account zone for that channel. ## How a date is read A scheduled 19:00 is interpreted in the channel's zone. If the channel has no own zone, the account zone applies. ## Detection During the tutorial and in the time zone screen you can send a city, your current time, or a location. The bot proposes a zone and you confirm. If detection fails, pick from the list. ## Related Set Time Zone, Auto Detect, Automatic Time Zone, Supported Zones, Examples, Wrong-time troubleshooting.

Q: Does changing the zone move already queued posts?
A: No. Queued posts keep the moment they were created for. New schedules use the new zone; review the calendar after a change.

## Set Time Zone
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/timezone_set.html

## Account zone ⚙️ Settings → 🕐 Time Zone , or /timezone . Choose from the list, search a city, or let the bot detect it. ## Channel zone 📢 Channels → open the channel → tap 🕐 Time Zone: … → pick the zone. This is what a scheduled date uses for that channel. ## Detection inputs • a city name ( London , New York ); • your current time ( 15:30 ); • your location; • the manual list ( Europe/Berlin , America/New_York ). ## After changing New posts use the new zone. Existing queued posts keep their original moment; check the calendar and edit if needed. ## What to set Set the account zone to where you actually are, and each channel's zone to where its audience reads. A channel for another country should not inherit your zone. Related: Time Zone, Scheduling Time Zone.

## Auto Detect
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/timezone_detect.html

Detection saves scrolling through a long list. ## Options • City — send London . The bot proposes the matching zone; confirm. • Current time — send 15:30 . The bot compares it with UTC and proposes a zone. • Location — send your location; the zone is derived from it. ## When it fails The bot says it could not detect the zone. That is a miss, not a lockout: try a larger city, send the current time, or pick from the list manually. ## Accuracy City detection is reliable for well-known cities; ambiguous names may resolve to another country. Always confirm the proposed zone before saving. Related: Set Time Zone, Automatic Time Zone.

## Automatic Time Zone
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/timezone_auto.html

Automatic detection uses your shared location once to pick the nearest zone. ## How it works • You share a location (not live tracking). • The bot picks the closest zone, for example Europe/Berlin . • You confirm; the value is stored in your settings. ## When to override • You travel often and schedule for your home audience. • You live near a border and the nearest zone is not the one you think in. • The channel targets another country — set the channel zone instead. ## Privacy The location is used to derive the zone and is not published. You can change the zone manually at any time. Related: Set Time Zone, Your Data.

## Supported Zones
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/timezone_list.html

The bot uses standard IANA time zone names: Europe/London , America/New_York , Asia/Kolkata , Australia/Sydney and so on. ## Coverage All standard zones from UTC−12 to UTC+14, including 30- and 45-minute offsets such as India (UTC+5:30) and Nepal (UTC+5:45). ## Finding yours Use the search field in the time zone screen with a city, country or abbreviation. The bot shows the current local time for the match so you can verify. ## Daylight saving IANA zones include DST rules. A post at 09:00 stays at 09:00 local time across a DST change — which is usually what you want. Related: Examples, Set Time Zone.

## Examples
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/timezone_examples.html

• UTC+0 — London, Lisbon, Reykjavik • UTC+1 — Berlin, Paris, Rome, Lagos • UTC+2 — Cairo, Johannesburg, Athens • UTC+3 — Moscow, Istanbul, Nairobi • UTC+4 — Dubai, Baku • UTC+5:30 — India (Mumbai, Delhi) • UTC+7 — Bangkok, Jakarta • UTC+8 — Beijing, Singapore, Manila • UTC+9 — Tokyo, Seoul • UTC+10 — Sydney, Melbourne • UTC−3 — São Paulo, Buenos Aires • UTC−5 — New York, Toronto • UTC−8 — Los Angeles, Vancouver Search the city in the picker; the bot resolves the zone and shows the current local time. Related: Supported Zones, Set Time Zone.

## Why Did My Post Go Out at the Wrong Time? Time Zones, Explained Simply
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_timezones.html

“I scheduled 9:00 and it posted at 12:00” — before anything else, check which clock the number 9:00 belongs to. Fast Scheduler schedules posts in a time zone , and the zone that matters is the one set for the channel, not the one on your watch. How the bot decides “when 9:00 is” Every channel has a time zone setting . When you schedule 9:00, the bot stores 9:00 in the channel's zone and converts it to UTC behind the scenes. If the zone is UTC (the default) and you are in, say, New York, your 9:00 local is 13:00 or 14:00 UTC — the post will “move” by 4–5 hours from your point of view. Set the channel's zone to your own city once, and from then on 9:00 means your 9:00, every time. The daylight-saving trap Zones that observe DST shift twice a year. A post scheduled for 9:00 in March may land at 8:00 or 10:00 relative to the wall clock in November, depending on how the zone handles the shift. If your audience notices a one-hour drift in spring or autumn, that is why. The schedule did not break — the zone's definition of 9:00 changed. Reschedule around the shift week if you post at a strict local hour. Checking and fixing the zone Open Time Zone in the bot (or /timezone ), pick the channel, and choose the city/zone that matches your audience — the list uses proper zone names like Europe/Berlin , so DST is handled by the same rules your phone uses. Upcoming posts keep their stored times; only new schedules use the new zone, so double-check anything queued for the same day you change it. Quick diagnosis table Off by a whole number of hours, constant — wrong zone set for the channel. Off by one hour, only in spring/autumn — DST shift; the zone is working correctly. Off by a few minutes, growing over weeks — rare; send /feedback with two examples.

Q: Does changing the time zone move my scheduled posts?
A: No. Existing posts keep their stored times; the new zone applies to schedules you create afterwards. Verify the next few posts after changing the zone.

Q: What time zone should I pick for an international audience?
A: Pick the zone of your largest audience segment, or UTC if you think in UTC. Consistency matters more than the specific zone.

## Why Was My Scheduled Telegram Post Published at the Wrong Time?
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_timezone_wrong_time.html

When a scheduled message fires at an unexpected hour, the clock itself is almost never wrong — the time zone used to interpret &ldquo;9:00&rdquo; is. Fast Scheduler resolves every time through two settings, and a mismatch between them explains nearly every &ldquo;wrong time&rdquo; report. The two clocks: user time zone and channel time zone Your user time zone — set once via /timezone and used whenever you type a time into the scheduling conversation. Each channel&rsquo;s own time zone — set per channel, because the audience that reads the channel may live in a different zone than you do. Schedules for that channel are interpreted in the channel&rsquo;s zone. If your user zone says UTC+3 but the channel zone says UTC+0, a message you schedule for 9:00 is stored as 9:00 channel time — and lands six hours earlier than you visually expected. Check both: /timezone for yourself, and the channel settings inside the bot for the channel. Daylight saving time Zones with DST shift by one hour twice a year. Fast Scheduler stores schedules in absolute terms, so a post that crossed a DST boundary can appear to &ldquo;move&rdquo; by an hour. If you live in a DST zone and noticed the shift right after the clocks changed, re-check the channel&rsquo;s zone — picking a zone like Europe/Berlin (which follows DST rules) versus a fixed UTC offset produces different results across the year. Quick diagnosis checklist Off by a round number of hours (3, 4, 6…) → time-zone mismatch; fix the channel time zone or your user zone. Off by exactly one hour right after late March / late October → DST; confirm the zone uses the right convention. AM/PM confusion — schedule with the 24-hour clock (14:00, not 2:00) to remove ambiguity entirely. Around midnight — double-check you scheduled the day you meant; the date picker always shows the resolved local date and time for final confirmation before saving. One more tip: the confirmation screen before saving shows the exact send time. Reading that single line — not the input you typed — is the ground truth for when the post will fire.

Q: Does each Telegram channel have its own time zone in Fast Scheduler?
A: Yes. Every channel carries its own time zone, and schedules for that channel are interpreted in the channel zone. Your personal /timezone setting applies to how you enter times while chatting with the bot.

Q: How do I change the time zone of a channel?
A: Open the bot, go to the channel settings, and set its time zone there. Existing scheduled messages keep their stored times, so new schedules pick up the change immediately.

# Language

## Language
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/language.html

Language changes the bot's interface, not your content. ## Available • English • Russian • Spanish English is the fallback when a translation is missing. ## Where to change it 🌐 Language in the menu, or /language . The change is immediate and stored per Telegram account, so it follows you across devices. ## Sync Fast Scheduler, the support bot and @SetDate_bot share your preference. When you change it in one, the others offer to sync. ## What it does not do • Your channel posts are never translated. • Commands such as /schedule work in any language. • Dates and times still follow the selected time zone, not the language. ## Related Change Language, Languages, Sync Across Bots, Missing Language?.

Q: How do I disable language sync?
A: Go to Language on the main menu → tap Disable Language Sync . This stops cross-bot sync offers between Fast Scheduler and @SetDate_bot, and turns off Telegram language detection. You can re-enable it anytime from the same menu.

Q: How do I hide language sync notifications?
A: Premium feature. Go to Language on the main menu → tap Hide Notifications . Sync still works but you won't see the notification popups. Toggle it back to show notifications again.

## Change Language
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/language_change.html

1. Tap 🌐 Language in the main menu, or send /language . 2. Pick a language. 3. The bot confirms and redraws the menu immediately. ## If the message is unreadable Send /language — the command is language-independent — and pick English to reset. ## What changes Buttons, prompts and help articles in both bots. Your scheduled posts, signatures and channel content stay exactly as written. Related: Language, Sync Across Bots.

## Languages
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/language_list.html

The interface is available in: • English ( en ) • Russian ( ru ) • Spanish ( es ) English is always available and fills any missing translation. The language menu shows the current list, so check there if a language was added recently. ## Reporting a bad translation Send feedback from @FastSchedulerSupport_bot with the screen and the wording. Translations improve from reports. Related: Change Language, Missing Language?.

## Sync Across Bots
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/language_sync.html

Your language preference is account-level and shared by the bots. ## What syncs Fast Scheduler, @FastSchedulerSupport_bot and @SetDate_bot. Change it in one and the others offer to apply it. ## The prompt The other bot sends a short message asking whether to switch. Confirm to apply, or ignore it to keep the other bot's current language. ## Why it can differ Each bot can hold its own value until you confirm a sync, which is useful if you read support in one language and work in another. Related: Language, Change Language.

## Missing Language?
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/language_add.html

If your language is not offered, English remains fully usable. ## Check first Open the language menu — it lists every currently supported language. New languages appear there without an app update. ## Request one Send feedback from @FastSchedulerSupport_bot (Send Feedback) and name the language. Requests are prioritised by demand. ## Meanwhile • Commands work in English regardless of the interface language. • Your content is never translated. • Dates accept numeric formats that do not depend on language. Related: Languages, Request a Feature.

## Language Help
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/language_help.html

Wrong language? Send /language and pick another. The command itself is language-independent, so it always works. Broken or untranslated menu? Send feedback with the screen name and the exact text; missing keys fall back to English in the meantime. Language follows your Telegram account, so switching devices keeps the choice. Related: Change Language, Send Feedback.

# Backup, Export & Import

## Backup, Export & Import
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/data.html

Everything you scheduled lives on the bot's server, not in your phone. Export gives you a readable file of it, Backup gives you one file that can rebuild the account, and Import puts a file back in. What each one is for • Export — a copy you can read, print, or edit in a spreadsheet. Cannot rebuild the account by itself. • Backup — a complete snapshot (.fsback / .fspback) that can be restored with Overwrite or Add. • Import — takes a backup, a message list, a spreadsheet, or a SetDate schedule and turns it into scheduled messages. Where it is Main menu → Data . The screen has two buttons: Export and Import . Commands /export , /backup and /import open the same screens. Do this before big changes Take a backup before a mass delete, a channel move, or a long vacation. See Create a Backup and Importing Your Data. The four management tools • Message List — browse per channel, preview, edit, delete. • Search — find a post by keyword. • Calendar — the month at a glance. • Statistics — counts, sends and per-channel numbers.

## Export
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/export.html

Screen: Main menu → Data → Export , or /export . Step 1 — tick what to export The first screen is a checklist of categories with a Select All toggle. Everything is ticked when you open it. Typical categories: scheduled messages, recurring messages, connected channels and bots, settings and time zones, storage items, and promo/referral data. Tick the ones you want and continue. Optional — narrow to channels If the checklist offers a channel scope, you can export only the channels you choose instead of everything. This is what makes a per-channel handover file possible. Step 2 — pick a format • .txt — plain readable text. • .csv — spreadsheet, opens in Excel or Google Sheets. • .json — structured data for tools and scripts. • .rtf / .odt — word-processor documents. • .fsback / .fspback — a full backup instead of a readable file (the .fspback one is password protected). Readable formats fit messages . A mixed selection (channels, settings, storage) needs a backup format, so the bot offers .fsback there. If your selection includes tokens , the only option is the password-protected .fspback . Step 3 — the bot sends the file The document arrives in the chat. Save it somewhere you control. Export is a Premium feature The Data screen is always visible, but producing a file requires Premium. On Free the screen shows the upgrade prompt. Need a restorable snapshot instead of a readable file? See Backup. Need to put a file back? Importing Your Data.

## Export Data
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/export_data.html
