From Data → Export (or /export ) you choose categories, not individual messages: • Scheduled messages — content, times, channels. • Recurring messages — the rules and the content. • Channels & bots — which channels are connected and which sender bot posts there. • Settings — language, time zone and similar preferences. • Storage items — the media library index. • Promo / referral — your invite progress and rewards. Tick everything for a full snapshot, or only a few categories for a small file. The selection is remembered while the screen is open; Select All flips the whole list at once. Formats and file handling are covered in Formats and Export a Chat.

## Export a Chat
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/export_chat.html

A per-channel export is useful when you hand a channel to a teammate, archive a finished campaign, or move one channel's plan into a spreadsheet. How 1. Open Data → Export . 2. In the channel scope step, clear All channels and tick just the channel you need. Ticking none blocks the export; the bot asks you to pick at least one. 3. Choose a readable format ( .txt , .csv , .json , .rtf , .odt ). 4. The file lists each message with its time and content. In a sender-bot context you only see channels where your role has the export permission — see Sender Bot Permissions. Images are not embedded. An export is text plus references, so the file stays small; to move real media, use Storage Boxes or a full backup.

## Formats
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/export_formats.html

Readable formats (messages) • .txt — plain text, one message after another. • .csv — spreadsheet with channel, date/time, content and media columns. • .json — full structured records, for scripts and tools. • .rtf — rich text for Word and most editors. • .odt — open document format for LibreOffice. Backup formats (everything) • .fsback — full snapshot, no password. • .fspback — full snapshot, encrypted with your password. Readable formats cannot carry channels, settings or storage, so when those are ticked the bot switches you to a backup format. Tokens force .fspback . Choose by destination: spreadsheet planning → .csv, printing or editing prose → .rtf/.odt, another tool → .json, disaster recovery → .fsback. See also Plain Text, CSV Export, JSON Export.

## Plain Text
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/export_text.html

A .txt export writes every message as readable text, one block after another, with the send time and channel above each message. Why it matters The same layout is what the importer expects, so a .txt file can be edited by hand and imported back as a batch of messages. Separate messages with a blank line; a date line starts a new entry. Formatting from the original post (bold, links) is kept where the format allows it; inline buttons and polls are not part of the text file. Next: Supported Import Formats.

## CSV Export
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/export_csv.html

.csv exports open in Excel, Google Sheets, Numbers and any other spreadsheet tool. Columns Each row is one message: channel, date/time, content, and media information. Good for • Planning a month of content with a teammate. • Reporting how many posts go to each channel. • Editing many captions at once, then importing the sheet back (see CSV Import). Save as UTF-8 so emoji and non-Latin text survive. Watch out: a spreadsheet may reformat dates on save — keep the format DD.MM.YYYY HH:MM if you plan to re-import.

## JSON Export
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/export_json.html

.json keeps the full structured record of each message — content, entities, times, channel reference and media references — so a script can process your schedule without parsing prose. It is meant for developers and for moving data between tools. The importer reads the same shape, so a JSON export can be imported back into this bot. Prefer a complete restorable snapshot? A .fsback backup keeps settings, bots, storage and recurring rules too — see Create a Backup.

## RTF Export
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/export_rtf.html

.rtf keeps simple formatting — bold, italics, line breaks — and opens in Microsoft Word, LibreOffice Writer, Google Docs and TextEdit. Use it when the output is a document to read, print, or hand to someone who does not use spreadsheets. Content is grouped by channel with the send time above each message. RTF is not re-importable; for a round trip use CSV or plain text.

## ODT Export
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/export_odt.html

.odt is the standard open-document text format. It opens in LibreOffice, OpenOffice, and Google Docs, and can be saved onward as .docx or .pdf. Same content as the RTF export — channel, time, message body — in a document you can style and print. Like RTF, ODT is for reading and editing, not for restoring a schedule. Use Backup for that.

## Import
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/import.html

Import is the way in: a backup, a message list, a spreadsheet, or a SetDate schedule becomes scheduled messages. Open it Main menu → Data → Import , or send /import . The bot then waits for a file; sending the document is the next step. Accepted files • .fsback / .fspback — full restore. • .txt — message list. • .csv — spreadsheet. • .json — structured export. • .rtf / .odt — readable exports. • SetDate schedule files. Details and pitfalls: Importing Your Data and Supported Import Formats.

Q: Can I import messages in bulk?
A: Yes! Send a .txt file where each message is separated by a blank line. All messages will be imported with the same date/time. You can then edit each one individually.

Q: What formats are supported for import?
A: Supported formats: .txt, .csv, .json, .rtf, .odt, .fsback (Fast Scheduler Backup), .fspback (Fast Scheduler Protected Backup).

## Importing Your Data
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/import_data.html

Steps 1. Open Data → Import or send /import . 2. Send the file as a document (not as text, not as a photo of a spreadsheet). 3. For .fspback , type the password when asked. 4. Full backups ask for Overwrite or Add . Message lists and spreadsheets go straight to the mapping step. 5. The bot reports how many messages were created and which rows were skipped, with the reason. Two kinds of import • Snapshot restore — a backup rebuilds messages, settings and connections together. • Message import — a text, CSV or JSON file only creates messages, inside the channel you pick. Next: Supported Import Formats, CSV Import, Restore Backup.

## Import a Chat
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/import_chat.html

A text or CSV import creates scheduled messages for one channel at a time. Steps 1. Send /import and upload the file. 2. Pick the target channel from the list. 3. The bot parses each block, shows what it read, and asks you to confirm. 4. Messages appear in Message List right away. Format rule Each block needs a date line. A blank line separates messages. Dates use the same formats you can type by hand, for example 25.12.2026 10:00 — see Date &amp; Time Formats. Media cannot ride inside a text file. Attach it afterwards by editing each message, or store it once and reuse it via From Storage.

## CSV Import
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/import_csv.html

CSV import is for content plans built in Excel or Google Sheets. The format Two columns are enough: • Date/Time — for example 25.12.2026 10:00 , or a relative form the bot understands (see Date &amp; Time Formats). • Content — the message text; line breaks can be written as \n . Extra columns are ignored, so a planning sheet with status or owner columns still imports. Save as UTF-8 so emoji and Cyrillic survive. Where messages land Rows are created in the channel you pick during the import. Nothing is published immediately; everything appears in Message List with its scheduled time. Common failures • Excel rewrote the dates — keep them as text or as the exact format above. • A row has a past date — the bot reports it instead of scheduling. • The sheet has a title row — remove it or make sure it does not look like a date. Round trip: CSV Export.

## JSON Import
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/import_json.html

A .json file from an export can be imported back. Send the file during the import flow ( Data → Import or /import ). The bot recreates each record: text, date and channel reference. If the file came from a different setup, messages land in your currently connected channel. Need settings, bots and recurring rules too? That is what a .fsback restore does — see Restore Backup. Structure and fields are described in JSON Export.

## Supported Import Formats
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/import_formats.html

• .fsback / .fspback — full backup. Offers Overwrite or Add and restores messages, settings and connections. • .txt — message list; a blank line starts a new message and each needs a date line. • .csv — spreadsheet with date and content columns. • .json — structured export. • .rtf / .odt — readable exports produced by this bot. • SetDate schedules — files generated by the SetDate bot, imported as-is. Everything except full backups only creates messages, and only in the channel you choose. Full backups can also restore settings and connections. If a file is rejected, check the extension first — the bot decides by extension, so a renamed file fails.

## Import From Storage
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/import_from_storage.html

When an import needs media, you can pull files from your own Storage Boxes instead of uploading them again. Where it appears In the media step of an import or of a SetDate-style build, choose From Storage , pick a box, then pick the item. The message is created with that media attached. Why bother • A spreadsheet cell of captions can become a full media post. • Nothing is re-uploaded, so nothing is re-compressed. • The same file can back many posts — see Using From Storage. Uploads and limits: Save Media.

## Backup
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/backup.html

A backup is a single file containing everything the bot knows about you: scheduled and recurring messages, connected channels and sender bots, settings, and storage references. Backup vs Export An export is a readable copy. A backup is a restorable snapshot — it can be loaded back with Overwrite or Add. See Create a Backup for the steps and What Is Backed Up for the inventory. Two file types • .fsback — plain backup. • .fspback — encrypted with a password you choose. Premium Full backups are a Premium feature. The Data screen is always reachable; without Premium it shows the upgrade prompt instead of the backup flow. A backup that has never been restored is a hope, not a backup. Test one — see Verify.

Q: How do I export my data?
A: Step by step: 1. Click Export on the main menu (page 2) or use /export 2. Choose what to export: Scheduled Messages , Recurring Messages , or Media Storage 3. Choose format: • .txt — plain text, human-readable • .csv — spreadsheet (opens in Excel/Google Sheets) • .json — structured data for developers 4. The file is sent to you as a document For a full backup (Premium): use /backup → choose password protection (optional) → the .fsback file is sent to you. To restore: use /import and send the .fsback file.

Q: How do I restore a backup?
A: Step by step: 1. Click Import on the main menu (page 2) or use /import 2. Send the backup file (.fsback or .fspback) 3. If password-protected, enter the password when prompted 4. The bot restores all your data — messages, channels, bots, settings 5. You'll get a confirmation when done Note: Restoring a backup replaces your current data. Make sure to export your current data first if you want to keep it.

Q: Can I set up automatic backups?
A: Automatic backups are not available as a built-in feature yet. However, you can manually export anytime: • Use /export for selective export (scheduled, recurring, or media) • Use /backup for a full backup (Premium, can be password-protected) Recommendation: export your data regularly, especially before making big changes.

Q: How do I create a password-protected backup?
A: Premium feature. Step by step: 1. Use /backup command 2. When prompted, choose Enable Password Protection 3. Enter a password (you'll need this to restore later — don't forget it!) 4. The .fspback file is generated and sent to you 5. To restore: use /import → send the .fspback file → enter the password Warning: Without the password, the backup cannot be restored. Keep your password safe!

Q: What's included in a full backup?
A: A full backup (.fsback / .fspback) includes: all scheduled messages (text, media, settings), all recurring messages, media storage items and boxes, channel connections and settings, bot tokens and assignments, user preferences (language, timezone), and referral data. Everything needed to restore your account to exactly the same state.

Q: What's the difference between .fsback and .fspback?
A: .fsback is a Fast Scheduler Backup (unencrypted, integrity-checked). .fspback is a Fast Scheduler Protected Backup — encrypted with a password you set (Premium only). Both hold the same data, but .fspback requires the password to restore. To create a .fspback: use /backup → choose Protected Backup → enter your password. Note: if your export includes sender bot tokens, the Protected Backup (.fspback) is chosen automatically.

## Create a Backup
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/backup_create.html

Steps 1. Send /backup , or open Data and choose Export with the backup format. 2. Tick the categories to include (everything is ticked by default). 3. Choose .fsback for a plain file, or choose the protected option and type a password for .fspback . 4. The bot builds the file and sends it to the chat as a document. 5. Save it off Telegram — cloud drive, computer, external disk. How often Before a mass delete, before moving channels, before a long break, and after a big campaign is set up. There are no automatic scheduled backups — see Scheduled Backups. Password warning A .fspback file cannot be opened without its password. No support route can recover it. Store the password in a password manager — see Backup Password.

## What Is Backed Up
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/backup_include.html

A full backup contains: • Scheduled messages — content, time, channel, media references, inline buttons, polls. • Recurring messages — the rules (daily/weekly/monthly/interval) and content. • Connected channels and sender bots — which channel is posted to, and which bot does the posting. • Settings — language, time zone, and similar preferences. • Storage — box names and the index of stored media. • Promo and referral data — invite progress and rewards. In short: everything needed to rebuild the same account on the same bot. Restoring works best into an account that still has the same channels connected — see Restore Backup.

## What Is Excluded
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/backup_exclude.html

A backup does not include: • Other people's data. Only your own records are packed. • The actual media files as duplicates — media is stored as references to Telegram files. On restore the references are re-verified, and anything Telegram no longer holds is reported. • Server logs and internal state. • Channel administrators granted through the sender bot beyond what the bot itself stores — Telegram still holds the source of truth there. If a category cannot be included, the report the bot sends with the file tells you which one and why.

## Backup Password
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/backup_password.html

Choosing the protected option turns the backup into an encrypted .fspback file. You type the password in the chat during the flow; the file is then unreadable without it. Rules that matter • The password is not stored anywhere you can retrieve it. • Lost password = lost backup. There is no reset and no support recovery. • A password-protected backup is required whenever your selection includes account tokens. • Restoring asks for the password once — see Restore Backup. Store it in a password manager, not in the same chat as the file.

## Backup Size
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/backup_size.html

Backup size depends on how much you have: number of messages, recurring rules, channels and storage entries. Text-heavy accounts produce small files — usually well under a few megabytes. Media is stored as references , not copies, so a schedule with hundreds of photos still yields a compact backup. On restore those references are re-checked against Telegram. If a file looks unexpectedly large, you probably exported with readable formats and long captions, or included many storage entries. Neither is a problem.

## Scheduled Backups
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/backup_schedule.html

Automatic recurring backups are not a feature of this bot. Nothing runs in the background that produces backup files for you. Replace it with a habit • Take a /backup before any destructive step (mass delete, channel disconnect, long pause). • After finishing a campaign setup, take one and keep it with the campaign material. • Keep the last two or three files in different places. For quick, readable copies between backups, use Export. For recovery, only a backup can rebuild the account.

## Restore Backup
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/backup_restore.html

Steps 1. Open Data → Import (or send /import ). 2. Send the .fsback or .fspback file as a document. 3. For a .fspback , type the password when asked. 4. Choose how to apply it: • Overwrite — replaces the categories in the backup with the backup's contents. Use it to reproduce an account exactly. • Add — keeps what you have now and adds the backup's messages alongside. Use it to merge an old plan into a live one. 5. The bot reports what was restored and what was skipped. Before you restore Overwrite is destructive to what it covers. Take a fresh backup of the current state first. Restoring a backup created on a different bot account works, but channels must be connected on the account doing the restore — see Channels.

## Verify
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/backup_verify.html

A backup is only proven by restoring it. A safe test 1. Take the backup you want to trust. 2. Keep a second, current backup of the live account. 3. Restore the first one with Add into a test account, or into the same account knowing you can restore the second file afterwards. 4. Check: are the messages there, are times right, are channels resolved? 5. Restore the current backup if you were testing in place. Signs of a damaged file • The bot rejects the file immediately. • It restores but reports missing media references. • Times shift by hours — usually a time-zone difference on the receiving account (see Time Zones). Restore steps: Restore Backup.

## Cloud
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/backup_cloud.html

The bot sends the backup as a Telegram document. Telegram documents stay available, but a chat is not a storage service and a lost device can mean a lost session. Keep a copy in at least two places • A cloud drive (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive). • Your computer's disk. • Optionally an external drive for monthly snapshots. Name files so you can tell them apart, for example fsback-2026-10-20.fsback . If the file is an .fspback , keep the password in a password manager — never in the same folder.

## Download
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/backup_download.html

The backup arrives as a document in your chat with the bot. Tap it and choose Save to Downloads / Save to Files , then move it somewhere with a real backup routine. On desktop, Telegram saves documents straight to your Downloads folder. On mobile, use the share sheet to send it to a drive. What not to do • Do not forward it to a group. • Do not rename the extension — .fsback and .fspback must stay as they are or the importer will not recognize it. Restore steps: Restore Backup.

## What Is the Difference Between .fsback and .fspback?
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_fsback_vs_fspback.html

Short answer: both are the same complete backup — the only difference is the password . A .fspback file is a Fast Scheduler Protected Backup — a password-protected .fsback file. The extra “p” stands for protected . What each format is .fsback — a Fast Scheduler Backup : a full backup of your Fast Scheduler data with no password . Anyone who gets the file can restore it, so treat it like a plain-text secret. .fspback — a Fast Scheduler Protected Backup : the same backup, encrypted . Restoring asks for the password you set when creating it. Without the password the data inside cannot be read. When you tap Create Backup (or send /backup ), the bot asks whether you want password protection. Choosing no password produces .fsback ; setting a password (and an optional hint) produces .fspback . A Premium feature — backups are part of the Export &amp; Backup toolkit that unlocks with Premium. What is inside either file Both formats package your selected data — scheduled messages, recurring messages, settings, and more — into one archive you can download, store in the cloud, or move to another account. Media you saved in Media Storage is referenced, not re-uploaded, so files stay small. Which one should you pick? Restoring to your own account right now? .fsback is fine and faster to use. Keeping the file long-term, sending it to a teammate, or migrating to a new phone? .fspback — the password protects your scheduled content from strangers. Restoring a file Send /import to the bot, attach the .fsback or .fspback file, enter the password if asked, then choose Overwrite (replace current data) or Add (merge with current data). Export a fresh backup before you overwrite anything.

Q: Is .fspback more secure than .fsback?
A: Yes. A .fspback file is encrypted with the password you set; a .fsback file is not protected at all. If the backup contains bot tokens or private content, prefer .fspback.

Q: I lost the password to my .fspback file. Can it be recovered?
A: No. The password cannot be reset or bypassed — not even by support. Keep the password (and the hint you optionally set) together with the file. Without it the backup is unreadable.

Q: Can I convert .fsback to .fspback (or back)?
A: Indirectly: restore the .fsback file into your account, then create a new backup and choose password protection to get a .fspback file. There is no direct file-conversion command.

Q: Which formats can I import besides these?
A: Imports also accept .json, .csv, .txt, .rtf and .odt files (and SetDate bundles). Those carry messages only, while .fsback/.fspback carry your full configuration.

## How to Back Up All Scheduled Posts in Telegram (and Restore Them Anywhere)
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_backup_full_guide.html

Rebuilding a month of scheduled posts by hand is nobody's idea of fun. Fast Scheduler's backup system exists so you never have to: one file captures everything, and restoring it on any account takes about a minute. What a backup contains A .fsback / .fspback file packages the parts of your account you select — typically: Scheduled messages — every queued post with its exact send time. Recurring messages — repeat rules (daily, weekly, custom intervals) and their expiry settings. Settings — language, time zone, signatures, channel preferences. Media Storage references — saved photos, videos and documents with their boxes. What is not included: user backups exclude sender-bot tokens, and payment history never leaves Telegram's systems. The export screen lets you review what goes into the file before you confirm. Creating a backup — step by step Backups are a Premium feature. With Premium active: 1. Open the menu → Data → Export (or send /backup ). 2. Pick what to include (scheduled, recurring, all). 3. Choose password protection : none for .fsback , or set a password + hint for .fspback . 4. The bot packs the archive and sends the file. Save it somewhere real — cloud drive, local disk, anywhere that survives losing your phone. Restoring — the safe way Send /import , attach the file, enter the password if prompted. The bot then asks how to apply it: Overwrite — replaces your current data with the backup's content. Anything not in the backup disappears. Add — merges the backup into your current data, keeping what you already have. Golden rule: export a fresh backup before restoring an older one. It is your undo button if the result surprises you. Good backup habits Take a fresh backup before deleting a channel, rotating a bot, or bulk-editing posts. Keep at least one .fspback with a strong password — shared drives get opened by more people than you think. After switching phones or accounts, restore + verify the Message List before the real posting week starts.

Q: Is backup free or Premium?
A: Creating .fsback/.fspback backups is part of the Export & Backup toolkit, which requires Premium. Importing files (/import) works on Free, so anyone can restore a backup received from someone else.

Q: Where should I store the backup file?
A: Anywhere outside Telegram: a cloud drive, your computer, or an encrypted notes app. Telegram keeps the file in your chat too, but Saved Messages is not a backup strategy.

Q: How big is a backup file?
A: Small — usually kilobytes to a few megabytes, because media is referenced rather than embedded. Text and schedules compress extremely well.

Q: Can I move my schedules to another Telegram account?
A: Yes. Create a backup on the old account, log into the new one, connect the channel and a sender bot, then restore the backup with Add mode. This is the standard migration path.

# Media Storage

## Media Storage
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/media_storage.html

Storage keeps photos, videos and documents so you never upload the same header twice. Open it from Storage in the main menu. Structure Boxes → items. One box = one collection (a product line, a channel's branding, a recurring promo). Each item keeps its Telegram file reference plus a name. What it is for • Posting the same image on a schedule. • Random media rotation — see Sequential mode and Random mode. • Bulk imports where media is picked from the library. Start here: Storage Boxes, then Create a Box. Uploading: Save Media.

Q: How do I create a storage box and save media?
A: Step by step: 1. Click Media Storage on the main menu (page 2) or use /storage 2. Click Create Box 3. Enter a name for your box (e.g., "Product Photos") 4. The box is created — now click on it to open it 5. Send photos, videos, or files to the bot — they'll be saved in this box 6. Later, when scheduling a message, choose From Storage as the media option and pick from your collection Free plan: 1 box, max 100 items, no videos. Premium: up to 20 boxes, 500 items.

Q: How do I rename or delete a storage box?
A: To rename : click Media Storage → select the box → click Rename → type the new name → confirm. To delete : click Media Storage → select the box → click Delete Box → confirm deletion. Warning: Deleting a box removes ALL media inside it permanently.

Q: Can I move items between storage boxes?
A: Yes — bulk move and copy is a Premium feature. Step by step: 1. Click Media Storage → open the source box 2. Use Move All or Copy All (optionally filtered by type: images, videos, files) 3. Choose the destination box from the list 4. The items are moved/copied — no need to re-upload On the Free plan you can move or copy one file at a time instead — open the item and use Move / Copy . This helps you reorganize your media collection without re-uploading anything.

Q: Can I download a whole storage box?
A: Yes — box download is a Premium feature: open the box and tap Download Box to get its files as an archive. On the Free plan open any item and tap Download to save files one at a time, without compression.

Q: What happens to my storage when Premium expires?
A: On the first day after expiry, you'll get a prompt to choose 1 storage box to keep . If you don't choose, the newest box is kept by default. Excess boxes are deleted after 17 days. The kept box is trimmed to the newest 100 items (videos are removed first, oldest first). To avoid this: reactivate Premium with /premium before day 17.

Q: Can I store videos in Media Storage?
A: Free plan: No in storage — you'll get an error if you try. Premium: up to 50MB per video. Videos larger than the premium limit cannot be saved to storage even on Premium. To check your plan: use /premium or click Premium on the main menu.

Q: How do I delete individual items from storage?
A: Step by step: 1. Click Media Storage on the main menu (or use /storage ) 2. Select the storage box containing the items 3. Browse the list of media items 4. Click on an item → click Delete 5. Confirm deletion — this is permanent and cannot be undone To delete everything: use Delete Box to remove the entire box and all contents.

Q: Can I preview media before selecting it for a message?
A: Yes! When scheduling a message and you reach the media step: 1. Choose From Storage 2. Select a storage box 3. Each item shows a preview — you can see the image/video before picking it 4. Click on the one you want → it's attached to your scheduled message 5. Confirm and your message is ready with the selected media

## Storage Boxes
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/ms_boxes.html

Media is organized into boxes . Open Storage from the main menu and you see your boxes with an item count each, plus ➕ Add Storage . Tapping a box opens its items: thumbnails with a name, and the actions Upload , Search , and — on Premium — Move All , Copy All and Download Box . Plan limits Free: 1 box, up to 100 items, no videos. Premium: up to 20 boxes, 500 items, videos allowed. More: Storage Limits, Create a Box, Quota.

Q: How do I create a storage box?
A: Open Media Storage , tap Create Box , give it a name, then save media into it directly from the schedule flow. Free plan allows 1 (max 100) box.

## Create a Box
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/ms_create.html

Steps 1. Open Storage from the main menu. 2. Tap ➕ Add Storage . 3. Send a name. It appears immediately as an empty box. 4. Open the box and upload media. Naming Name by purpose, not by file: Product shots , Channel headers , Winter promo . You will pick from this list inside a scheduling flow, where long names get cut off. Limits per plan: Storage Limits. Renaming later: Rename Box.

## Rename Box
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/ms_rename.html

Open Storage → tap the box → use the rename action, then send the new name. The box keeps every item. Renaming does not break schedules: they reference the media, not the name. Useful when a box was created for a campaign that has since become evergreen. Related: Manage Storage.

## Archive
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/ms_archive.html

Archiving hides a box you no longer actively use while keeping its items saved. Open Storage , pick the box, choose archive. Archived boxes stay available to your account and keep counting toward your plan's limits, so archiving is tidiness, not extra space. To reclaim space, delete items instead — see Delete Media. Restore an archived box at any time from the same place.

## Quota
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/ms_quota.html

Your quota is measured in items , across all boxes. • Free — 1 box, up to 100 items, photos and documents only. • Premium — up to 20 boxes and 500 items, videos included. The storage screen shows how full you are. When the cap is hit, the bot refuses new uploads with an upgrade prompt. Free space by deleting unused items — Delete Media — or move items into a single box to free a box slot. If Premium lapses, cleanup follows the timeline in Lifecycle.

## Preview
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/ms_preview.html

Tapping an item in a box opens it: the media itself, its name, its type, and the actions available ( Use , Move , Copy , Replace , Delete ). Preview first when a box has similar files — several product shots, several headers — so the post does not ship the wrong image. Videos play inline. Next: Using From Storage.

## Search Storage
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/ms_search.html

Inside a box, use Search and type part of an item's name. Matching items are listed so you can pick one immediately. Search matches names, not image content — there is no visual recognition. If you store lots of similar files, the fix is naming: prefix by purpose ( promo-winter-01 , promo-winter-02 ) and search becomes reliable. Related: Rename Box, Manage Storage.

## Manage Box
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/ms_box_manage.html

Inside an open box: • Upload — send photos, videos (Premium) or documents to add them. • Search — filter by name. • Item actions — Use , Move , Copy , Replace , Delete . • Rename / Delete box — manage the box itself. • Premium bulk tools — Move All , Copy All (optionally filtered by type) and Download Box . Item actions are in Copying Items, Move Media, Replace Media, Delete Media. Bulk tools: Bulk Move, Copy &amp; Box Download.

## Save Media
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/ms_save.html

Steps 1. Storage → open a box. 2. Tap Upload (or just send the file while the box is open). 3. Send photos, videos or documents. Each one is added as an item. 4. Optionally name the item so search finds it later. What happens to the file Photos and videos are compressed on the way in — the same pipeline used when scheduling. Documents are stored as-is, so their size counts fully against your quota. Videos need Premium. Limits: Storage Limits. Compression details: Media Compression &amp; Retention.

## Stored Photos
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/ms_photo.html

Photos are the default storage content and the only media type available on the Free plan. Each upload is compressed to your plan's limits (dimensions and quality differ between Free and Premium — see Media Compression &amp; Retention). The compressed copy is what gets posted later, so what you preview is what your readers see. Reuse a stored photo with From Storage, or rotate a set with Random mode.

## Stored Videos
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/ms_video.html

Videos can be stored and reused only on Premium : up to 50MB. On Free, sending a video during a scheduling flow still works if it fits the media size limit — it is simply not kept in a box afterwards. Storing it requires Premium. Videos are compressed on upload like photos, with the Premium limits shown in Media Compression &amp; Retention. Reuse them through From Storage. Plan comparison: Storage Limits, Storage on Premium.

## Stored Documents
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/ms_document_storage.html

Documents (PDF, DOCX, ZIP and similar) can be saved to a box and reused in scheduled posts. Unlike photos and videos they are stored without compression , so a few large documents can eat a big part of your quota. Names matter more here: file names are often the only way to tell two documents apart, so rename items clearly. Documents post as a file attachment with the caption you write. Limits: Storage Limits.

## Using From Storage
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/ms_from_storage_help.html

While scheduling, the media step offers From Storage next to uploading new media. Steps 1. Schedule a message and reach the media step. 2. Choose From Storage . 3. Pick a box, then an item. 4. Continue — the post is created with that exact file. Combined with Sequential or Random modes this is how you post a rotating media library without touching it again — see Media Modes. If an item was deleted after being used, affected posts fall back to text-only — see Delete Media.

## Manage Storage
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/ms_manage.html

All storage actions live under Storage in the main menu: • Boxes — create, rename, delete. Open one to work inside it. • Items — upload, preview, search, copy, move, replace, delete. • Premium bulk tools — Move All , Copy All (optionally filtered by type) and Download Box for the whole box as one archive. Items persist until you delete them. If Premium lapses, the expiry cleanup described in Lifecycle may remove excess media. Start from Storage Boxes.

## Copying Items
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/ms_copy.html

Copy places a duplicate of an item into another box; the original stays where it is. Move relocates it instead. Steps 1. Open the box → tap the item → Copy . 2. Pick the destination box. 3. The item appears there immediately. When copying beats moving • A logo that belongs to several campaign boxes. • Seasonal collections that share evergreen assets. • A favourites box mirroring items from working boxes. Copies are independent: deleting one never affects the other, and every schedule referencing either keeps working. Premium bulk version: Copy All.

## Move Media
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/ms_move.html

Steps 1. Open the source box → tap the item → Move . 2. Choose the destination box. 3. The item leaves the source and appears in the destination. Schedules that reference the item keep working — the reference follows the media, not the box. Moving is the right tool when you are reorganizing by campaign rather than duplicating. Premium adds Move All , which moves a whole box — or only one type inside it — in one action. See Bulk Move, Copy &amp; Box Download.

## Replace Media
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/ms_replace.html

Replace puts a new file in place of an existing item while keeping the item and its references. Steps 1. Open the box → tap the item → Replace . 2. Send the new file. 3. The item is updated. The catch Any schedule using that item posts the new file. That is exactly what you want for a corrected product shot; it is wrong if you meant to keep the old version somewhere. Copy the item first if you need both.

## Delete Media
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/ms_delete.html

Open the box → tap the item → Delete . What happens to posts that used it Scheduled messages that referenced the item are not deleted. They become text-only messages instead of failing at send time. Check those posts in Message List if the image mattered. Deleting items frees quota immediately — see Quota. Deleting a whole box is done from the box menu and removes all of its items.

## Bulk Move, Copy & Box Download
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/ms_bulk.html

These three tools sit inside any open box and require Premium. Move All • Moves every item — or only one type (images, videos, files) — into a box you pick. • Use it to split a mixed box by type or retire a finished campaign in one action. Copy All • Same flow, but the source box keeps its items — seeding a new campaign box from an archive without touching the original. Download Box • Packs the entire box into a single archive and sends it to you, so you can keep an offline copy or move it elsewhere. Single-item versions: Copying Items, Move Media.

Q: Is bulk move/copy a Premium feature?
A: Yes — Move All , Copy All , and Download Box need Premium. On Free you can move, copy, or download one file at a time instead.

Q: Can I move only videos or only photos?
A: Yes. Move All and Copy All offer an optional type filter (images, videos, files), so one tap can split a mixed box by type.

Q: What do I get when I download a box?
A: One archive with the box files, for offline backup or sharing with a teammate. On Free, open items one by one and tap Download instead.

## Storage Limits
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/ms_limits.html

Free • 1 box • up to 100 items total • photos and documents; no videos in storage Premium • up to 20 boxes • 500 items total • videos allowed (up to 50MB) Upgrading or downgrading keeps what you already saved; when a plan shrinks, the excess is handled during the expiry process rather than deleted silently. Timeline: Lifecycle. Premium tools: Storage on Premium.

## Storage on Premium
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/ms_premium.html

Premium storage: • 20 boxes instead of 1, up to 500 items. • Videos allowed (up to 50MB). • Higher media size limit (100 MB) and better compression quality — see Media Compression &amp; Retention. • Move All / Copy All — reorganize a whole box in one tap, optionally only one media type. • Download Box — save an entire box as a single archive. On Free you can still move, copy and download items one at a time. Upgrade via /premium — Premium.

## Media Compression & Retention
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/media_retention.html

All media you send to the bot is automatically compressed &mdash; this shrinks the file Telegram stores and sends, and keeps it within your plan's size limits. Compression Comparison Feature │ Free │ Premium ───────────────────┼────────────────────┼─────────────────────── Photo max │ 1600px │ 2500px Photo quality │ Q65 │ Q90 Video max │ 620p │ 1080p Video CRF │ 28 │ 23 Video bitrate │ 1Mbps │ 2Mbps Audio bitrate │ 64k │ 128k Voice bitrate │ 48k │ 96k 4K media │ Blocked │ Allowed Compression is applied automatically when you upload media to: Media Storage, Scheduled / Recurring messages, Feedback attachments, Broadcasts, and anywhere else in the bot. Documents and stickers are stored as-is without compression. Media Retention & Cleanup The bot periodically removes old media references that are no longer needed: Ratings • Admin reply media in rating reviews: deleted after 30 days • The rating (stars, review text) stays forever Feedback / Support tickets • Attachments in closed / spam tickets: deleted after 30 days from closure • The conversation text stays forever Media Storage • Items are kept until you delete them manually • Never auto-deleted Scheduled Messages • Media reference is removed immediately after the message is sent • No data lingers Recurring Messages • Media stays until you delete the recurring message • Free accounts: recurring message expires after 1 year and is auto-removed

Q: Is my media quality reduced?
A: Yes. All photos, videos, audio files, and voice messages are compressed to save Telegram server storage. Free users get aggressive compression (photos 1600px/Q65, video 620p/CRF28, audio 64k). Premium users get gentler compression (photos 2500px/Q90, video 1080p/CRF23, audio 128k). On a phone screen the difference is barely noticeable. Free users are also blocked from uploading 4K media (photos ≥3840px or videos ≥2160p). Upgrade to Premium to send high-resolution content.

Q: How much smaller will my files get?
A: Typical savings depend on the original file: • Photos: free 60–85%, premium 30–50% • Videos: varies by source; a 50MB video at 1080p can drop to ~5–8MB for free users or ~15–25MB for premium users • Audio/Voice: re-encoded at the target bitrate, so a 320kbps file at 10MB would become ~2MB (free 64k) or ~4MB (premium 128k)

Q: Can I get my original uncompressed file back?
A: No. Once the bot compresses a file, only the compressed version is stored. Always keep your original files safe on your own device.

## When to Use Storage
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/storage_use_case.html

Use storage when: • The same photo or video goes out repeatedly (products, headers, promos). • You want consistent branding across channels. • You build schedules in bulk and need media without re-uploading. • You want the bot to rotate media automatically — Random mode rotates through stored photos. Skip storage when: • It is a one-off post — attach the media during scheduling. • The file is a large one-time video. Attaching directly is covered in Adding Photos &amp; Videos.

Q: When is media storage useful?
A: Whenever you reuse visuals — promo banners, cover images, or recurring content. Save once, then attach to any scheduled message without re-uploading.

## Lifecycle
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/storage_lifecycle.html

Stored items persist until you delete them — there is no automatic aging while your plan is active. When Premium lapses • Excess boxes are removed on day 17 after expiry. • The kept box is trimmed to 100 items, with videos removed first. • Scheduled messages are not deleted — ones that used removed media fall back to text-only. Renew before day 17 to keep all media. Plan details: Storage Limits, Premium Expiry.

Q: What happens to storage boxes on expiry?
A: You keep one box you choose. Day 17: other boxes are deleted and your kept box is trimmed to 100 items. Renew before then to keep everything.

## What Is Media Storage and How Do You Use It Without Losing Your Mind?
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_media_storage_guide.html

Media Storage is your in-bot asset library: save a photo, video, or document once, then reuse it in any scheduled post without re-uploading. If you repost evergreen content or reuse brand imagery, this is the feature that saves the most time per week. Boxes: folders with a purpose Assets live in boxes — named containers like “Brand”, “Memes”, “Product shots”. Free gets 1 box with 100 items (no video in storage); Premium gets 20 boxes with 500 items total with video support. Boxes keep the picker fast and your library mentally organized — one box per campaign is a good default. Saving and reusing Save: forward or upload media to the storage, or save straight from a scheduled message you are composing. Reuse: while scheduling, open the storage instead of attaching a file — pick the asset, done. Telegram file references are reused, so nothing is re-uploaded and quality is not recompressed per post. Organize: move items between boxes, rename, delete. The limits that actually matter Item count — the 100-item Free box fills fast with albums; delete stale assets or upgrade. Video on Free — storage refuses video on Free; schedule videos directly instead, or move to Premium for video-in-storage. Size — same upload caps as messages: 10 MB on Free, 100 MB on Premium. A cleanup cadence that works Once a month: open each box, delete anything unused in 60 days, archive campaign boxes by renaming with a date prefix. Two minutes, and the picker stays a joy instead of an archaeology dig.

Q: Does deleting a media item break scheduled posts using it?
A: Posts keep working — a scheduled message holds its own reference to the media. Deleting from storage only removes it from the library for future posts.

Q: Can I share a box with another admin?
A: Storage is per account. To share assets, export them as part of a backup or send the files directly — the other account saves them into their own storage.

# Tools

## Tools
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tools.html

Message List ( /list ) — the workhorse. Browse per channel, preview, edit, delete, duplicate. Details: Message List. Search ( /search ) — find a post by keyword across every scheduled and recurring message. Details: Search. Calendar ( /calendar ) — the month at a glance; tap a day for its posts. Details: Calendar. Statistics ( /stats ) — counts, sends and per-channel numbers. Details: Statistics. All four are on the second page of the main menu. In a sender-bot context they only show the channels your role can see — Sender Bot Permissions.

## Message List
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/message_list.html

Open it: Main menu → Message List , or /list . With more than one channel connected you pick a channel first. What the list shows Each row is a message with its job number, send time (or recurring rule) and a short preview. Scheduled and recurring messages can be filtered apart. Tapping a message opens the same controls everywhere in the bot: Preview , Duplicate , Edit , Delete , and Back . Other buttons on the list screen • ➕ New — starts the scheduling flow. • Delete All — removes every scheduled and recurring message for that channel after a confirmation. More: Editing a Message, Duplicate Messages, Deleting a Message.

## Search
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/search.html

There are two search features — do not confuse them: • Search in Tools finds scheduled and recurring messages by their text. • Search inside a storage box finds media items by name. Searching messages 1. Tap Search on the main menu (second page) or send /search . 2. Type a keyword or phrase. 3. Matching messages are listed with their job number and send time. 4. Tap a result → preview, edit, duplicate or delete. Matching is case-insensitive and matches parts of words. A job number finds one message exactly — handy when a notification gave you the ID. More: Search Filters, Deleting Found Messages, Search Storage.

Q: What if I want to browse all messages?
A: Use Message List to browse messages by channel instead of searching.

## Search Messages
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/search_messages.html

1. Tap Search (or send /search ). 2. Send a word or phrase. 3. Browse results; tap one to preview, edit, duplicate or delete. Search is case-insensitive and matches partial words, so sale finds Sale , sales and wholesale . If you know the job number, sending it is an exact match. Search covers message text — not captions inside media files, and not storage item contents (that is storage search).

## Search Filters
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/search_filter.html

There are no dropdown filters. Narrowing works in three ways: • Scope by channel — open Search from a channel's context ( Bots → the connected bot) and results are limited to that channel. • Pick distinctive words — search matches any message containing what you type, so a longer phrase is a tighter filter. • Use a job number — exact match, ideal when you already know which message you mean. For browsing by time instead of text, use Calendar or Message List.

## Deleting Found Messages
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/search_delete.html

Every result opens the normal message controls: preview, edit, duplicate and delete . Cleaning a finished campaign 1. Search its keyword. 2. Open each result and delete it — deletion is permanent and asks for confirmation, and the bot confirms which job was removed. 3. Repeat until the search returns nothing. Faster for a whole channel Delete All in the Message List removes every scheduled and recurring message for that channel in one confirmed step. Take a backup before a mass delete.

## Calendar
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/calendar.html

Open it: main menu (page 2) → Calendar , or /calendar . Pick a channel if you have several. What you see • A month grid where each day lists its scheduled send times. • Previous / Next to change month. • Both one-time and recurring messages — recurring entries are expanded across the month according to their rule. Tapping a day opens that day's messages, and each one opens the usual preview / edit / duplicate / delete controls. Calendar is the fastest way to spot collisions — three posts at the same minute — which same-day limits may also refuse. Related: Message List, Search.

Q: How do I see all my messages in a list?
A: Use Message List for a full list view instead of the calendar.

## Statistics
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/statistics.html

Open it: main menu (page 2) → Statistics , or /stats . The overview shows • Scheduled and recurring message counts right now. • Messages sent today and in total. • Total messages created. • Connected channels. Per channel Open a channel row for its own view: total posts, average views, comments and reactions, and the top reactions on your posts. Limits and usage Your plan's caps (pending messages, same-day posts, recurring rules, storage) are visible there too, which is the quickest way to see why a schedule was refused — see Limits &amp; Usage. Charts that need Premium are marked with the upgrade prompt; the underlying counts remain visible.

## How Can I See Views, Reactions and Comments on My Telegram Channel Posts?
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_stats_views.html

Telegram shows view counts under every channel post, but it never shows you trends : which topics overperform, what time of day your audience actually reads, which posts collected the most reactions. Fast Scheduler records the metrics of every post it publishes and turns them into dashboards you can browse in seconds. Where the numbers live Open Statistics on the bot&rsquo;s main menu (page 2) or send /stats . You get: Usage totals — lifetime messages sent, messages sent today, and how many schedules and recurring messages are currently active. Per-channel dashboards — for every connected channel: average views, comments and reactions per post, plus the top reactions your audience uses. Leaderboards (Premium) — your top posts ranked by the metric you pick: Views, Comments, Reactions or Top Commenters. Each board shows 10 entries per page by default (up to 50) and can be filtered by period (day, week, month, year or all time). What is counted — and what is not Statistics are recorded when Fast Scheduler publishes a post and Telegram reports back the post&rsquo;s metrics. Manually posted content that never passed through the bot is deliberately excluded, so the numbers describe your scheduled content honestly. Comments made in the discussion group under a channel post are picked up too, which is what powers the Comments metric and the Top Commenters board. Three ways to actually use this Find your format. Sort by Views for a month: if the top five posts share a pattern (length, media type, topic), schedule more of it. Time your channel. Compare identical formats posted at different hours, then move recurring messages toward the winning window — the best posting times guide below has the general playbook. Watch reactions, not just views. Views measure reach; reactions and comments measure resonance. A post with half the views but double the reaction rate is usually the better template.

Q: Does Fast Scheduler track posts I publish manually?
A: No. Only posts published through Fast Scheduler are recorded, which keeps your dashboards focused on your scheduled content strategy.

Q: Are statistics leaderboards free?
A: Per-channel averages and usage totals are available to everyone. Leaderboards that rank your top posts by views, comments or reactions are part of Premium.

Q: What metrics can leaderboards rank by?
A: Views, comments, reactions and top commenters — each filterable by day, week, month, year or all time, with up to 50 posts per page.

# Pro Tips

## Pro Tips
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tips.html

Short, tested habits — not features. Each tip links to the article that explains the underlying screen. The five that matter most • Set the time zone once, before your first post — Set Time Zone. • Preview every post before it goes out — Review Before Sending. • Keep one storage box of reusable media — Storage Boxes. • Duplicate instead of rewriting — Duplicate Posts. • Take a backup before every mass delete — Create a Backup. Pick a topic below for the rest.

## Backup Tips
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tips_backup.html

• Back up before deleting in bulk, disconnecting a channel or importing a snapshot. • Keep the file outside Telegram — a chat is not storage. • Use .fspback when the export includes tokens; a plain .fsback leaves them out. • Test-restore once. A backup you never restored is a guess. • Name files with the date so you can pick the right one later. Details: Create a Backup, Restore Backup, Verify.

Q: How often should I make a backup?
A: Make a backup before big changes and keep the auto-backup you receive when Premium expires (day 3). A backup restores your channels and settings.

## Bulk Tips
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tips_bulk.html

• Build the plan in a spreadsheet, then import it — CSV Import. • Use Duplicate for a series, then change only the date and the first line. • Recurring messages cover anything repeated daily or weekly — Recurring Messages. • Keep media in a box and attach it from storage instead of re-uploading — Using From Storage. • Spread posts across the day; same-minute collisions are the easiest mistake to make in bulk.

Q: How do I batch-schedule many messages?
A: Upload a .txt file with date+message blocks (see Batch Scheduling for the exact format). The bot creates one scheduled message per block.

## Channel Tips
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tips_channels.html

• Give every channel its own sender bot so a ban or token reset never affects the others — How Posting Works. • Set the channel's time zone on its card if its audience is in a different country. • Check the signature once, live, before a campaign — Signature. • Verify the bot is still an admin after changing channel administrators. • Use Channel Stats to see which channel actually gets views.

Q: Why is my channel not posting?
A: Check the bot is still a channel admin with Post Messages, the timezone is correct, and the sender bot is connected.

## Feedback Tips
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tips_feedback.html

• One issue per ticket. Two bugs in one report usually get one fixed. • Include the job number, the exact time and what you expected. • Attach a screenshot of the error, not a description of it. • Use the payment category for money issues so it is routed correctly. • Check your existing tickets before opening a duplicate. Start here: Send Feedback.

Q: What should I include in a bug report?
A: Your user ID, the exact error or screenshot, the channel involved, and what you expected to happen. This helps us fix it faster.

## Language Tips
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tips_language.html

• The language setting changes the bot interface , not the posts you schedule — your text stays exactly as typed. • Switch it in Settings → Language or with /language . • The Support Bot has its own language setting; changing one does not always change the other. • If a screen looks untranslated, that string may simply be English only — see Missing Language.

Q: How do I switch the bot language?
A: Send /language and pick your language. It applies immediately to all your channels.

## Migration Tips
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tips_migration.html

• Export a backup from the old account first — Create a Backup. • Connect the same channels on the new account before importing, so the references resolve. • Import with Add to merge instead of overwriting what is already there — Restore Backup. • Re-check times after the move; a different account time zone shifts the wall clock. • Keep the old account reachable until a few posts have sent successfully.

## Payment Tips
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tips_payment.html

• Check the price and period on the confirm screen before paying. • Never pay twice because the first invoice looked stuck — open Premium Status first. • Monthly plans renew automatically; packs do not. • If Premium did not activate, send the receipt and transaction ID through support — Premium Troubleshooting. • Premium is non-refundable once delivered; the only exception is non-delivery within 7 days of the payment — Refunds.

Q: Which payment method activates Premium fastest?
A: Telegram Stars activates instantly. See Payments for details.

## Premium Tips
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tips_premium.html

• Unlimited pending messages is the biggest win: build a month at once instead of trickling. • Video in storage plus Random mode means a rotating visual feed with no work — Media Modes. • Leaderboards and per-channel reports show what to post more of. • Use Move All / Download Box to keep storage tidy — Bulk Storage Tools. • Remember the expiry timeline before a long pause — Premium Expiry.

Q: What is the best Premium plan?
A: Yearly plans give the best daily price. Compare plans in /premium to pick what fits your volume.

## Preview Tips
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tips_preview.html

• Preview is cheap; a wrong post in a channel is not. • Check the first line — it is the only part most readers see in the feed. • Look for broken links and unclosed formatting tags — Formatting &amp; Inline Buttons. • Confirm the media is the right file, not just the right name. • Verify the time zone line on the preview if the channel serves a different region.

Q: Can I edit a message after I preview it?
A: Yes — the preview lets you change time, channel, or content before confirming. After saving, edit it via Message List.

## Queue Tips
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tips_queue.html

• Use Message List per channel as the daily check — Message List. • Delete campaigns that already ran; they clutter the queue and eat your Free pending limit. • Search by campaign keyword and clean up in one pass — Deleting Found Messages. • Calendar shows collisions at a glance — Calendar.

Q: What order are queued messages sent?
A: Earliest scheduled time first; equal times are sent in creation order. Check sent reports for confirmations.

## Recurring Tips
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tips_recurring.html

• Recurring is for genuinely repeating content: daily quotes, weekly digests, monthly reminders. • Pause rather than delete when a series is on hold — Pause &amp; Resume. • Check the rule on the card before trusting it; 'every 2 weeks' and 'weekly' look similar in a list. • Recurring messages expire on the schedule shown in Recurring Limit.

Q: Can recurring messages be paused?
A: Yes — open the recurring message in Message List to pause, edit, or delete it. Paused messages stop sending until resumed.

## Referral Tips
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tips_referral.html

• Share your personal link, never a generic bot link — it carries your ID. • The invited person must actually start the bot and be verified; a click alone earns nothing — Verification. • Self-referral and fake accounts void the credit — Abuse. • Watch progress in Your Referral Stats.

Q: When do I get referral rewards?
A: After invited friends join and send at least 1 messages. Track your balance in /referral .

## Search Tips
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tips_search.html

• Search the distinctive words of the first line, not the whole post. • A job number is an exact match — fastest route to one message. • Scope by channel when you have several — Search Filters. • Storage search is separate and matches item names — Search Storage.

Q: Does search work across all channels?
A: Yes — search covers all your scheduled and recurring messages across every channel at once.

## Security Tips
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tips_security.html

• Treat a bot token like a password. Anyone with it can post as your bot — Token Safety. • Never paste a token into a group, a screenshot or a support chat; the bot never asks for it. • Reset a leaked token in @BotFather and reconnect — Rotate Token. • Enable Telegram two-step verification on your account — Account Safety.

## Signature Tips
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tips_signature.html

• Keep it one line; long signatures eat caption space. • Use it for a link or handle, not for the whole call to action. • Signatures are per channel — different channels can carry different ones — Signature. • Remember signatures are a Premium feature; on Free the field is not applied.

Q: Can I use one signature per channel?
A: Yes — each channel has its own signature setting. Signatures strip automatically when Premium expires after day 3.

## Storage Tips
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tips_storage.html

• One box per purpose, not one giant box. • Name items so search works: promo-winter-01 . • Replace instead of delete-and-reupload when a file needs an update — Replace Media. • Copy, don't move, assets shared by several campaigns — Copying Items. • Empty boxes before downgrading; cleanup follows Lifecycle.

Q: What happens to my storage on Premium expiry?
A: On day 0 you pick one box to keep. Day 17: non-kept boxes are deleted and your kept box is trimmed to 100 items. Renew before then to keep everything.

Q: Can I store videos in Media Storage?
A: Yes. Videos are kept within the per-item size limits (up to 25MB for free / up to 50MB for Premium) and stored separately from photos, without quality loss.

## Time Zone Tips
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tips_timezone.html

• Set your account zone before scheduling anything — Set Time Zone. • A channel can have its own zone, which overrides your account zone for posts scheduled from that channel. • After travelling or a daylight-saving change, re-check a pending post's time. • If a post went out hours off, read Why Was My Post Late? first.

Q: Why do my posts send at the wrong time?
A: Your channel timezone is used for scheduling. Change it with /timezone to match your audience.

## Troubleshoot Tips
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tips_troubleshoot.html

• Check the channel first: is the sender bot still an admin? • Check the message: is it still in the Message List, or did it already send? • Check the time zone before blaming the scheduler. • Check the media: was the stored file deleted or replaced? • If all four are fine, report it with the job number — Send Feedback.

Q: Where do I start when something breaks?
A: Check the Troubleshooting category first. If it's still broken, use Feedback with your user ID, error text, and steps to reproduce.

## The Best Times to Post in Telegram (and How to Test Them Properly)
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tg_best_posting_times.html

“Post at 9:00” advice is usually recycled guesswork. Here is what actually moves the needle on Telegram, plus a testing method you can run with a scheduler in one week. Windows that generally work Morning commute — 8:00–10:00 local time. News, digests, “start of day” content. Lunch dip — 12:30–14:00. Light, skimmable posts do well. Evening prime time — 19:00–22:00. The strongest window for most channels; long-form and media belong here. The key word is local . If your audience spans zones, anchor to your largest cluster's evening, and let the channel's time zone setting do the conversion for you. Consistency beats cleverness Subscribers learn your rhythm. A channel that posts daily at 9:00 trains its audience to show up at 9:00 — measurable in view-rate stability. This is the strongest argument for scheduling (and recurring rules) over manual posting: the schedule becomes a product feature. How to test slots properly 1. Pick two candidate slots (e.g. 9:00 vs 20:00) and alternate similar content between them for 7–10 days. 2. Compare views in the first hour , not totals — that is when your regulars arrive. Fast Scheduler's statistics screen shows view dynamics per post. 3. Keep the winner as a recurring rule, and re-test quarterly. Audiences drift with seasons and habits. Small things that quietly help Don't stack posts 5 minutes apart — spacing beats bursts for notification fatigue. Media posts slightly outperform text-only at equal times in most niches. Skip the “dump 6 posts at midnight” pattern; Telegram's own limits and your subscribers' patience both prefer a steady drip.

Q: Does Telegram show “time of post” that I can use for testing?
A: Views are timestamped; compare first-hour views across slots. The statistics screen gives you per-post numbers without extra tools.

Q: How many posts per day is healthy?
A: 2–4 for most content channels. Beyond that, watch unsubscribes — the metric that punishes oversharing fastest.

# Feedback & Support

## Feedback & Support
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/feedback.html

The ticket form is not in this bot. Fast Scheduler's help and support live in the separate Support Bot , @FastSchedulerSupport_bot . How to file a ticket 1. Send /feedback in Fast Scheduler. 2. Tap the button in the reply — it opens the Support Bot. 3. In the Support Bot, start a new request, choose a category, describe the issue and attach a file if useful. 4. Send it. You get a ticket reference immediately. For payment problems use /paysupport instead: it opens the same Support Bot on its payment intake, where you can pick a subcategory such as refund or duplicate charge. Tracking The Support Bot's My requests lists every ticket with its status, and replies arrive in that chat. Details: View My Feedback, Status Meanings. Language Feedback must stay civil. One mild profanity gets a warning and the message is still delivered; heavily abusive messages are blocked before they reach support.

## Send Feedback
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/feedback_new.html

Steps 1. In Fast Scheduler send /feedback (or tap Feedback in the main menu). 2. The bot replies with a button; tap it to open @FastSchedulerSupport_bot . 3. In the Support Bot choose new request . 4. Pick a category: • Bug — something broken. • Feature request — something missing. • Payment — money issues, with subcategories such as refund, charged but Premium not activated, duplicate charge, cancellation or renewal, failed payment, plan/price/promo. • Other — anything else. 5. Write the description. Attach a screenshot or file if it helps. 6. Send. Keep the ticket reference. Bug reports move fastest with: what you did, the exact error text, the job number if a post is involved, and the time it happened. Next: View My Feedback, Attachments.

## Bug Reports
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/feedback_category_bug_detail.html

A good report answers four questions: 1. What did you do? The exact buttons, in order. 2. What happened? The error text, copied or screenshotted. 3. What did you expect? The behaviour you wanted. 4. When and where? Time, channel, and job number if a post is involved. Add anything unusual: a fresh token, a channel admin change, a bulk import, a Premium expiry that day. Those details usually point straight at the cause. File it via Send Feedback.

## Feature Requests
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/feedback_category_feature_detail.html

The most useful requests describe a task: "I want to post the same album to three channels at slightly different times" beats "add multi-channel albums". Include how often you need it and the workaround you use today. A request that names a real repeated problem is much easier to prioritise than one that names a missing toggle. Check the Help Center first — some of it may already exist under a different name, for example Duplicates, Recurring Messages or Media Modes.

## Payment Issues
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/feedback_category_payment_detail.html

Payment tickets go through /paysupport and open the Support Bot's payment intake. Pick the subcategory that matches: • Refund — see Refunds first. • Charged but Premium not activated — include the receipt. • Duplicate charge — include both transaction IDs. • Cancellation or renewal — say whether you want it stopped or reversed. • Failed payment — include the error text. • Plan, price or promo — name the plan and the promo code. Never pay a second time to "unstick" an invoice; check Premium Status first.

## Other
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/feedback_category_other_detail.html

Use Other for questions about accounts, language, partnerships, or anything the three main categories would file wrongly. Write a specific subject line — it becomes the ticket title and is what support scans first. If your question is actually a how-to, the Help Center will usually answer it faster: start from Getting Started or the FAQ.

## View My Feedback
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/feedback_view.html

Open the Support Bot ( @FastSchedulerSupport_bot ) and choose My requests . Every ticket you filed is listed with its subject, category and status. Tapping a ticket opens the full thread: your original message, any attachments, and support's replies. Replies also arrive as normal messages in that chat, so you can answer without opening the list again. In Fast Scheduler itself, Feedback only explains the route — there is no local ticket list. Status meanings: Status Meanings.

## History
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/feedback_history.html

Your ticket list is also a history of your account's problems. Before opening a new ticket, check whether the same issue was already reported and answered — the reply often contains the fix. For repeated failures (a channel that keeps rejecting posts, an import that keeps failing) include the earlier ticket reference in the new one. That gives support the context immediately.

## Status Meanings
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/feedback_status_help.html

• Open — received, waiting for a human reply. • Replied — support answered; read the thread and continue there if needed. • Closed — resolved. Reopening the same topic is usually slower than a new ticket with fresh details. • Spam — filtered out for abuse or duplication; it will not get a reply. Status changes do not send a separate notification for every step; the reply itself is the notification. Check My requests if you are unsure.

## Replies
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/feedback_reply.html

Support replies inside the same Support Bot chat. Answer there, in the same thread, instead of filing a new ticket — that keeps the history together. If a reply asks for a transaction ID, a job number or a screenshot, send exactly that. Most delays are missing details, not missing attention. Related: Status Meanings, Response Time.

## Attachments
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/feedback_file.html

You can attach a file while filing a ticket in the Support Bot — a screenshot, a CSV that failed to import, a backup that would not restore. Keep it relevant and small. **Never attach a file containing a bot token, password or backup encryption password.** Support never needs them, and a token in a chat is a security incident — see Token Safety. One attachment per issue is usually enough; if you need several, describe the order in the text.

# Frequently Asked Questions

## Frequently Asked Questions
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/faq.html

The FAQ is grouped so you can jump straight to the area you care about. Each group has its own questions and links to the full article behind the answer. Start with Scheduling, Sender Bots or Payments if you are in a hurry; Best Practices is the summary of everything this Help Center teaches.

## Scheduling FAQ
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/faq_schedule.html

Can I schedule several messages at once? Yes — send multiple blocks or dates in one flow, or import a file — Multi-Channel Scheduling, Import. Can I send media before the date? Yes, the media is held pending — Adding Photos &amp; Videos. How do I change a scheduled post? Message List → the message → Edit — Edit Messages. How do I delete one? Same screen, Delete , then confirm — Deleting a Message. Can I repeat a post automatically? Use a recurring message — Recurring Messages. What is the maximum caption length? Shorter than a text message; see Formatting.

Q: Do I need a sender bot to schedule messages?
A: Yes. After connecting a channel, connect a sender bot for it from Bots - scheduling unlocks once every channel has its own bot. Posts then appear from your bot's name, and you also get lower delivery delays and per-channel statistics.

Q: Can I edit a message after I schedule it?
A: Yes. Open Message List (or use /list ), tap the message, then Edit — you can change the text, the date/time, the media, or even the target channel. Use /edit with the job ID for a direct shortcut.

Q: How many scheduled messages can I store?
A: Free plan: 100 pending messages stored at once. Premium: unlimited . If you go over the free limit you will receive a notice listing the excess; messages stay frozen but are not deleted.

Q: How many messages can I send per month?
A: Free plan: 100 sent messages per channel per calendar month . Premium: unlimited sends. There is no daily cap on either plan.

Q: Can I schedule the same message to multiple channels?
A: Each scheduled message targets one channel. Free plan: 1 channel . Premium: up to 3 channels , each with its own sender bot, time zone, and signature.

Q: Can I schedule a poll or quiz?
A: Yes. Create the poll/quiz in any chat and forward it to the bot during scheduling — or build it right in the scheduling flow, where supported. Note: Telegram only allows anonymous polls in channels.

Q: What media can I attach to a scheduled message?
A: Photos, videos, GIFs, documents, and albums. Free plan videos: up to 25MB (no 4K). Premium: up to 50MB with 4K support. Use Normal, Random, or Sequential media modes.

Q: Can I schedule a recurring message (daily / weekly / monthly)?
A: Yes. Free plan: 1 recurring message . Premium: unlimited . Set the interval and time, then manage it (edit, pause, delete) from Message List .

Q: Can I use HH:MM to schedule for today?
A: Yes. When entering the date, a time in HH:MM format schedules the message for today at that time. Full dates like 2026-08-20 14:30 also work.

Q: Can I upload a .txt file to schedule many messages at once?
A: Yes. Send a .txt file and the bot parses it into multiple scheduled posts. This is the fastest way to build a month of content — combine it with the SetDate companion bot.

Q: What time zone is used for my scheduled times?
A: Each channel has its own time zone (set in Channel Settings ), which defaults to your account time zone. Verify the listed time zone before confirming a schedule.

Q: What happens if my Premium expires during a schedule?
A: Nothing is deleted right away. Messages to non-kept channels stop sending after a grace period, and you get a prompt to download a full .fsback backup you can restore later with /import .

Q: How do I see everything I have scheduled?
A: Open Message List (or /list ). You can preview, edit, pause, or delete any scheduled or recurring message there.

Q: Can I schedule a forwarded message?
A: Yes. During scheduling, forward a message from any chat — the bot copies its text and media into the scheduled post. You can edit the caption before confirming.

Q: Can I schedule an album of photos?
A: Yes. Send several photos together during the media step and choose Normal mode — they post as a single grouped album.

## Sender Bot FAQ
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/faq_bot.html

Why do I need a sender bot? So posts appear from your own bot's name and photo instead of the scheduler's — Connecting a Bot. Do I need one bot per channel? One bot can be assigned to one channel at a time; separate bots keep a ban isolated — How Posting Works. Where do I get a token? @BotFather → /newbot — Add a Sender Bot. The bot was promoted but posting fails. Check the specific rights — Permission. The token leaked. Revoke it in @BotFather and reconnect — Rotate Token.

Q: Why should I add a sender bot?
A: A sender bot is required for every channel - posts are sent through it, so they appear from your own bot's name with lower delivery delay and per-channel statistics. Connect one from Bots before scheduling.

Q: How do I create and connect a sender bot?
A: Create the bot with @BotFather ( /newbot ), add it as an admin in your channel, then enter its token in Sender Bots Management . One bot per channel.

Q: Why is my bot not posting?
A: Make sure the bot is an admin in the channel, the token is correct, the channel is connected, and you have not hit the Free plan monthly send cap (100 per channel).

## Payment FAQ
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/faq_payment.html
