## Best Practices
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/faq_best_practices.html

1. Set the time zone before the first post. 2. One sender bot per channel so failures stay isolated. 3. Preview everything — it is one tap and catches most mistakes. 4. Keep a media box of reusable files instead of re-uploading. 5. Space posts at least a minute apart in the same channel. 6. Duplicate rather than rewrite. 7. Clean the queue weekly with Message List and Search. 8. Back up before any mass change. Full guides: Getting Started, Scheduling Messages, Pro Tips.

Q: When is the best time to post?
A: Schedule at times your audience is active. Use your per-channel statistics to see which hours and days perform best.

Q: How should I structure a big campaign?
A: Space it over several days instead of one burst. Steady, consistent posting outperforms a random flood.

Q: Should I reuse media?
A: Yes — keep on-brand media in Media Storage and reuse it with Random or Sequential modes rather than re-uploading.

Q: Why back up before big changes?
A: A full .fsback backup lets you restore everything if something goes wrong during a rework, reconnection, or migration.

Q: What should I run as recurring?
A: Anything regular — daily quotes, weekly digests, monthly announcements. Recurring messages handle the rhythm so you only schedule the one-offs manually.

## How to Move Fast Scheduler to a New Phone or Another Telegram Account
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_move_channel_account.html

Fast Scheduler stores your schedules in the cloud (on the bot's server), not on your phone. That makes moving house surprisingly painless — the only thing that really matters is which Telegram account owns the schedules . Same account, new phone Do nothing. Open Telegram on the new phone, log in, and chat with @FastSchedulerBot — your channels, bots, schedules and settings are exactly where you left them. There is no local app and nothing to sync. Different account (new number, team handover, second project) Schedules belong to the Telegram account that created them, so a new account starts empty. The clean path: 1. On the old account: /backup → include everything → save the .fsback / .fspback file. 2. On the new account: /start the bot, connect the channel , then pair its sender bot (this is mandatory — the sender bot is what actually posts). 3. Send /import with the backup file, choose Add or Overwrite . 4. Check the Message List and Calendar; confirm the time zone matches, then skim the first few upcoming posts. If you are on Free and your setup has more than one channel, temporarily move the extra channels out or upgrade — the restore brings everything over, but Free limits apply on the new account. Handing a channel to someone else permanently The same flow works for handovers: the new owner connects their own account to the same channel (they need admin rights in it), pairs a sender bot, and imports the backup you send them. After they confirm the Message List looks right, you can delete your own schedules to avoid double-posting — two accounts scheduling the same channel will post twice .

Q: Will my schedules keep firing while I migrate?
A: Yes — the old account keeps posting until you delete its schedules or the channel/bot setup changes. Pause or delete there before going live on the new account to avoid duplicates.

Q: Do I need Premium on the new account to restore?
A: No. Importing a backup is free. Premium is only needed for creating backups and for the extra channels/bots the backup may contain.

## Why Is My Telegram Channel Posting Twice? (Duplicate Posts, Explained)
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_duplicate_posts.html

Double posts are annoying for subscribers and make a channel look automated in the worst way. The good news: the cause is nearly always one of four things. 1. Another account still schedules the channel The most common cause after a migration or team handover: the old account's schedules were never removed. Both accounts happily queue posts for the same time. Fix: in the other account, open Message List and delete its schedules (or disconnect the channel). If you cannot access the old account, remove the bot from the channel's admin list — that stops the posting immediately. 2. Two sender bots are admin in the channel Every channel must pair with exactly one sender bot, and that bot should be the only bot with posting rights. If you created a second bot and added it as admin, posts may arrive from both. Keep one sender bot per channel as admin; remove extra bots from the channel. 3. The message got scheduled twice Easy to do when re-sending the same text after an edit, or when importing while old schedules exist. Open the Message List for the day and scan for same-time twins before the posting window. The Calendar view makes clusters obvious. 4. The recurrence rule was duplicated, not edited Creating a new daily rule instead of editing the existing one produces two identical posts every day. Check the recurring list — if two rules share the same text and time, delete one. Still posting twice? Send /stats to see what is queued, then use /feedback with the channel name and two timestamps of a duplicate pair. Support can trace which connection produced each post.

Q: Does Fast Scheduler retry a post that failed, causing doubles?
A: A retry only happens when the send did not confirm. If Telegram accepted the post but the confirmation was lost (rare network hiccup), you can get one duplicate. It does not re-send confirmed posts.

Q: Can I merge two accounts scheduling the same channel?
A: Yes — export from the old account, import with Add on the new one, then clear the old account. Never leave both active.

## Telegram Channels vs Groups vs Bots: The Difference That Actually Matters
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tg_channels_explained.html

Telegram has three kinds of “places”, and content creators mix them up constantly. Here is the mental model that sticks. A channel is a megaphone One-way broadcasting: admins post, subscribers read. No reply threads by default (though a discussion group can be attached), unlimited subscribers, and posts carry the channel's name — or the name of the posting bot if “Sign messages with a bot” is on. Channels are where scheduled content lives. A group is a campfire Everyone talks. Groups are for community; up to 200k members in supergroups, full message history, topics if enabled. You do not “schedule to a group” the way you do to a channel — that is what channels are for. A bot is a worker Bots are accounts run by software. In your channel's context, a bot is the hands that type the message: a bot must be an admin with Post Messages for anything to be published. That is exactly why Fast Scheduler pairs a sender bot with your channel — your bot posts, under your brand. Why this matters for scheduling Want posts to appear at fixed times? Channel + scheduler + sender bot. Want subscribers to discuss the posts? Attach a linked discussion group to the channel — comments live there automatically. Want automation, menus, and commands? That is the bot layer — the part Fast Scheduler turns into a full publishing workflow. One nuance worth knowing: Telegram shows signed posts as “via bot” only when the admin chooses to sign with the bot; otherwise the post simply appears under the channel name. Either way, the sender bot did the typing.

Q: Can a scheduled post go to a group?
A: Fast Scheduler targets channels (including chat-announcement channels). Groups are conversational — schedule announcements to a channel instead.

Q: Do subscribers see which bot posted?
A: By default a channel post shows just the channel name. If the channel enables signing posts with the admin bot, the sender bot is credited.

## How Do I Schedule Many Telegram Posts at Once? (Bulk Scheduling with SetDate)
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_setdate_bulk.html

Scheduling one post is quick. Scheduling thirty — a week of content for a news channel, a course drip, a product launch sequence — needs a different tool: SetDate , the companion bot built for exactly this. The five-minute bulk workflow 1. Open SetDate. Open @SetDate_bot directly — or tap 📅 Use SetDate Bot whenever Fast Scheduler suggests it. 2. Feed it content. Send your text messages one after another — typed, pasted, or uploaded as a .txt file. Photos and videos are attached later, when you pick media options during import. 3. Choose a start date and how many posts should go out per day. 4. Define posting times — for example 09:00, 14:00 and 18:00 — and SetDate distributes your messages across that grid. 5. Send the batch back. One tap and every message appears in Fast Scheduler as a normal scheduled post, fully editable afterwards. Why this beats scheduling by hand One sitting instead of thirty. You write all content while you are in the writing mood, then let the grid place it. Perfect for recurring formats. A daily tip at 10:00 for the next two weeks is two fields in SetDate, not fourteen conversations. Everything stays editable. After import, each post is a regular scheduled message — search it, edit it, delete it, or move it in the calendar. Bulk for repeated content: recurring messages If the same message should repeat — a weekly digest, a daily reminder — you do not need bulk import at all: create a recurring message once and it reschedules itself. Free plans run 1 recurring message; Premium removes the cap (Unlimited) and its rules never expire. Tip: before importing a large batch, glance at your channel&rsquo;s time zone (see the time-zone guide) so the grid lands on the hours you actually meant.

Q: What is the SetDate bot?
A: SetDate is Fast Scheduler’s companion bot for bulk scheduling: you prepare many messages there, choose a start date and daily posting times, and import them all into Fast Scheduler in one click.

Q: Can I edit posts after bulk import?
A: Yes. Imported messages become ordinary scheduled messages — open the Message List or calendar and edit, move or delete any of them individually.

Q: How many posts can I import at once?
A: SetDate handles up to 500 posts (200,000 characters, 20 MB .txt) per batch. Imported messages also count against your scheduled-message limit (100 pending on Free, unlimited on Premium), so a batch that fits both caps can be imported in one go.

## Telegram Channel vs Group: What Is the Difference and Which One Do You Need?
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/tg_channel_vs_group.html

New Telegram creators constantly mix these up, and picking wrong shapes everything after it — including how you schedule. Here is the short, practical version. The one-line difference A channel is a megaphone: only admins publish, everyone else reads. A group is a round table: every member can post and reply. A channel can have a linked discussion group , which adds a comment thread under every channel post — the best of both worlds. Choose a channel when… You publish content to an audience: news, deals, tutorials, drops. You want a clean feed readers can scroll without chatter. You care about per-post view counts — channels show them, groups do not. Choose a group when… Conversation is the product: support, community, coordination. You want members to see each other and reply freely. The classic combo Most serious projects end up with both : a channel for polished posts, plus a linked discussion group for the conversation under them. Telegram links them in the channel settings; from then on every channel post automatically gets a comment thread. Where Fast Scheduler fits Fast Scheduler publishes to channels — that is where scheduled broadcast content belongs. Because it also tracks the discussion-group comments under the posts it publishes, your statistics cover the conversational side too: average comments per post and Top Commenters leaderboards work with the combo setup out of the box. The practical recipe: plan and queue polished posts in the channel, and let the linked group absorb the discussion they spark.

Q: Can Fast Scheduler post to groups?
A: Fast Scheduler schedules to channels, which is the broadcast use case it is built for. For community discussion, create a channel with a linked discussion group — comments there are tracked in your statistics.

Q: What is a discussion group in Telegram?
A: A group linked to your channel in channel settings. Every channel post gets a comment thread in that group, giving readers a place to reply without polluting the channel feed.

## What Is Fast Scheduler? The @FastSchedulerBot Explained
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_what_is_fast_scheduler.html

Fast Scheduler is a Telegram post scheduler bot — its handle is @FastSchedulerBot and its official site is fastscheduler.github.io . It queues and automatically publishes posts to Telegram channels: you write content when inspiration strikes, and the bot delivers it at the hour your audience actually reads. Telegram has no built-in scheduler for channels; Fast Scheduler is the tool that fills that gap. Which “Fast Scheduler” is this? Several unrelated products use the name Fast Scheduler . The one this page describes is the Telegram bot for scheduling channel posts , run by the Fast Scheduler team and reachable only at these official addresses: Bot: @FastSchedulerBot on Telegram (t.me/FastSchedulerBot). Support / feedback: @FastSchedulerSupport_bot . Official site and Help Center: fastscheduler.github.io . Companion bulk tool: @SetDate_bot . If a page about “Fast Scheduler” never mentions @FastSchedulerBot, @FastSchedulerSupport_bot or fastscheduler.github.io, it is describing a different product — Fast Scheduler is not affiliated with those tools. How it works in three roles The main bot (@FastSchedulerBot) is your control room: every conversation, every schedule, every statistic happens here. Your channel — connect it once by making the bots admins; the bot verifies rights and tracks it from then on. A sender bot — a small bot of your own (created in @BotFather in two minutes) that actually publishes the posts, so your channel&rsquo;s byline is your brand, not ours. Connecting one is required: scheduling unlocks only after each channel has a sender bot. What you can do with it Schedule anything — text, photos, videos, GIFs, voice, stickers, documents, polls, albums, with full formatting, spoilers and URL buttons. Recurring messages — a post that repeats daily, weekly or on custom patterns without re-scheduling. Batch scheduling — paste several date + post blocks in one Telegram message (or upload a .txt file) and queue all of them at once, on Free and Premium. See the batch format for the exact syntax and a copy-paste example. Statistics — views, comments and reactions per channel, with leaderboards of your top posts. Team features — admin permissions, shared channel limits, ownership transfer with confirmation phrases. Backups &amp; export — encrypted .fspback (Fast Scheduler Protected Backup) backups, JSON/CSV exports, migration between accounts. Free vs Premium, honestly Free : 1 channel and sender bot, 100 pending scheduled messages, 100 sends per channel per month, 1 recurring message — enough to run one channel seriously. Premium ($6.83/mo or $68.03/yr) : 3 channels and sender bots, unlimited scheduled queue, unlimited sends, unlimited recurring messages, bigger uploads (100 MB), leaderboards, backups and more. Batch messages, inline buttons and scheduling on both plans are not paywalled — the queue size is the difference. What the scheduling format looks like Scheduling is plain text. A post is a date and time on the first line and the content below it; a blank line starts the next post, so five posts can go in one message: today 10:23 Morning news digest: three stories worth your time &lt;inline&gt;Read more&lt;link="https://example.com/news"&gt; 12.12.2026 18:28 New drop is live. Limited stock, 24 hours only. Accepted times include today / tomorrow with a clock time, DD.MM.YYYY HH:MM , ISO dates and a bare HH:MM ; inline buttons use &lt;inline&gt;Text&lt;link="…"&gt; . See How to schedule many Telegram posts at once for every format and limit. Who it is for News channels that publish on rhythm, creators who batch their week in one sitting, shops running drops at precise hours, and community managers who share channels with a team. If you have ever set a 3 a.m. alarm to post manually — this bot is the cure. Start here: open @FastSchedulerBot , press Start, connect your channel, pair a sender bot, and schedule your first post before your coffee cools.

Q: Is Fast Scheduler free?
A: Yes — the Free plan runs one channel with 100 pending scheduled messages and 100 sends per channel per month, forever. Premium at $6.83/mo lifts every cap and adds statistics leaderboards, backups and bigger uploads.

Q: Why does Fast Scheduler need a sender bot?
A: Your sender bot publishes the posts, so your channel’s byline is your own brand instead of a third-party bot. It is created by you in @BotFather and connected in two minutes.

Q: Can Fast Scheduler send messages to a Telegram channel automatically?
A: Yes. That is its core purpose: scheduled messages publish automatically at their set time through your sender bot, including media, formatting and buttons.

Q: Is this Fast Scheduler the same as other apps called Fast Scheduler?
A: No. This is the Telegram post scheduler bot @FastSchedulerBot, documented at fastscheduler.github.io. Unrelated products share the name; they are not affiliated with this bot unless they link to @FastSchedulerBot.

Q: Can I schedule several posts at once in one message?
A: Yes. Send several date + text blocks separated by blank lines, or upload a .txt file with the same format. It works on Free and Premium; only the pending queue size differs.

# Text Commands

## Text Commands
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/commands.html

Every main-menu feature also has a command, which is faster on a desktop keyboard and works when a menu is buried. Commands are sent as ordinary messages in the bot chat; the bot replies in the same chat. Some need an argument — /edit 42 or /dub 42 — and a few open a small conversation instead, such as /schedule . The full list is in All Commands. If you are unsure which screen you need, the interface map shows the menus.

Q: What other features are available?
A: Search finds messages by keyword. Statistics shows your usage. Calendar gives a monthly overview.

Q: How do I find my messages?
A: Use Search (/search) to find by keyword, or Message List (/list) to browse all.

Q: What is /cancel used for?
A: /cancel stops any active operation and returns you to the main menu. Useful if the bot is waiting for input and you want to start over.

Q: How do I use a promo code?
A: Go to Premium → Redeem Promo Code, or use /promocode. Enter the code exactly as provided.

## All Commands
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/commands_list.html

Core • /start — open the main menu • /help — help entry point (redirects to the Support Bot) • /cancel — cancel the current operation • /skip — skip the current optional step Scheduling • /schedule — schedule a message • /recurring — create a recurring message • /edit — edit a scheduled message • /dub — duplicate a scheduled or recurring message • /delete — delete messages • /list — message list • /search — search messages • /calendar — month view Channels &amp; bots • /channel , /channels , /newchannel — connect or manage channels • /bots , /addbot , /listbots , /removebot — sender bots • /signature — signature settings Data &amp; tools • /data — import/export hub • /export , /import , /backup • /storage — media storage • /stats — usage statistics Account • /premium , /promocode , /referral • /language , /timezone • /feedback , /paysupport Administrator commands exist too but are not part of the user interface.

## /schedule
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/commands_schedule.html

/schedule starts the same conversation as the ➕ New button: choose the channel, send the content (text, media, album, poll, or a forwarded post), then send the date and time. You can send media before or after the date — the bot keeps it pending. /cancel aborts at any point and discards the draft. Step-by-step: One-Time Schedule. The date formats are in Date &amp; Time Formats.

## /search
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/commands_search.html

/search opens the search box. Send a word or phrase and the bot lists matching scheduled and recurring messages with job numbers and send times. A job number searches exactly. Results open the normal preview / edit / duplicate / delete controls. Full behaviour: Search. Storage search is separate — Search Storage.

## /edit
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/commands_edit.html

/edit &lt;job_id&gt; opens that message for editing. Without an ID the bot asks which message you mean. Editing keeps the same job and the same scheduled time unless you change the time explicitly. Media can be replaced during the edit. The button route is Message List → message → Edit ; see Edit Messages for what each edit changes.

## /dub
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/commands_dub.html

/dub &lt;job_id&gt; creates a copy of that scheduled or recurring message. The copy gets a new job number and, for one-time messages, moves to the next day so it does not collide with the original. Quotas still apply: a duplicate counts as a new pending message and must fit your plan's limits. If it does not, the bot shows the limit message instead of creating it. Full guide: Duplicate Posts.

## /cancel
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/commands_cancel.html

/cancel stops whatever conversation is open — scheduling, editing, importing, feedback — and returns to the main menu without saving the draft. It is safe: nothing half-finished is scheduled. If you already created a message and want it gone, delete it from the Message List instead — Deleting a Message.

## /data, /export, /import, /backup
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/commands_data.html

• /data — the hub screen with Export and Import . • /export — pick categories and a format, receive a file — Export. • /import — send a backup, text, CSV or JSON file — Import. • /backup — build a restorable snapshot — Create a Backup. All four end with a document in the chat. Save it off Telegram.

## /premium
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/commands_premium.html

/premium opens the Premium menu: your current status and expiry, the plan comparison, buying, promo code entry and the cancel button. It is also where your user ID is shown, which support asks for. If a payment did not activate Premium, check here before paying again. Details: Premium, Buy Premium, Premium Status.

## /referral
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/commands_referral.html

/referral shows your personal invite link, how many people joined through it, and the Premium days credited. Share the exact link — it carries your ID, which is how credit is matched. Verification rules and abuse limits are in Rules. Start: How Referrals Work.

## Settings
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/commands_settings.html

⚙️ Settings in the main menu holds the account-level preferences: • Language — interface language. • Time Zone — the zone used to read the times you type. • Signature — per-channel sign-off (Premium). • Data tools and the feedback route. Channel-specific settings (zone, signature, admin roles) are on the channel card, not here — Manage Channels. See Settings &amp; Configuration.

## /language
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/commands_language.html

/language opens the language list. Pick one and the interface switches immediately — menus, buttons and help texts. It does not translate your posts; content is sent exactly as you wrote it. The Support Bot keeps its own setting. More: Change Language, Languages.

## /help
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/commands_help.html

In Fast Scheduler, /help does not open a local article list. It replies with a short message and a button that opens the Support Bot ( @FastSchedulerSupport_bot ), which contains the full Help Center, the AI topic finder and the feedback form. You can also open the website Help Center — every article in the Support Bot has an Open in Web button pointing at it. The same articles are browsable at Getting Started in this site.

# Troubleshooting

## Troubleshooting
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/errors.html

Most problems fall into five buckets: 1. Nothing was sent — the message is not there, or the sender bot lost admin rights — No Post Sent. 2. It was sent late or early — almost always a time zone difference — Late Post. 3. Media failed — the file was deleted, replaced or too large — Media Fails. 4. Permission errors — the bot is not an admin, or your role lacks the right — Permission. 5. The bot itself is unreachable — Bot Down. Each article ends with what to send support if the fix does not work.

Q: How do I exit a stuck flow?
A: Use the /cancel command at any time to exit the current operation and return to the main menu.

Q: Payment went through but Premium didn't activate
A: Wait 2-3 minutes — there can be a small delay with some payment providers. If still not active after 5 minutes, check with /premium . If Premium still shows as inactive, contact @MaximalXP with your user ID, payment method, and transaction details.

Q: I used a referral link but didn't get Premium days
A: Referral Premium days are only credited when the referred person 1) is a NEW user (never used the bot before), and 2) connects a channel. Just starting the bot with the link is not enough. Check /referral to see your status. Contact @MaximalXP if requirements were met.

Q: My scheduled messages stopped sending
A: Check: 1) Your sender bot is still connected and is admin in the channel. 2) You haven't hit the Free plan monthly send cap (100 per channel). 3) The channel hasn't been removed. 4) Your Premium hasn't expired (if you had channels above the free limit). Use /stats to check your status.

Q: I accidentally deleted something — can I recover it?
A: If you have a backup (.fsback or .fspback file), you can restore it with /import . Without a backup, deleted data cannot be recovered. We recommend regular exports to avoid data loss.

Q: How do I delete my account or all my data?
A: Contact @MaximalXP directly to request account deletion. You can also manually delete your data using the export/backup feature first to keep a copy. Your scheduled messages, media, and settings will be permanently removed.

Q: Can I get a refund for Premium?
A: Premium is non-refundable once it has been delivered. The only case we refund is non-delivery — you paid and Premium was never activated (or the same period was charged twice) — and such a request must reach us within 7 days of that payment . Email fastschedulebot@gmail.com with the transaction ID, your Telegram username, the payment date and what did not arrive — we acknowledge within 7 business days .

Q: My bot token was revoked by @BotFather
A: If you reset your bot token in @BotFather, the old token stops working immediately. Go to Bots → 🔁 Replace Token under the bot and enter the new token from @BotFather. Your scheduled messages will resume once the new token is saved.

## Common Errors
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/error_common.html

• "Bot is not an administrator" — promote the sender bot in the channel. • "Not enough rights to send" — the bot can read but not post; enable post messages. • "Chat not found" — the channel was deleted, the bot was removed, or the username changed. • "Message is too long" — captions have a much smaller limit than text messages; shorten the caption. • "File is too large" — over your plan's media limit. • "Too many requests" — Telegram rate limiting; wait and retry. Categories: Channel Errors, Media Errors, Rate Limited, Timeouts, Network Errors.

## Network Errors
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/error_network.html

A network error means the request never reached Telegram or the reply never came back. The bot retries automatically for transient failures. What you can do • Wait a minute and check the Message List — the post may have gone out. • Do not reschedule immediately; that is how duplicates appear. • If it repeats for every post, report it with the time and channel. Duplicates: Duplicate Posts.

## Timeouts
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/error_timeout.html

Timeouts usually happen on heavy files or big imports. The action may still complete after the message says it failed. Check before retrying • Message List — did the message appear? • Storage — did the upload land? • Import report — were rows created? If nothing happened, retry once with a smaller file or fewer rows.

## Rate Limited
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/error_rate.html

Telegram limits how fast a bot may post to a channel. Sending many messages in the same minute, or a media group right after a text post, can hit that limit. Avoid it • Space posts at least a minute apart in the same channel. • Keep albums and text posts in separate minutes. • Do not delete and re-create a message repeatedly. The bot waits and retries when Telegram asks it to; a persistent limit means the schedule is too dense — see Same-Day Limits.

## Media Errors
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/error_media.html

Common causes • The file exceeds your plan's limit — Media Limit. • The stored item was deleted from a box — schedules fall back to text-only (Delete Media). • The format is unsupported as a photo; send it as a document. • The caption is longer than the caption limit for that media type. Retrying the same oversized file will fail again. Re-upload a smaller version or attach from storage — Using From Storage.

## Channel Errors
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/error_channel.html

• Chat not found — the channel was deleted, made private and the bot removed, or renamed. Reconnect it — Add a Channel. • Not enough rights — the bot is an admin without the post permission. Fix it in channel settings — Channel Permissions. • Wrong channel — the message belongs to another channel in your account; check the channel name on the preview. Sender-bot specifics: How Posting Works.

## Forbidden
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/error_forbidden.html

A forbidden error means Telegram rejected the request, not that the network failed. The usual reasons: the bot was removed or blocked, the channel is restricted, or the token was revoked in @BotFather. Fix 1. Check the bot is still a member/admin of the channel. 2. If the token was reset, reconnect the bot — Rotate Token. 3. If the channel is restricted, only Telegram support can lift it. Why posting needs a sender bot: Connecting a Bot.

## Payment Errors
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/error_payment.html

• Payment window closed — invoices expire; start a new one from Buy Premium. • Stars balance too low — top up in Telegram, then retry. • Paid but still Free — check Premium Status; activation is normally instant, and a refresh of the Premium menu re-reads it. • Charged twice — do not buy again; contact support with both transaction IDs — Payment Issues. Refund rules: Refunds.

## No Post Sent
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/troubleshoot_nopost.html

Work through this list in order: 1. Is it still in the Message List? If yes, it was not sent; if no, it either sent or was deleted. 2. Is the sender bot still an admin? A channel admin change silently removes posting rights. 3. Did the channel change? Renamed, made private, or migrated — the connection points at the old chat. 4. Was Premium active? After expiry, frozen channels stop sending — Premium Expiry. 5. Was the time zone changed? The post may be queued for later than you expect. Still missing? Send the job number and the scheduled time through Support.

## Late Post
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/troubleshoot_late.html

The scheduler sends at the moment it recorded. If the wall clock in the channel looks wrong, the recorded moment is off — almost always a time zone mismatch. Check • Your account zone: Set Time Zone. • The channel's own zone on its card — it overrides the account zone for that channel. • Daylight saving changes since you scheduled. • A message imported from a file written in another zone — CSV Import. Related: Why Was My Post Published at the Wrong Time?.

## Media Fails
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/troubleshoot_media.html

If a message arrived as text only, its media reference was lost. Causes • The storage item was deleted — schedules fall back to text instead of failing (Delete Media). • The item was replaced and the new file is unsupported or too large. • Telegram no longer holds the original file. • The caption exceeded the media caption limit, so the text was split. Re-attach the media by editing the message — Edit Messages.

## Permission
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/troubleshoot_perm.html

Two different permission systems can block an action: • Telegram channel rights — the sender bot must be an admin with permission to post. Fix in channel settings. • Bot roles — in a sender-bot context, your role must include the action (schedule, delete, export…). Ask the owner — Sender Bot Permissions. If the bot is promoted but still refused, check the specific checkbox: 'post messages' is separate from 'edit messages' and 'delete messages'.

## Bot Down
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/troubleshoot_bot.html

If the bot does not reply to /start at all: 1. Check your internet and try Telegram desktop. 2. Check whether you blocked the bot — open the chat and press Restart . 3. Wait a few minutes; short restarts happen. 4. If the Support Bot also does not answer, the outage is on the service side. Scheduled posts are stored server-side and are not lost while the bot restarts; they send once it is back, within the same minute if possible.

Q: What do I do when a bot seems offline?
A: Reconnect the sender bot from Sender Bots and confirm it's a channel admin. Telegram restarts bots periodically — wait a few minutes before retrying.

## Scheduled Message Didn’t Post? The 6 Real Causes
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_post_not_sent.html

When a post misses its slot, the cause is almost always in the delivery chain — the schedule itself is the least likely suspect. Work this list top to bottom; each item fixes the majority of cases. 1. The sender bot lost its admin seat Someone cleaned up admins and removed your sender bot. Check Manage Channel → Administrators : your sender bot must be there with Post Messages . Re-add it, and the queue resumes. 2. The token was revoked or replaced A /revoke in @BotFather kills the old token everywhere instantly. If the bot shows the sender as disconnected, open Bots → 🔁 Replace Token under the bot and paste the fresh token. 3. Permissions were narrowed Admin exists but without Post Messages — a silent killer after permission tightening. Open the admin entry and re-enable posting. 4. The channel changed identity Username changed or the channel was converted — the old link no longer resolves. Reconnect the channel; schedules are kept. 5. Telegram rate limits on bursts Telegram throttles aggressive posting bursts channel-wide. If several posts fire close together and one fails, it is usually this. Space posts by minutes, not seconds — the scheduler already does, but third-party bots added to the channel can collide with it. 6. The monthly send cap (Free) On Free, sends pause at 100 per channel per month until the 1st. The bot warns you before the cap; /stats shows the counter. Premium lifts the cap entirely. Fastest diagnosis Send /stats (status of everything) and check the sender-bot status screen. Still mysterious? /feedback with the channel and the missed time — support can see delivery attempts and will tell you exactly which step failed.

Q: Will missed posts send later automatically?
A: A post that failed delivery is marked failed, not silently retried forever. Fix the underlying cause, then delete it and schedule it again.

Q: How do I know if it was the monthly cap?
A: The bot notifies you at the cap, and /stats shows monthly usage per channel. If neither shows the cap, it was delivery-side — start the checklist from the top.

# Privacy

## Privacy
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/privacy.html

The bot stores what it needs to run your schedule: • Telegram identifiers — your user ID, and the IDs of channels you connect. • Your content — message texts, media references, poll and button data. • Settings — language, time zone, signature, and the bot tokens you connect (stored encrypted). • Operational records — delivery results, used for statistics and troubleshooting. What it never does • It does not read channels it is not connected to. • It does not post anything you did not schedule. • It does not sell or share your data with advertisers. The binding document is the website Privacy Policy — Privacy Policy. Data controls: Your Data, Delete Account.

## Your Data
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/privacy_data.html

• Messages you schedule — text, media references, buttons, polls, times. • Channels and bots — IDs, usernames, which bot posts where. • Preferences — language, time zone, signature. • Storage — box names and media references. • Money trail — Premium status and expiry, promo and referral credit. • Support tickets you send through the Support Bot. Everything is tied to your Telegram user ID. There is no email/password account — your Telegram identity is the account. Export or back it up: Export, Create a Backup.

## Consent
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/privacy_consent.html

Using the bot means you agree to it storing the data needed to deliver your posts, and to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy on the website. You can withdraw by deleting your data and stopping use — see Delete Account. Withdrawal does not undo completed payments; those follow Refunds. Legal texts: Terms, Privacy Policy.

## Third Parties
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/privacy_thirdparty.html

• Telegram — the platform that delivers every message and holds media files. Its own privacy policy applies to the chat itself. • Payment providers — Telegram Stars processes payments; the bot never sees card data. • Hosting — the server that runs the bot stores its database. There are no advertising networks receiving your content. Support tickets are read by the support team to answer you.

## Export Data
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/privacy_export.html

Two routes: • Readable copy — Data → Export , choose categories and a format (Export). • Restorable snapshot — /backup , giving a .fsback (Create a Backup). Export is the honest answer to "what do you have about me": it contains exactly the records described in Your Data.

## Delete Account
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/privacy_delete.html

Account deletion is handled by a human, because it is irreversible. Contact @MaximalXP on Telegram or email fastschedulebot@gmail.com from the account in question, and state clearly that you want the account and its data deleted. What is removed Scheduled and recurring messages, storage entries, settings, channel and bot connections, referral data. Before you ask • Take a backup if you might return. • Request any refund before deletion — a deleted account cannot be refunded afterwards. Full procedure: the website Privacy Policy, Privacy Policy.

## Token Safety
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/security_token.html

A sender bot's token lets anyone post as that bot. Treat it like a password: • Never post it in a group, screenshot or support chat. Support never asks for it. • If it leaks, open @BotFather → /mybots → your bot → API Token → Revoke current token , then reconnect the new token — Rotate Token. • Backups that include tokens are forced into the encrypted .fspback format — Backup Password. The bot stores tokens encrypted and uses them only to post to your channels.

Q: Should I keep my bot token secret?
A: Absolutely. Never share your sender bot token or payment details in chat. Anyone with a token could post to your channels.

## Account Safety
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/security_2fa.html

Your bot account is only as safe as your Telegram account. • Enable two-step verification in Telegram Settings → Privacy and Security. • Review Active Sessions and end anything unfamiliar. • Do not sign in to Telegram on shared devices. • If your account is compromised, revoke sender-bot tokens in @BotFather — an attacker with your session can post through them. Token handling: Token Safety.

Q: Do I need Telegram two-step verification?
A: Recommended. Two-step verification protects your Telegram login — and therefore your bot access and connected channels — from unauthorized use.

## Data Safety
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/security_data.html

• Access to the database is limited to the service operators. • Bot tokens are stored encrypted, not in plain text. • Backups you create are yours; the encrypted form is unreadable without your password. • Support sees only what you send in a ticket. You control the copies you download — keep them somewhere safe and keep .fspback passwords in a password manager. See also Your Data and Backup Password.

Q: Where is my data stored?
A: Your data is stored by the bot and used only to run schedules. Export or backup your data anytime, and contact support for data-related requests.

## How Do I Delete My Fast Scheduler Account and All My Data?
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_delete_data.html

You can leave Fast Scheduler completely — no subscriptions to cancel by email, no dark patterns, no &ldquo;are you sure&rdquo; maze. One message, and everything tied to your Telegram account is erased. How to request deletion Contact @MaximalXP in Telegram and ask to delete your account. Deletion is permanent and covers all data associated with your user ID: scheduled and recurring messages, media storage, sender-bot tokens, channel connections, settings, statistics and referral records. Export first — deletion has no undo Before deleting, create a backup with /backup (a Premium toolkit) or export individual lists, so your content plan survives the account. Once deletion runs, there is no recovery path — the data no longer exists to restore. What happens on Telegram&rsquo;s side Your sender bots keep existing in @BotFather — they are your bots, created with your account. If you want them gone too, revoke or delete them there after deletion. Revoke first if you plan to keep using them elsewhere. The bot loses admin rights relevance immediately, but you can also remove @FastSchedulerBot and your sender bot from your channels&rsquo; admin lists yourself — a good hygiene step that takes ten seconds per channel. Already-published posts stay in your channel, of course — deletion cannot rewrite history. How long data is kept normally While you are an active user, every category of data is kept only while it is useful: schedules until they are deleted or sent, bot tokens until you disconnect the bot, and account records until you delete the account. The Privacy Policy&rsquo;s retention table lists each category with its exact lifetime.

Q: Who do I contact to delete my Fast Scheduler account?
A: Message @MaximalXP on Telegram and request account deletion. The deletion is permanent and removes all data linked to your Telegram ID.

Q: Can I delete everything but keep the bot?
A: Yes — you can delete individual schedules, media and sender bots from inside the bot without deleting your account. Full deletion is only for leaving the service entirely.

Q: Should I export a backup before deleting?
A: Definitely. After deletion there is no way to restore anything, so create a backup with /backup first if there is any chance you will return.

# Legal & Terms

## Legal & Terms
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/legal.html

• Terms of Service — rules for using the bot, plan limits, fair use, and what happens on abuse — Terms. • Privacy Policy — what data is stored, why, and your rights — Privacy Policy. • Refund Policy — Premium is non-refundable except non-delivery, within 7 days of the payment — Refunds. All three live on the website with effective dates, and earlier versions are kept in the version history. The October 2026 refresh is summarised in October 2026 Policy Refresh. Short version: schedule only content you have the right to publish, follow Telegram's own rules, and refunds follow the published policy.

## Privacy Policy
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/legal_privacy.html

The Privacy Policy is published on the website and is the authoritative text. It covers what is collected, the legal bases, retention, processors, international transfers and your rights. This Help Center summarises it — the summary is friendly, the policy is binding. When they differ, the policy wins. Details: Privacy Details, GDPR, Your Data.

## Privacy Details
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/legal_privacy_detail.html

• Data is kept while your account exists and while it is needed to deliver scheduled posts. • Deleting a message removes it from the schedule; media references may persist in Telegram itself. • Account deletion removes your records; backups you downloaded are outside the service's control. • Data-protection contact: fastschedulebot@gmail.com . The website Privacy Policy states exact retention periods and the processors involved — Privacy Policy.

## Legal Terms
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/legal_terms.html

The Terms of Service on the website are the binding agreement. In plain language, they require that you: • own or have permission to publish the channels you connect; • post only content you have the right to post; • follow Telegram's Terms and channel rules; • not abuse referrals, payments, trials or the service itself. Plan limits and fair-use rules are part of the agreement — Limits. Details: Terms Details.

## Terms Details
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/legal_terms_detail.html

• Fair use — automated bulk posting that violates Telegram's rules can get a channel restricted; the bot cannot prevent that. • Suspension — accounts that abuse payments, referrals or other users can be suspended. • Availability — the service aims for continuous operation but does not guarantee uninterrupted delivery; Telegram outages are outside its control. • Liability — limited as described in the Terms. The full text, with the effective date, is the authoritative version — Legal Terms.

## Your Data
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/legal_data.html

You can: • Access — export everything — Export. • Correct — edit or delete messages and settings in the bot. • Erase — request account deletion — Delete Account. • Object or restrict — write to the data-protection contact. Requests are answered within the timeframe required by applicable law; complex requests can take longer, as described in the policy.

## GDPR
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/legal_gdpr.html

If you are in the EEA or the UK, the GDPR (and the UK GDPR) gives you rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability and objection. • Access and portability — Export gives you the data in machine-readable form. • Erasure — Delete Account. • Anything else — email fastschedulebot@gmail.com from the account in question. The website Privacy Policy names the controller and the supervisory route for complaints — Privacy Policy.

## Legal Contact
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/legal_contact.html

For legal notices, privacy requests, or data deletion, contact @MaximalXP on Telegram or email fastschedulebot@gmail.com . Include your Telegram user ID (shown in /premium ) and a clear description of the request. Deletion requests must come from the account they concern. Ordinary support questions are faster through the Support Bot — Send Feedback.

## October 2026 Policy Refresh
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/legal_update.html

The October 2026 refresh updated the three public documents: • Terms — clarified plan limits, fair use and suspension. • Privacy Policy — clarified retention, processors and the data-protection contact. • Refund Policy — Premium is non-refundable except non-delivery, and a non-delivery request must reach us within 7 days of the payment. Earlier versions remain readable in the website version history, so you can compare what changed. Documents: Terms, Privacy Policy, Refund Policy.

Q: Do I need to accept the updated policies?
A: No extra tap is needed. Per the Terms, material changes are announced in-app, and continued use after the effective date means acceptance. If you disagree, stop using the service and export or delete your data first.

Q: Where can I read the previous versions?
A: On the website under Legal → version history. Every past version stays published with its effective date, so changes are auditable.

Q: Did the refund rules change?
A: The October 2026 text states the rule plainly: Telegram Stars purchases are final, Premium is non-refundable once delivered, and the only exception is non-delivery , which must be requested within 7 days of the payment. The request address is fastschedulebot@gmail.com and we acknowledge within 7 business days.

# Contact & Support

## Contact & Support
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/contact.html

• Support Bot — @FastSchedulerSupport_bot , the fastest route. Send /feedback in Fast Scheduler to get there with one tap — Send Feedback. • Telegram — @MaximalXP for direct contact — Telegram Support. • Email — fastschedulebot@gmail.com for formal requests and payments — Email. Before writing, search the Help Center: most questions are already answered in Getting Started, Troubleshooting or the FAQ.

## Support
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/contact_support.html

• How-to question — the Help Center or the Support Bot's AI topic finder. • Bug — a ticket through the Support Bot, with a screenshot. • Payment or refund — the payment category in the Support Bot, or /paysupport . • Legal, privacy, deletion — @MaximalXP or email. One channel per issue is enough; asking in three places slows the answer.

## Telegram Support
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/contact_telegram.html

The fastest human contact is @MaximalXP on Telegram. Send: • your user ID (visible in /premium ), • a one-paragraph description of the problem, • the exact error text or a screenshot, • the channel name, if a post is involved. For tickets you want tracked with a status, use the Support Bot instead — Send Feedback.

## Email
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/contact_email.html

Email fastschedulebot@gmail.com for formal requests, partnerships, payment problems and privacy requests. Include: • your Telegram user ID (from /premium ), • a clear subject line, • for payments: the transaction ID, purchase date and plan, • screenshots or links where relevant. Email is answered more slowly than the Support Bot. Refund rules: Refunds.

## Report a Bug
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/contact_bug.html

Route: /feedback in Fast Scheduler → the button to the Support Bot → new request → Bug . Include • What you did, button by button. • What happened — the exact error text. • The job number and the scheduled time, if a post is involved. • The channel and sender bot names. • A screenshot if the problem is visual. What happens next: the ticket gets a status you can follow in My requests — Status Meanings.

## Request a Feature
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/contact_feature_detail.html

Route: /feedback → Support Bot → new request → Feature request . A request that gets built usually contains: • the task you are trying to do, • how often you need it, • the workaround you use today, • an example (a screenshot of the spreadsheet you maintain by hand is gold). Check first whether the feature exists under another name — Media Modes, Duplicates, Recurring Messages.

## Response Time
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/contact_response.html

• Support Bot tickets — usually within a day or two; Premium reports are looked at first. • Direct Telegram — often within hours on weekdays. • Email — 1–3 business days. The biggest factor is not the queue, it is the detail: a ticket with a job number, a screenshot and an exact time is often resolved in one reply. Refund acknowledgement: within seven business days — Refunds.

# Settings & Configuration

## Settings & Configuration
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/config.html

Settings are split between your account and each channel. ## Account settings Open ⚙️ Settings (right button on the sender bot's page 2) or send /settings : • 🌐 Language — interface language. • 🕐 Time Zone — the default zone. • 💾 Media Storage — your reusable files. • 📝 Signature — a footer for posts (Premium). • ⭐ Premium — plan and payment. • 🎁 Referral Program — invite link and rewards. • 📮 Feedback — opens the support entry point. • 📋 All commands — the full command list. ## Channel settings In the sender bot, the left ⚙️ Settings : • 🔒 Hide channel from strangers / 🔓 Show — Public Mode. • 👥 Admins — owner-only co-admin management. • 🏠 Open @FastSchedulerBot — back to the hub. ## Channel-level values Time zone, signature, sender bot and admins belong to the channel, not the account. Change them from the channel card or the sender bot, not from account settings. ## Commands as shortcuts /language , /timezone , /signature , /storage , /commands open the same screens. The full list is in All Commands. Related: Every Menu and Button, Settings.

Q: Why do language and time zone appear in two places?
A: They are account defaults. Channels can override the time zone, and signatures are per channel, which is why channel settings exist separately.

## How to Add an Automatic Signature to Every Telegram Post
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/qa_signature_guide.html

A signature is the footer that appears under every post in a channel: credit, CTA, hashtags, promo. Set it once in Fast Scheduler and every scheduled message carries it — you stop copy-pasting “@yourchannel” to the end of everything. Setting it up 1. Open Signature via /signature (or tap 📝 Signature on the review screen). Premium feature. 2. Pick the channel — signatures are per channel , so your main channel can carry a promo while the announcements channel stays clean. 3. Send the text. Formatting works: bold , italic , links, even emoji-free minimalism if that is your style. From the next send onward, the signature is appended to every post in that channel. Existing scheduled posts pick it up automatically at send time — no need to reschedule anything. What belongs in a good signature The channel handle — the classic “@yourchannel” line, since forwarded copies keep the credit. One action — “Reply to buy”, “Details: link”. A signature with three CTAs has zero. Hashtags for navigation — if the channel uses tag-indexing, the signature is the perfect place for the constant ones. Changing and removing The same menu edits or clears the signature; clearing stops appending immediately (again, applied at send time, so posts already published keep their footer — that is a feature, not a bug). Per-channel control means experimenting is cheap.

Q: Can I use different signatures for different channels?
A: Yes — signatures are configured per channel. Each connected channel gets its own text (or none).

Q: Does the signature count toward the message length?
A: It is part of the final message text, so extremely long signatures can hit Telegram’s 4096-character limit on top of long posts. Short signatures are better anyway.

# More topics

## Connecting a Bot
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/connect_bot.html

A sender bot is a Telegram bot you create and own. Fast Scheduler uses its token to send your posts, so the author of every post is your bot rather than the shared scheduling bot. ## Create the token 1. Open @BotFather . 2. Send /newbot , choose a display name, then a username ending in bot . 3. Copy the token (format 1234567890:ABCdef… ). Treat it like a password. ## Connect it 🤖 Bots → 🔑 I Have a Token → send the token. The bot verifies it and shows which bot it belongs to. If you already sent a token for another bot, it asks whether to replace it. ## Attach the channel One bot = one channel. Easiest: open the sender bot and tap the green ➕ Add bot to a channel button — Telegram's picker pre-selects administrator rights. The bot re-checks on its own after 10 seconds (5 automatic checks per day). ## If it is still not an administrator Channel → Administrators → Add Administrator → your bot → Post Messages . Return to the bot and press 🔄 Check Again . The main bot does not need to be added. ## What moves into the sender bot Scheduling, recurring messages, the message list, statistics, calendar and channel settings (Hide channel, Admins). This is per-channel isolation: two channels cannot see each other's queues. ## Limits Free: 1 bot. Premium: 3 bots. The bot list shows the count and each bot's channel. ## Managing it later 🤖 Bots → a bot → ⚙ Manage : • 🔑 Change token — same bot, new token. • 🔁 Replace bot — a different bot takes over; data moves. • 🔀 Switch channel — point this bot at another of your channels. • ⇄ Swap bots — exchange channels between two bots. • 🗑 Remove bot — detach it from the channel. ## Troubleshooting • Invalid token — incomplete copy. Copy the full line. • Bot is not admin — promote your bot in the channel; the main bot's rights are irrelevant here. • Bot limit reached — Sender Bot Limit. • Posts still come from the old name — check which bot is attached on the channel card; a replaced bot may still be the channel's admin (harmless, but remove it from Telegram's admin list for clarity). ## Related Add a Sender Bot, Manage Sender Bots, How Posting Works: Sender Bots, Bot Permissions.

Q: Does the sender bot need to be online?
A: No. Fast Scheduler keeps the token and posts through the Bot API directly. The bot does not need a running process of yours.

Q: Is my token stored safely?
A: Tokens are stored server-side and are never shown back in full. Exports containing tokens are always encrypted as a Protected Backup (.fspback) with a password you choose.

## Connecting a Channel
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/connect_channel.html

A connection is a three-way agreement: your Telegram account is an admin, @FastSchedulerBot is an admin with posting rights, and the bot can resolve which channel you mean. ## Requirements • You are an administrator of the channel. • @FastSchedulerBot is an administrator with at least Post Messages . • For posting through a sender bot, that bot is also an admin with Post Messages. ## Connect in the bot 📢 Channels → 📢 Connect Channel , then send: • @yourchannel • https://t.me/yourchannel • an invite link • a forwarded post from the channel • the numeric ID, e.g. -1001234567890 Forwarding works for private channels and is the most reliable method: it carries the channel identity without exposing a username. ## What happens after connecting The channel appears in the overview with its time zone and a "no sender bot" state. Scheduling is locked until a sender bot is attached — that is the next step: Step 2: Connect a Sender Bot. ## Multiple channels Free plan: 1 channel. Premium: up to 3 . Every channel has its own sender bot, time zone, signature, queue and statistics. Use the channel picker before scheduling to choose where a post goes; managed channels appear as 🤖 Managed: … and redirect to their sender bot. ## Per-channel details on the card Open the channel from 📢 Channels to see its sender bot, time zone and counts. Actions: • 🕐 Time Zone: … — set the channel's own zone. • 🔄 Change Channel — move the sender bot to another channel you own. • 🔗 Disconnect Channel — remove the link; queued posts pause, nothing is lost. ## Exact errors and fixes • "Bot is not an admin" — promote @FastSchedulerBot with Post Messages, then send the channel again. • "Channel not found" — wrong username or a private channel; forward a post. • "Invalid format" — send the link alone, or the @username alone. • "You are not an admin of this channel" — ask the owner to promote you. • "This channel is already connected" — it belongs to this account already; open it from the channel overview instead of adding it twice. ## Related Add a Channel, Channel Permissions, Unlink vs Delete, Remove a Channel.

Q: Why can’t I schedule right after connecting?
A: Because the channel has no sender bot yet. Add one from 🤖 Bots → 🔑 I Have a Token and make it an administrator of the channel.

Q: Can two accounts manage one channel?
A: Ownership belongs to the account that connected it. Other people can be added as channel admins inside the sender bot with limited permissions, but not as a second independent Fast Scheduler owner.

## Step 1: Connect Your Sender Bot
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/gs_step1.html

Every channel is served by its own sender bot: a Telegram bot you own that posts under its own name. The setup therefore starts with it. ## Why your own bot • Posts appear from your bot's name and photo, not from a shared bot. • No shared queue, so delivery does not wait behind other channels. • Statistics, leaderboards, backups and admin management live in that bot. • Inline buttons on posts work through your bot. ## Do it 1. 🤖 Bots → 🔑 I Have a Token , or ➕ Create bot to be walked through @BotFather. 2. Send the token as one message. The bot calls Telegram to verify it and shows the username. 3. Tap the green Open @your_bot button. The channel and the time zone are connected inside that bot. ## Next Step 2: Connect the Channel and Set the Time Zone.

## Step 2: Connect the Channel and Set the Time Zone
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/gs_step2.html

Open the sender bot. Because it has no channel yet it shows the "I'm live" screen, not a dashboard. ## Add it to the channel • Green ➕ Add bot to a channel — Telegram's picker opens with the bot pre-selected as an administrator and Post Messages ticked. • Or forward a post from the channel, or send its @username / t.me link. • Private channel: add the bot as an administrator from the channel's own settings; it detects that on its own. ## The automatic check After the button, the bot re-checks once after 10 seconds and continues by itself. The automatic check is capped at 5 per day ; after that use 🔄 Check Again , which is unlimited. ## The time zone A city, your current time, a shared location or the list. It is stored for this channel only; other channels keep their own zone and the account default is written only if it is still empty. ## Next Step 3: Schedule a Message.

## Step 3: Schedule a Message
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/gs_step3.html

This is the actual job: queue a post. Run it inside the sender bot for the channel, because that is where the channel's scheduling lives. ## 1. Open the scheduler Tap 📅 Schedule a Message , or send /schedule . The prompt shows the accepted format with an example. ## 2. Send the date and the post The first line is the date and time; everything after it is the post: 25.12.2026 10:00 Happy holidays from our channel! Accepted date forms: • DD.MM.YYYY HH:MM — 25.12.2026 10:00 • DD/MM/YYYY , DD-MM-YYYY • ISO YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM — 2026-12-25 10:00 • today 18:00 , tomorrow 09:00 , day after tomorrow 09:00 • a bare time, e.g. 09:00 or 9:00 PM — means today, and rolls to tomorrow automatically if that time already passed • 12-hour times with AM/PM are understood; without a suffix the bot picks the next sensible reading. If the date is in the past the bot refuses with "Date is in the past" and keeps the flow open so you can send a corrected line. ## 3. Several posts in one message Separate messages with a blank line. Every block starts with its own date line: 25.12.2026 10:00 First post 26.12.2026 10:00 Second post You can send more blocks afterwards; the bot keeps a pending count. A .txt file with the same blank-line rule works too. ## 4. Media (optional) After the text the bot offers media modes: 📷 Normal , 🎲 Random , 🔀 Sequential , ⏭ Skip Photos , and 💾From storage when storage is enabled. Send the files, then tap ✅ Done (N) . Plain text needs no files — tap Skip Photos. Full explanation: Media Modes Explained. ## 5. Review and confirm The review card shows the channel(s), the exact time, a preview, the media count and the number of inline buttons. Use: • ✏️ Edit — replace the text (and optionally the time); • 💾 Change media — swap the attached files; • 📢 Change channel — send to a different channel; • 📢 Choose channels — several channels at once (Premium); • ✅ Schedule — commit. ❌ Cancel stops without saving. ## 6. Check that it exists 📋 Message List → Scheduled messages shows it with an ID; 📅 Calendar shows it on its day. From there you can preview, edit, duplicate with /dub ID or delete. ## Formatting and buttons Markdown-style formatting and Telegram entities are preserved. Inline buttons use: &lt;inline&gt;Button text&lt;link="https://example.com"&gt; Put each button on its own line. -- keeps two buttons on one row; // starts a new row; add style="success" , style="primary" or style="danger" for colours. Full reference: Formatting & Inline Buttons. ## What is not supported Premium/custom emoji are stripped (text stays), Telegram date formatting and Articles are not rendered, checklists are not supported, and polls must be anonymous. The full list is in Supported Content Types.

Q: Why does the bot say "Date is in the past"?
A: The parsed moment is already behind the channel time zone. Check the zone on the channel card and send a future time; a bare HH:MM that already passed rolls to tomorrow only when no date is given.

Q: Can I schedule without media?
A: Yes. Choose ⏭ Skip Photos at the media step, or send the text-only post and confirm. No files are attached.

Q: Where did my post go after confirming?
A: It is queued, not sent. Open 📋 Message List → Scheduled messages, or 📅 Calendar, to see it. It publishes automatically at the chosen time.

## Your Account
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/start_account.html

There is no sign-up form. The first time you message the bot, an account is created for your Telegram user ID. ## What identifies you Your numeric Telegram user ID is the account key. It is shown in the Premium screen and support uses it to find your data. Never share tokens or codes; the user ID alone is not a secret but it is what support asks for. ## What is stored • your connected channel IDs and their time zones; • scheduled and recurring posts you created; • sender bot tokens (encrypted at rest); • your settings: language, time zone, preferences; • feedback tickets you send. Media is stored by Telegram file reference where possible; the bot does not keep a private copy of every channel post. ## Plans The plan controls limits: channels, sender bots, queued messages, recurring rules, media size and storage. Current values are always in Free Plan Limits and Premium Plan Limits; the in-bot checkout is the authoritative price. ## Language and time zone Change language in ⚙️ Settings → 🌐 Language or /language . Change the zone in ⚙️ Settings → 🕐 Time Zone or /timezone . Language syncs with the support bot and SetDate; the time zone can differ per channel. ## Your data 🗂 Data offers 📤 Export and 📥 Import . Full backups live under /backup . To delete data or your account, contact support: Delete Account. ## Multiple devices The account follows your Telegram account, not the device. Open the bot on a phone or desktop and the same channels, queues and settings are there.

Q: Where do I find my user ID?
A: Open /premium; the screen shows your account ID. Support may also ask for it when investigating a ticket.

Q: Can I move my account to another Telegram account?
A: No automatic migration exists. Export your data, then import it into the other account (subject to plan limits), or contact support before deleting anything.

## Send Your First Post
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/start_schedule.html

This is the shortest complete path from an empty queue to a post that publishes itself. It assumes the channel is connected and has a sender bot — if not, start with Getting Started. ## 1. Open the right chat Open your sender bot (the bot you created in @BotFather), not the main bot. If you are in the main bot, 📢 Channels → the managed channel → 🤖 Open Sender Bot takes you there. ## 2. Start the scheduler Tap 📅 Schedule a Message . A prompt appears with the format and an example. ## 3. Send the date and the post together 25.12.2026 10:00 Our first scheduled post — hello! The first line must be the date/time. Everything below it is the post. If you only send a time ( 18:30 ), the bot schedules it for today, or tomorrow if that moment has passed. ## 4. Choose media If you do not need files, tap ⏭ Skip Photos . Otherwise: • 📷 Normal — the same file on every post (logo, watermark). • 🎲 Random — one random file from the set you send. • 🔀 Sequential — files in order, one per post. • 💾From storage — reuse files already saved in Media Storage. Send the files, watch the counter, then tap ✅ Done (N) . Details: Media Modes Explained. ## 5. Review The card shows the channel, the exact time, a preview, media and inline-button counts. Check the time and time zone first — they are the usual surprises. Then: • ✅ Schedule — queue it. • ✏️ Edit — change the text. • 💾 Change media — replace files. • 📢 Change channel — choose another destination. ## 6. Confirm and verify The bot confirms and assigns an ID. Check 📋 Message List → Scheduled messages or 📅 Calendar . Both show the post before it goes out. ## 7. After it is sent It disappears from the scheduled list and appears in statistics for the channel. If it failed, the calendar marks it ❌ Failed and the bot reports the reason — see Common Errors. ## First-post mistakes to avoid • Sending the text before the date line — the bot needs the first line to be the date. • Using a past date — refused on purpose. • Forgetting the sender bot — scheduling stays locked. • Putting a blank line inside one post — that starts a new message block. • Scheduling on the Free plan with 100 messages already queued — see Scheduled Limit.

Q: Can I write the post first and set the date later?
A: No. In the scheduling flow the first line is parsed as the date/time. Send the date first, then the text. To change the time of an existing post, use Edit from the Message List.

Q: How do I send the same post to two channels?
A: On the review card tap 📢 Choose channels and tick every destination. Each copy is sent by that channel’s own sender bot. Multi-channel targeting is a Premium capability.

## Quick Tips
URL: https://fastscheduler.github.io/help/a/start_tips.html

• Batch your week, not your day. Write five to ten posts in one sitting and queue them; daily manual posting is what scheduling is meant to replace. • Use a bare time for today. Sending 18:30 as the first line schedules today at 18:30, or tomorrow if it already passed. • Separate posts with a blank line. One dated block per post; that is also how a .txt upload works. • Preview before you confirm. The review card is the last place where a typo costs nothing. • Learn the message ID. Every queued post has an ID; /dub ID duplicates it, /edit changes it, and the delete menu accepts IDs directly. • Set the channel's zone, not just yours. The channel card controls what "19:00" means for that audience. • Reuse media from storage. A logo or banner saved once can be attached in Normal mode to every post. • Keep a recent backup. /backup before big reorganisations; tokens are encrypted automatically. • Use the support bot for help. @FastSchedulerSupport_bot has the same articles plus a human reply. • Don't fight the locked channel. If a channel is marked managed, its controls live in its sender bot — open it instead of looking for a duplicate button. Related: Bulk Tips, Queue Tips, Time Zone Tips.

Q: What is the fastest way to fill a week?
A: Open the scheduler once and send several dated blocks separated by blank lines, or use the SetDate companion bot to generate a whole schedule and import it in one click.
